title: Dirichlet p-adic L-functions, special values, and Eisenstein measures, Part II: Ray-class and automorphic interpolation
summary: Ray-class and automorphic interpolation over number fields, as the Part II of DirichletPadicLFunctions fixed by the accepted RS-14. L0 builds the p-power ray-class limit Cl⁺_F(𝔫p^∞) from Tau Ceti’s finite ray class groups, with the closure of the global units, the dimension r₂ + 1 + δ_{F,p} (Leopoldt defect), reciprocity, algebraic and p-adic avatars of Hecke characters, Gauss sums and depleted L-functions, locally analytic distributions with descent, evaluation, twist, norm and Euler-factor operations, and the conditional evaluation-and-interpolation principle (existence from norm relations; uniqueness only under a growth theorem). L1 constructs Barrera Salazar–Williams’ automorphic cycles and evaluation maps for GL₂ over any number field and proves their critical-value formula (Theorem 5.7), compared with rational modular symbols. L2 builds overconvergent modular symbols over F, the corrected compactness and slope-vanishing lemmas, the small-slope control theorem (Theorem 8.7), the distribution µ_Φ with its norm relation and choice-independence, the interpolation Theorem 11.1 with every factor named, growth and uniqueness for F totally real (Bergdall–Hansen, under Leopoldt) or imaginary quadratic (Williams), and the ℚ/Hilbert/Bianchi specialisations. L3 proves Deligne–Ribet (partial zeta distributions, Hilbert Eisenstein series and their constant terms after Dasgupta–Kakde, the irreducibility of the Igusa tower, the p-adic q-expansion principle, the measures and pseudo-measure, group-ring Eisenstein families) and Katz’s ordinary CM construction (p-ordinary CM types, CM points, periods, differential operators and algebraicity, the Eisenstein measure, Theorem (5.3.0), the functional equation, the Hida–Tilouine tame version). L3h plans Hsieh’s anticyclotomic square-root distribution with Theorems A–C and the BDP/Castella–Hsieh specialisation, with a proposed sub-layer L3m for the mod-p nonvanishing inputs (Hida’s linear independence and density, Hida’s and Hsieh’s µ = 0, Hsieh 2012, Finis). L4 plans the EHLS doubling construction (setting, ordinary Hecke algebras and congruence ideals, the three hypotheses, differential operators, Eisenstein measure, global and local zeta integrals, Main Theorem 9.2.2) and Disegni–Liu’s cyclotomic construction (Siegel hermitian varieties, big-cell sections, Panchishkin unramified representations, the p-adic doubling integral, Theorem 3.37, the parity of the vanishing order). L4e plans the Eischen–Wan finite-slope Klingen families with their p-adic L-function and the r = 2 constant-term divisibility. L5 compares normalisations across the constructions, places every construction in the one evaluation formalism, and states the Coates–Perrin-Riou/Panchishkin existence proposition without asserting it.

conventions.frobenius: Artin reciprocity is arithmetically normalised (Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory layer 11); Hsieh’s geometric rec_K and Skinner’s geometric convention are converted by inversion at each use.
conventions.rayClass: Cl⁺_F(𝔫p^∞) is the limit of the narrow ray class groups of modulus 𝔫p^m with all real places; the class of the ideal (a) corresponds to a in the ideal description and to a^{-1} under the idelic map u ↦ [u at p].
conventions.units: Global units enter through the topological closure of their image in (O_F ⊗ ℤ_p)^×; no Leopoldt hypothesis is built into a definition (sourceIssues E4).
conventions.charts: Fibre functions use the forward chart φ_{a_y}(z) = φ(a_yz) (sourceIssues E1).
conventions.embeddings: ι_∞ : ℚ̄ → ℂ and ι_p : ℚ̄ → ℂ_p are fixed; every interpolation formula names the embedding through which algebraic values are compared, and Disegni–Liu’s formula holds for all ι.
conventions.uniformisers: BSW’s U_𝔭 are normalised by fixed uniformisers π_𝔭 ∈ L; µ_Φ depends on them.
conventions.slopes: Slope decompositions use the endpoint convention of LocallyAnalyticDistributions §4.16 (roots of valuation ≤ h, equality included).
conventions.uniqueness: Choice-independence of a construction is not uniqueness by interpolation; the latter needs a growth theorem in every chart direction.

nodes.title: Continuous unit invariance extends to the closure
nodes.statement: Let G be a topological group, E ⊆ G a subgroup with topological closure Ē, Y a Hausdorff space and φ : G → Y continuous. If φ(ez) = φ(z) for every e ∈ E and z ∈ G, then φ(ez) = φ(z) for every e ∈ Ē and z ∈ G. In particular a continuous function on (O_F ⊗ ℤ_p)^× invariant under the totally positive global units congruent to 1 modulo f is invariant under their closure, and so factors through the quotient by that closure.
hypotheses: G is a topological group (continuous multiplication suffices); Y is Hausdorff.
No compactness, rank computation or Leopoldt hypothesis is used.
proofSteps: Fix z ∈ G. The two maps e ↦ φ(ez) and e ↦ φ(z) are continuous on G and agree on E.
Equality of continuous maps into a Hausdorff space on a set extends to its closure (Set.EqOn.closure); quantify over z.
acceptance: Applied to G = (ℤ_p)^× ⊃ E = {±1}·(1+pℤ)^ℤ-type examples, it is exactly the statement that the locally constant functions on the ray-class limit are the unit-invariant ones; it says nothing about locally analytic descent, which ray-class-distributions proves.

sources.match: BSW regard a function on the ray-class group as a family of functions on (O_F ⊗ ℤ_p)^× invariant under the global units E(f); continuity makes this invariance pass to the closure that the ray-class quotient actually divides by.
Katz identifies Gal(L(p^∞)/L(1)) with (O_L ⊗ ℤ_p)^× modulo the closure of the global units, which is the quotient this lemma serves.

nodes.title: The ray-class tower of p-power conductor and fixed tame modulus
nodes.statement: Let F be a number field, p a rational prime and 𝔫 an integral ideal of O_F prime to p. For m ≥ 0 let 𝔪_m be the Tau Ceti modulus with finite part 𝔫·p^m O_F and infinite part all real places, and Cl⁺_F(𝔫p^m) := RayClassGroup(𝔪_m), the narrow ray class group. The transition maps classMap(𝔪_m ∣ 𝔪_{m'}) for m ≤ m′ form an inverse system of finite groups with surjective transition maps, and Cl⁺_F(𝔫p^∞) := lim_m Cl⁺_F(𝔫p^m) is a profinite abelian group (the limit in ProfiniteGrp of the finite discrete groups). For a modulus f dividing 𝔫p^∞ the projection Cl⁺_F(𝔫p^∞) → Cl⁺_F(f) is continuous and surjective, and for 𝔫 ∣ 𝔫′ (both prime to p) the tame change map Cl⁺_F(𝔫′p^∞) → Cl⁺_F(𝔫p^∞) is the limit of the classMap’s.
hypotheses: F a number field, p a prime, 𝔫 ≠ 0 an integral ideal prime to p.
The narrow (all real places) modulus is used, as in BSW and Katz; the wide version is the quotient by the image of the signs and is recovered by taking the infinite part empty.
proofSteps: Instantiate RayClassGroup at 𝔪_m; finiteness is finite_rayClassGroup, transitions are classMap with classMap_comp_classMap, surjectivity is classMap_surjective.
Form the limit with ProfiniteGrp.limit over the directed set ℕ; each finite group carries the discrete topology.
Surjectivity of the projections follows from surjective transitions in a countable inverse system of finite sets (compactness of the limit).
Tame change: classMap(𝔪_m(𝔫) ∣ 𝔪_m(𝔫′)) commutes with the transitions, so it passes to the limit.
acceptance: For F = ℚ, 𝔫 = (1): Cl⁺_ℚ(p^∞) ≅ ℤ_p^×; the class of the ideal (a), a > 0 prime to p, corresponds to a under the ideal-theoretic description of each level and to a^{-1} under the idelic map u ↦ [u at p], a convention every comparison must track.
For F imaginary quadratic of class number 1 with p split: Cl⁺_F(p^∞) ≅ (O_F ⊗ ℤ_p)^× / O_F^×, of ℤ_p-rank 2.

sources.locator: §1.1 p. 5 (narrow ray class group modulo f) and §1.2.2 p. 6 (Cl⁺_F(p^∞) as F^×\A_F^×/U(p^∞)F_∞⁺)
sources.match: BSW define the narrow ray class groups and the p-power limit group on which their p-adic L-function lives.
Deligne–Ribet take G to be the ray class group of conductor f·p^∞, the Galois group of the maximal abelian extension unramified outside fp and the infinite places.
Panchishkin writes Gal_p as the projective limit over moduli supported at p of the narrow ray class groups J(m)/P(m).

nodes.title: The unit-closure exact sequence of the ray-class limit
nodes.statement: With 𝔫 prime to p, let E_+(𝔫) be the group of totally positive units of O_F congruent to 1 modulo 𝔫, embedded diagonally in U_p := (O_F ⊗ ℤ_p)^×, and let Ē_+(𝔫) be the topological closure of its image. There is an exact sequence of profinite groups 1 → Ē_+(𝔫) → U_p → Cl⁺_F(𝔫p^∞) → Cl⁺_F(𝔫) → 1, where the middle map sends a p-adic unit to the class of the idele that is it at p and 1 elsewhere. The closure is essential: with the bare image E_+(𝔫) the kernel would not be closed when the unit rank is positive. Choosing representatives a_y for Cl⁺_F(𝔫f) (f ∣ p^∞, f divisible by every prime above p) gives the homeomorphism Cl⁺_F(𝔫p^∞) ≅ ⊔_{y∈Cl⁺_F(𝔫f)} G_y, G_y the fibre over y, with each G_y ≅ {z ∈ U_p : z ≡ 1 mod f}/Ē_+(𝔫f) by multiplication by a_y^{-1}; for 𝔫 = (1) this is BSW’s decomposition over Cl⁺_F(f).
hypotheses: 𝔫 prime to p; totally positive units; the closure is taken in the p-adic topology of U_p.
proofSteps: At each finite level the Tau Ceti exact sequence O_F^× → (O_F/𝔫p^m)^× × signs → Cl_F(𝔫p^m) → Cl_F → 1 (mulExact_unitsResidueSignHom_residueSignRayClass, mulExact_residueSignRayClass_rayClassToClassGroup) restricts on totally positive units to E_+(𝔫) → (O_F/𝔫p^m)^× → Cl⁺_F(𝔫p^m) → Cl⁺_F(𝔫) → 1 after quotienting the tame part.

Pass to the inverse limit over m: the terms are finite, so the limit of the exact sequences is exact; the limit of the images of E_+(𝔫) is the closure of its image in U_p (an inverse limit of finite images is closed and contains E_+ densely).

The decomposition into fibres G_y follows by fixing the image in Cl⁺_F(𝔫f) and translating by a_y^{-1}; the kernel of {z ≡ 1 mod f} → Cl⁺_F(𝔫p^∞) is Ē_+(𝔫) ∩ (1 + f) = Ē_+(𝔫f), the closure meeting the open subgroup 1 + f in the closure of E_+(𝔫f).
acceptance: F = ℚ: Ē_+ is trivial (the only totally positive unit is 1) and the sequence reads 1 → ℤ_p^× → Cl⁺(p^∞) → 1.
F real quadratic: Ē_+ has ℤ_p-rank 1, because F is abelian and so satisfies Leopoldt at every p (IntegralIwasawaTheory:L4/abelian-leopoldt); the quotient U_p/Ē_+ then has ℤ_p-rank 1.

sources.match: BSW pass to the limit of the exact sequences O_{F,+}^× → (O_F/f)^× → Cl⁺_F(f) → Cl⁺_F → 0 and decompose Cl⁺_F(p^∞) into the fibres G_y over Cl⁺_F(f) (equation (11)); see sourceIssues E4 for the closure.
Katz identifies the kernel to the Hilbert class field with (O_L ⊗ ℤ_p)^× modulo the closure of E(L).

nodes.title: Dimension of the ray-class limit and the Leopoldt defect
nodes.statement: Cl⁺_F(𝔫p^∞) is a compact commutative p-adic analytic group: it has an open subgroup topologically isomorphic to ℤ_p^d, and its torsion subgroup Δ is finite. Its dimension is d = r₂ + 1 + δ_{F,p}, where r₂ is the number of complex places and δ_{F,p} is the Leopoldt defect of F at p (the dimension of the kernel of the p-adic logarithm on O_F^× ⊗ ℚ_p, IntegralIwasawaTheory:L4/leopoldt-defect). Equivalently, the ℤ_p-rank of Ē_+(𝔫) equals r₁ + r₂ − 1 − δ_{F,p}. A chart Cl⁺_F(𝔫p^∞) ≅ Δ × ℤ_p^d (after choosing a splitting of the finite part) makes it an analytic group in the sense of LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L0/analytic-manifold-atlases, and every continuous character factors through the chart.
hypotheses: No Leopoldt hypothesis is assumed; δ_{F,p} ≥ 0 is part of the formula.
The splitting Δ × ℤ_p^d is a choice; statements that depend on it say so.
proofSteps: U_p = (O_F ⊗ ℤ_p)^× has an open subgroup isomorphic to ℤ_p^{[F:ℚ]} through the p-adic logarithm on a small principal-unit subgroup; [F:ℚ] = r₁ + 2r₂.

By Dirichlet's unit theorem (NumberField.Units.rank, finrank_modTorsion) E_+(𝔫) has ℤ-rank r₁ + r₂ − 1, and the ℤ_p-rank of its closure is r₁ + r₂ − 1 − δ_{F,p} by the definition of the defect (the logarithm of the closure spans the image of O_F^× ⊗ ℚ_p).
From ray-class-unit-sequence the dimension is [F:ℚ] − rank Ē_+ = r₂ + 1 + δ_{F,p}; the finite quotient Cl⁺_F(𝔫) and the torsion of U_p/Ē_+ give the finite part Δ.
A compact commutative p-adic analytic group splits non-canonically as Δ × ℤ_p^d.
acceptance: F = ℚ: d = 1 (Δ = (ℤ/p)^× for p odd).
F imaginary quadratic: d = 2 (r₂ = 1, no units of infinite order).
F totally real satisfying Leopoldt at p: d = 1; abelian F satisfies Leopoldt (IntegralIwasawaTheory:L4/abelian-leopoldt).

BSW's example F = ℚ(∛2): the units have rank 1, U_p has rank 3, and d = 2 (the defect vanishes here: the unit rank is 1 and the p-adic logarithm of a unit of infinite order is nonzero), so ray-class distributions grow in two directions while the critical Hecke characters are only parallel.

sources.match: BSW explain that the quotient by the units has ℤ_p-rank [F:ℚ] minus the unit rank when the units embed with full rank, and treat F = ℚ(∛2) as an example of rank 2.

nodes.title: Reciprocity for the ray-class limit
nodes.statement: Global Artin reciprocity, with Tau Ceti’s arithmetic Frobenius normalisation, gives a topological isomorphism Art : Cl⁺_F(𝔫p^∞) ≅ Gal(F(𝔫p^∞)/F), where F(𝔫p^∞) is the maximal abelian extension of F unramified outside the primes dividing 𝔫p and the infinite places; the class of a prime 𝔮 ∤ 𝔫p maps to its arithmetic Frobenius. It is compatible with the finite-level maps Cl⁺_F(𝔫p^m) ≅ Gal(F(𝔫p^m)/F), with the tame change maps (restriction of Galois groups) and, for F ⊂ F′, with the norm/transfer maps. Hsieh’s geometrically normalised reciprocity rec_K is the composite of Art with inversion; every statement exported from this layer names its normalisation.
hypotheses: Arithmetic Frobenius convention of tauceti:ClassFieldTheory layer 11.
Conversions to geometric conventions (Hsieh 2014; Skinner) are by inversion and are recorded at each use.
proofSteps: At each finite level apply global Artin reciprocity for the ray class field of conductor 𝔪_m (ClassFieldTheory layer 11).
Compatibility of the finite-level isomorphisms with classMap and with restriction of Galois groups is functoriality of the Artin map in the modulus.
Pass to the inverse limit; both sides are profinite and the maps are continuous isomorphisms of compact Hausdorff groups.
acceptance: For F = ℚ, 𝔫 = (1): Art identifies ℤ_p^× with Gal(ℚ(μ_{p^∞})/ℚ), the class of a prime ℓ ≠ p mapping to Frob_ℓ, which acts on μ_{p^∞} by ζ ↦ ζ^ℓ.
With Hsieh’s geometric normalisation the same prime class maps to Frob_ℓ^{-1}.

nodes.title: Algebraic and p-adic avatars of Hecke characters
nodes.statement: Fix embeddings ι_∞ : ℚ̄ → ℂ and ι_p : ℚ̄ → ℂ_p. Let ϕ be an algebraic (arithmetic) Hecke character of F of conductor dividing 𝔫p^∞ and infinity type r ∈ ℤ[Σ] (Σ the complex embeddings), so that ϕ_∞(z) = ε_ϕ(z)·z^r with ε_ϕ the sign character of {±1}^{Σ(ℝ)} defined by ε_ϕ(ι) = ϕ_∞(ι)ι^r. Let w_r : F^× → ℚ̄^× be w_r(γ) = ∏_σ σ(γ)^{r_σ}, with its p-adic extension w_r^p on (F ⊗ ℚ_p)^×. The p-adic avatar is ϕ_{p-fin}(x) = ε_ϕ(x)ϕ_f(x)w_r^p(x_p) on A_F^×; it is trivial on F^×, on F_∞⁺ and on U(𝔫p^∞), hence a continuous character Cl⁺_F(𝔫p^∞) → ℂ_p^× that is locally algebraic of weight r. The algebraic avatar is the ℚ̄-valued character a ↦ ι_∞^{-1}(ϕ(a)) on ideals prime to 𝔫p. Through ray-class-reciprocity, ϕ_{p-fin} is a Galois character; its local factors are ϕ(𝔮) := ϕ(π_𝔮) at 𝔮 ∤ 𝔫p (0 at ramified primes), giving the Euler factors (1 − ϕ(𝔮)N𝔮^{-s})^{-1}.
hypotheses: ϕ is arithmetic: its infinity type r is an admissible type (Weil); its finite part takes values in a number field.
Embeddings ι_∞, ι_p are fixed once and for all and recorded in every interpolation formula.
proofSteps: Use the complex Hecke characters, their local components, conductors and infinity types of GlobalNumberFields layers 9–10.
Algebraicity of the finite part (Weil) lets ϕ_f be read in ℚ̄ and then in ℂ_p via ι_p.

Check the three trivialities (on F^×: ϕ_{p-fin}(γ) = ϕ(γ)/w_r^∞(γ)·w_r^p(γ) = 1 since ϕ is trivial on F^× and both w’s come from w_r; on F_∞⁺ by construction; on U(𝔫p^∞) since x_p = x_∞ = 1 and ϕ has conductor dividing 𝔫p^∞).
Continuity: ϕ_f is locally constant and w_r^p is continuous.
acceptance: The avatar of a finite-order character is the same character read through ι_p.

For F = ℚ and ϕ = |·|^{-1} (infinity type −1), the avatar sends the class of a prime ℓ ≠ p to ℓ and a unit u at p to u^{-1}: it is the p-adic cyclotomic character composed with the arithmetic Artin map.

nodes.title: Locally algebraic characters of the ray-class limit are avatars
nodes.statement: The map ϕ ↦ ϕ_{p-fin} is a bijection from algebraic Hecke characters of F of conductor dividing 𝔫p^∞ (with values read through ι_∞) onto continuous characters χ : Cl⁺_F(𝔫p^∞) → ℂ_p^× that are locally algebraic, i.e. agree with z ↦ z^r for some r ∈ ℤ[Σ] on an open subgroup of the image of U_p. The weight r must lie in Weil’s set Ξ of admissible infinity types: r + c·r parallel (c complex conjugation) is necessary but not sufficient in general, and when F has a real place only parallel r occur; conversely every r ∈ Ξ occurs (Weil; BSW Proposition 1.2).
hypotheses: Embeddings fixed as in hecke-character-avatar.
proofSteps: Injectivity: ϕ is recovered from ϕ_{p-fin} by restoring ε_ϕ and w_r^∞ (the formula in hecke-character-avatar is invertible).

Surjectivity: given χ locally algebraic of weight r, the idele character x ↦ χ(x)·w_r^p(x_p)^{-1}·w_r^∞(x_∞) is continuous and trivial on F^× (both w’s restrict to w_r on F^×), with algebraic values by the standard argument (it is locally constant on the finite ideles, and the finitely many class representatives have powers in F^×·U). Since χ is trivial on the image of the units while equal to z^r near 1, w_r is trivial on a finite-index subgroup of O_F^×, which is Weil’s admissibility condition on r.
Admissibility of r is Weil’s criterion, quoted by BSW as Proposition 1.2 with the description of the admissible set Ξ from Hida’s book.
acceptance: F totally real: only parallel weights occur, so every locally algebraic character is a finite-order character times a power of the cyclotomic character.
F imaginary quadratic: every (r₁, r₂) ∈ ℤ² is admissible.

nodes.title: Gauss sums and p-depleted Hecke L-functions
nodes.statement: For a Hecke character ϕ of conductor f and a finite idele d representing the different, τ(ϕ) := ϕ(d^{-1}) Σ_{b ∈ (O_F/f)^×} ϕ_f(b) e_F(b d^{-1}(π_f^{-1})_{v|f}), where e_F : A_F/F → ℂ^× is the standard additive character (e^{2πi Tr} at infinity, e_ℓ(−Tr) at finite places) and (π_f^{-1})_{v|f} has components π_w^{-v_w(f)} at w | f and 0 elsewhere; it is independent of d and equals the product of Deligne’s local ε-factors at the places dividing f. For a set S of finite places, the S-depleted L-function is L^{(S)}(ϕ, s) := L(ϕ, s)·∏_{𝔮∈S}(1 − ϕ(𝔮)N𝔮^{-s}), and L*(ϕ, s) := L^{(S_p)}(ϕ, s) with S_p the primes above p.
hypotheses: L(ϕ, s) is the complex Hecke L-function with its meromorphic continuation (AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.1/hecke-l-functional-equation).
ϕ(𝔮) = 0 at primes dividing the conductor, so depletion at such 𝔮 changes nothing.
proofSteps: τ(ϕ) is a finite sum; independence of d is the standard change of variables b ↦ bu with u a unit at f.
Its factorisation into local ε-factors is AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.1/local-gauss-sum with AL.1/explicit-epsilon-factors.
The depleted L-function is a product of the continued L(ϕ, s) with finitely many entire factors.
acceptance: The Gauss sum of the trivial character of conductor (1) is 1.

For F = ℚ and a primitive Dirichlet character χ mod f, τ(χ) agrees with Mathlib’s gaussSum of χ with the additive character a ↦ e^{2πia/f} up to the sign convention of e_ℓ(−Tr), which BSW fix explicitly.

sources.match: BSW define e_F, the Gauss sum τ(ϕ) with the explicit adelic representative, note its independence of d and its relation with Deligne’s ε-factors, and give the twisted-sum identity of Proposition 1.7.

nodes.title: Nonvanishing of L(χ, 0) for totally odd characters
nodes.statement: Let F be totally real and χ a totally odd finite-order Hecke character (ray class character) of F. Then L(χ, 0) ≠ 0, and L*(χ, 0) = L(χ, 0)∏_{𝔭|p}(1 − χ(𝔭)) vanishes exactly when χ(𝔭) = 1 for some 𝔭 | p.
hypotheses: F totally real; χ of finite order with χ_v(−1) = −1 at every real place v.
proofSteps: The functional equation (AL.1/hecke-l-functional-equation) relates L(χ, 0) to L(χ̄, 1) times Γ-factors; for χ totally odd the archimedean factors are Γ_ℝ(s+1) at each real place, which have no pole or zero at s = 0, and the ε-factor is nonzero.
L(χ̄, 1) ≠ 0 for a nontrivial finite-order Hecke character (nonvanishing on Re s = 1, AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4/hecke-nonvanishing-on-line-one).
The statement about L* is the definition of depletion.
acceptance: F = ℚ, χ odd Dirichlet: L(χ, 0) = −B_{1,χ} ≠ 0.
DKV’s trivial zeros: L*(χ, 0) = 0 iff some prime above p splits completely in the field cut out by χ, so r_p(χ) counts those primes.

nodes.title: Locally analytic distributions on the ray-class limit and their descent
nodes.statement: Let L ⊂ ℂ_p be a complete extension of ℚ_p. D(Cl⁺_F(𝔫p^∞), L) is the strong dual of the space A(Cl⁺_F(𝔫p^∞), L) of locally analytic L-valued functions, for the analytic structure of leopoldt-dimension-formula: the distributions on a compact analytic manifold of LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L0/locally-analytic-dual-nuclear, a nuclear Fréchet space. Measures (bounded distributions) form the subalgebra identified with the completed group algebra (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L1). For f ∣ p^∞ divisible by every prime above p and representatives a_y of Cl⁺_F(𝔫f), a function φ on Cl⁺_F(𝔫p^∞) is the same as the family φ_{a_y}(z) := φ(a_y z) of functions on {z ∈ U_p : z ≡ 1 mod f} invariant under Ē_+(𝔫f) (forward chart; see sourceIssues E1); a distribution is determined by its values on the clopen pieces G_y. The Mellin transform identifies D(Cl⁺_F(𝔫p^∞), L) with the ring of rigid analytic functions on the character space (LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L3/mellin-frechet-isomorphism), measures corresponding to the bounded functions.
hypotheses: L contains the values needed (the images of the embeddings of F and the character values); the analytic structure comes from the chart Δ × ℤ_p^d, and the space does not depend on the chart.
proofSteps: Transport the definitions of LocallyAnalyticDistributions L0 along the analytic chart of leopoldt-dimension-formula.

Descent: precomposition with the open map U_p → G_y ⊂ Cl⁺_F(𝔫p^∞) identifies locally analytic functions on G_y with Ē_+-invariant locally analytic functions on the congruence subgroup; by unit-invariance-closure, invariance under E_+(𝔫f) suffices.
Clopen decomposition of distributions along Cl⁺_F(𝔫p^∞) = ⊔ G_y (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L0/clopen-decomposition-equivalence for measures, the same argument for distributions).
Mellin transform: LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L3/mellin-frechet-isomorphism on the chart.
acceptance: For F = ℚ, 𝔫 = (1), D(Cl⁺_ℚ(p^∞), L) = D(ℤ_p^×, L), the space on which DirichletPadicLFunctions’ Kubota–Leopoldt distributions live.

nodes.title: Evaluation, norm, twist and tame-change maps on ray-class distributions
nodes.statement: For µ ∈ D(Cl⁺_F(𝔫p^∞), L): (i) evaluation at a locally algebraic character, ev_ϕ(µ) := µ(ϕ_{p-fin}), and at a finite-level function (a locally constant function factoring through Cl⁺_F(𝔫p^m)); (ii) for 𝔫 ∣ 𝔫′ the pushforward (norm) along tameChange, with ev_ϕ(tameChange_*µ) = ev_{ϕ∘tameChange}(µ); (iii) twisting by a continuous character ψ, Tw_ψ(µ)(φ) := µ(ψφ), with ev_ϕ(Tw_ψ µ) = ev_{ϕψ}(µ) and Tw_ψ Tw_ψ′ = Tw_{ψψ′}; (iv) pushforward along a continuous surjection of ray-class limits q : Cl⁺_F(𝔫′p^∞) → Γ onto a quotient (for instance an anticyclotomic quotient), with ev_φ(q_* Tw_{ψ^{-1}} µ) = ev_{ψ^{-1}(φ∘q)}(µ). Characters that do not factor through q are evaluated only through (iii).
hypotheses: All maps are continuous L-linear; for distributions the twisting character ψ must be locally analytic (LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L3/mellin-twist); for measures a continuous ψ suffices.
proofSteps: Pushforward and multiplication by a locally analytic function are continuous operations (LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L3/mellin-pushforward, L3/mellin-twist give the Mellin formulas).
The evaluation formulas are the definitions of pushforward and twist applied to characters.
acceptance: For F = ℚ these are the twist and pushforward operations on D(ℤ_p^×, L) used for the Kubota–Leopoldt branches.
GZ.9’s convention: with q : Γ̃ → Γ and auxiliary ψ, ev_φ(q_* Tw_{ψ^{-1}} µ) = ev_{ψ^{-1}(φ∘q)}(µ).

nodes.title: The conditional evaluation-and-interpolation principle
nodes.statement: Let 𝒞 be the set of moduli f ∣ p^∞ divisible by every prime above p, and suppose given: (a) for each f ∈ 𝒞 a distribution µ^f ∈ D(Cl⁺_F(𝔫p^∞), L); (b) units α_𝔭 ∈ L^× (𝔭 | p) with the norm relation µ^{f𝔭} = α_𝔭 µ^f for all f ∈ 𝒞 and 𝔭 | p; (c) a set 𝒳 of algebraic Hecke characters of conductor dividing 𝔫p^∞ and, for ϕ ∈ 𝒳 of conductor f_ϕ, with f′_ϕ := f_ϕ ∏_{𝔭∈B(ϕ)} 𝔭 (B(ϕ) the primes above p not dividing f_ϕ), an evaluation formula µ^{f′_ϕ}(ϕ_{p-fin}) = c(ϕ)·L^{alg}(ϕ) with explicit c(ϕ). Then µ := α_f^{-1}µ^f, with α_f := ∏_{𝔭^r∥f} α_𝔭^r, is independent of f ∈ 𝒞 and satisfies µ(ϕ_{p-fin}) = α_{f′_ϕ}^{-1}c(ϕ)L^{alg}(ϕ) for every ϕ ∈ 𝒳. Uniqueness holds only under a growth theorem: if µ has order h (LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L2 order-r distributions, in the vector-order sense along the chart) and the avatars {ϕ_{p-fin} : ϕ ∈ 𝒳}, multiplied by finite-order characters, span the locally polynomial test functions of the degrees that bound determines, then any µ′ of the same order with the same interpolation values equals µ. Without such a growth theorem the principle gives existence and choice-independence only.
hypotheses: All data in (a)–(c) are actual objects with proved relations; nothing is postulated by a structure field.
The uniqueness clause needs the growth bound and the spanning condition; it fails at the critical order (LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L2/critical-vector-counterexample).
proofSteps: Independence of f: for f ∈ 𝒞 and 𝔭 | p, α_{f𝔭}^{-1}µ^{f𝔭} = α_f^{-1}α_𝔭^{-1}α_𝔭µ^f; any two f, f′ ∈ 𝒞 are joined through f·f′ by finitely many such steps (induction on the total exponent, staying inside 𝒞).
Interpolation: take f = f′_ϕ in the definition of µ.

Uniqueness: apply the multidegree extension/uniqueness theorem (LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L2/tensor-multidegree-extension, L2/amice-velu-vishik in dimension one) on each chart component, after the ray-class growth adapter (L2/rayclass-growth-adapter) converts conductor bounds into rectangular growth.
acceptance: BSW: µ^f from overconvergent evaluations, α_𝔭 the U_𝔭-eigenvalues, c(ϕ) from Theorem 5.7 and Corollary 10.2; uniqueness only for F totally real (Leopoldt) or imaginary quadratic.
Rational case: Pollack–Stevens’ µ is h-admissible with h = v_p(α) and is unique when h < k + 1 (ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions:L2/interpolation-and-uniqueness).

sources.match: BSW normalise by λ_f^{-1}, prove independence of f from the one-prime relation, deduce interpolation at characters unramified at some 𝔭 | p, and explain that uniqueness needs an admissibility theorem available only for F totally real or imaginary quadratic.
Panchishkin recalls that an h-admissible measure extends uniquely to locally analytic functions and is determined by its values on characters times x_p^r with r < h (Amice–Vélu, Višik).

nodes.title: Admissible weights and the weight-λ coefficient modules for GL₂/F
nodes.statement: Let F be a number field with complex embeddings Σ (d = [F:ℚ] = r₁ + 2r₂), c complex conjugation on Σ. A weight λ = (k, v) ∈ ℤ[Σ] × ℤ[Σ] is admissible if k = c·k ≥ 0 and k + 2v is parallel. For a ring A, V_k(A) = ⊗_σ V_{k_σ}(A) with V_n(A) the homogeneous polynomials of degree n in two variables and GL₂ acting by (a b; c d)·f(X, Y) = f(bY + dX, aY + cX); V_λ(A) is V_k(A) with the action twisted by ∏_σ det(γ_σ)^{v_σ}. Its dual V_λ(A)* = Hom(V_λ(A), A) carries the right action (P|γ)(f) = P(γ·f). The level is Ω₁(𝔫) = {(a b; c d) ∈ GL₂(Ô_F) : c ≡ 0, d ≡ 1 mod 𝔫} with p ∣ 𝔫, Y₁(𝔫) = GL₂(F)\GL₂(A_F)/Ω₁(𝔫)K_∞⁺Z_∞ (K_∞⁺ = SO₂(ℝ)^{r₁} × SU₂(ℂ)^{r₂}), of real dimension whose middle compactly supported degree is q = r₁ + r₂. For a right GL₂(F)-module M on which the units of Ω₁(𝔫) ∩ Z act trivially, L₁(M) is the local system with action γ(g, m)ukz = (γgukz, m|γ^{-1}); for a right Ω₁(𝔫)-module, L₂(M) uses (g, m) ↦ (γgukz, m|u). For M a GL₂(F ⊗ ℚ_p)-module the two are isomorphic by (g, m) ↦ (g, m|g_p).
hypotheses: F any number field; λ admissible; 𝔫 ⊂ O_F with p ∣ 𝔫; the centre condition of BSW Definition 3.2 holds for the modules used.
proofSteps: V_λ(A) is a finite free A-module of rank ∏_σ(k_σ + 1) with an algebraic GL₂(A)^Σ-action, i.e. the algebraic weight of AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups:AF.4/algebraic-weight for Res_{F/ℚ}GL₂.

Y₁(𝔫) is ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces’ X_K for G = Res_{F/ℚ}GL₂ and K = Ω₁(𝔫) (with the centre and K_∞⁺ conventions of BSW); its decomposition into h components Γ^i₁(𝔫)\H_F (h the narrow class number) is ALS.0/component-decomposition.

L₁ and L₂ are the arithmetic local systems of ALS.1/arithmetic-local-system for the GL₂(F)-action and the Ω₁(𝔫)-action respectively; the isomorphism is ALS.1’s comparison for modules that extend to GL₂(F ⊗ ℚ_p).
acceptance: F = ℚ: λ = (k, v) with k ≥ 0 any integer, V_λ = Sym^k twisted by det^v, the coefficient module of ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions:L0/polynomial-coefficients, and q = 1.
F imaginary quadratic: Σ = {σ, cσ}, k = (k, k) is forced by k = c·k, matching Williams’ Bianchi weight (k, k).

nodes.title: Cuspidal eigenforms of weight λ over F and their twisted L-functions
nodes.statement: A cusp form of weight λ and level Ω₁(𝔫) is Φ : GL₂(A_F) → V_{k*}(ℂ) satisfying the automorphy condition Φ(zgu) = Φ(g)ρ(u, z) for u ∈ K_∞⁺, z ∈ Z_∞ (ρ the weight-λ representation of BSW §1.3), right Ω₁(𝔫)-invariance, left GL₂(F)-invariance, the Casimir eigencondition at each infinite place, moderate growth and cuspidality; S_λ(Ω₁(𝔫)) is the space. For a Hecke eigenform Φ with T_I-eigenvalues λ_I and a Hecke character ϕ, L(Φ, ϕ, s) = Σ_{0≠I⊂O_F} λ_I ϕ(I) N(I)^{-s}, continued to ℂ, L(Φ, ϕ) := L(Φ, ϕ, 1), and for ϕ of infinity type j + v the completed value Λ(Φ, ϕ) := ∏_{σ∈Σ} Γ(j_σ + 1)/(−2πi)^{j_σ+1} · L(Φ, ϕ). A character ϕ of infinity type j + v is critical for Φ when 0 ≤ j ≤ k.
hypotheses: Φ cuspidal Hecke eigenform; ϕ arithmetic Hecke character.
proofSteps: S_λ(Ω₁(𝔫)) is the space of cohomological cusp forms of AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups:AF.3/cusp-form with the weight condition of AF.4/cohomological-representation for Res_{F/ℚ}GL₂.

L(Φ, ϕ, s) is the standard L-function of the cuspidal representation generated by Φ twisted by ϕ, shifted by BSW’s normalisation; continuation is GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer:R16.5/whittaker-integral-comparison with AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.2/global-godement-jacquet, and for F = ℚ the shift between classical and unitary normalisations is R16.5/classical-l-function-comparison; over general F BSW’s normalisation L(Φ, ϕ) := L(Φ, ϕ, 1) is the analogous shift.
acceptance: F = ℚ, Φ the adelisation of a weight k + 2 newform f: L(Φ, ϕ, s) is the classical L(f, ϕ, s) up to BSW’s shift and Λ includes Deligne’s Γ-factors.

nodes.title: Eichler–Shimura–Harder for GL₂ over F
nodes.statement: There is a Hecke-equivariant injection S_λ(Ω₁(𝔫)) ↪ H^q_c(Y₁(𝔫), L₁(V_λ(ℂ)*)), q = r₁ + r₂, sending an eigenform Φ to a class φ_ℂ with the same Hecke eigenvalues; it is the composite of Harder’s map to cuspidal cohomology with the inclusion of cuspidal into compactly supported cohomology. Under the decomposition Y₁(𝔫) = ⊔_{i=1}^h Γ^i₁(𝔫)\H_F, compactly supported cohomology splits (non-canonically, after a large coefficient extension) as the direct sum over components.
hypotheses: Cohomological weight λ; Hecke operators normalised as in BSW §3.2.1 (Dimitrov).
proofSteps: The automorphic-to-cohomology map for GL₂ over a general number field: the (𝔤, K)-cohomology of the cohomological cuspidal representation in degree q, transported to the cohomology of the locally symmetric space (Borel–Wallach range, AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups:AF.4/borel-wallach-tempered-range) and to the de Rham/Betti comparison (ALS.1/sheaf-singular-comparison).
Hecke equivariance: Hecke correspondences act compatibly on automorphic forms and on cohomology (ALS.3/hecke-operator-formula).
This general-F theorem is requested from ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces (see requests); for F = ℚ it is ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions:L0/eichler-shimura-isomorphism.
acceptance: F = ℚ: the Eichler–Shimura isomorphism for Γ₁(N) in degree 1.
F imaginary quadratic: Harder’s isomorphism in degree q = 1 for Bianchi forms (Williams §2).

sources.match: BSW state the Hecke-equivariant injection from cusp forms into compactly supported cohomology in degree q, referring to Hida’s explicit recipe, and the decomposition over components.
Williams makes the Bianchi case explicit through differentials on H₃ and the associated modular symbol.

nodes.title: Periods and algebraicity of critical values (Hida)
nodes.statement: Let Φ be a cuspidal eigenform of weight λ = (k, v) and level Ω₁(𝔫), K a number field containing the Galois closure of F and the Hecke eigenvalues of Φ. For each character ε of the Weyl group {±1}^{Σ(ℝ)} there is a period Ω^ε_Φ ∈ ℂ^×, depending only on Φ and ε and well defined up to K^×, such that for every Hecke character ϕ of infinity type j + v with 0 ≤ j ≤ k and ε_ϕ = ε, Λ(Φ, ϕ)/(Ω^ε_Φ τ(ϕ)) ∈ K(ϕ), the field generated over K by the values of ϕ. The period depends on ε_ϕ(ι) = ϕ|_{{±1}}(ι)ι^{j+v}, not on the restriction of ϕ alone; there are 2^{r₁} periods.
hypotheses: Hecke characters are arithmetic (otherwise K(ϕ) need not be finite over K).
proofSteps: Hida’s theorem (Hida, Duke 1994, Theorem 8.1), proved through the rationality of the ε-isotypic parts of the cohomology class φ_ℂ (Proposition 3.7) and the integral formula (Theorem 4.6); Shimura proved the totally real case.
The ε-isotypic part of the eigenclass is one-dimensional over ℂ and has a K-rational generator; Ω^ε_Φ is the ratio.
acceptance: F = ℚ: two periods Ω^± (Shimura), the period lines of ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions:L1/period-lines.
F imaginary quadratic: r₁ = 0, a single period.

sources.match: BSW quote Hida’s algebraicity theorem with periods Ω^ε_Φ indexed by Weyl-group characters and note that the period depends on ε_ϕ, not on ϕ restricted to the signs.

nodes.title: The period-normalised modular symbol θ_K of an eigenform
nodes.statement: For an eigenform Φ with Eichler–Shimura class φ_ℂ, the Weyl group {±1}^{Σ(ℝ)} acts on H^q_c(Y₁(𝔫), L₁(V_λ(ℂ)*)) through ι·[x_∞ components] (BSW §3.2.2), commuting with Hecke operators. For a character ε put φ^ε_ℂ := 2^{-r₁} Σ_ι ε(ι) φ_ℂ|ι, which lies in the ε-eigenspace, and φ^ε_K := φ^ε_ℂ/Ω^ε_Φ, which lies in H^q_c(Y₁(𝔫), L₁(V_λ(K)*))[ε]. Then θ_K := Σ_ε φ^ε_K and, for a finite extension L/ℚ_p containing ι_p(K), θ_L is the image of θ_K in H^q_c(Y₁(𝔫), L₂(V_λ(L)*)) through L₁ ≅ L₂.
hypotheses: Periods fixed once for each ε (hida-period-algebraicity).
proofSteps: The Weyl action is induced by ι·(g, P) ↦ (ι·g, P) on local systems; it commutes with Hecke operators.
φ^ε_ℂ is the ε-isotypic projection; K-rationality of φ^ε_K is Hida’s Theorem (BSW Proposition 3.7).
θ_L is obtained by scalar extension along ι_p and the local-system isomorphism of admissible-weight-coefficients.
acceptance: F = ℚ: θ_K = φ⁺/Ω⁺ + φ⁻/Ω⁻, the ±-decomposition of ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions:L0/plus-minus-decomposition.

nodes.title: BSW automorphic cycles X_f and their embedding in Y₁(𝔫)
nodes.statement: For an integral ideal f of F let E(f) = {x ∈ O_{F,+}^× : x ≡ 1 mod f}, F_∞¹ = {x ∈ F_∞⁺ : |x_v|_v = 1 for all v | ∞}, and X_f := F^×\A_F^×/U(f)F_∞¹. Then X_f = ⊔_{y∈Cl⁺_F(f)} X_y, and for representatives a_y (with (a_y)_∞ = 1) multiplication by a_y gives E(f)F_∞¹\F_∞⁺ ≅ X_y, a connected orientable real manifold of dimension q = r₁ + r₂. The map η : A_F^× → GL₂(A_F), x ↦ (x, (xπ_f^{-1})_{v|f}; 0, 1) induces a well-defined η_f : X_f → Y₁(𝔫) sending X_y into the component of Y₁(𝔫) indexed by the image of y in Cl⁺_F.
hypotheses: f integral; π_f the finite idele with components π_w^{-v_w(f)} at w | f (BSW Definition 1.6).
proofSteps: Well-definedness: for γ ∈ F^×, u ∈ U(f), r ∈ F_∞¹, η(γxur) = (γ 0; 0 1)·η(x)·(u, ((u−1)π_f^{-1}); 0, 1)·(r, 0; 0, 1) with (γ 0; 0 1) ∈ GL₂(F), the third factor in Ω₁(𝔫) and the last in the centre-times-K_∞⁺ part (BSW eq. (6)).
Component statement: det η_f(x) = x.
The fibre description is the isomorphism (7) of BSW §4.2.2.
acceptance: F = ℚ: X_f is a disjoint union of copies of ℝ_{>0}, and η_f(x) traces the path from the cusp a/f to ∞ (the modular symbol {a/f} − {∞}).

nodes.title: Classical evaluation maps Ev_{f,j} and Ev_ϕ
nodes.statement: For a Hecke character ϕ of conductor f and infinity type j + v (0 ≤ j ≤ k), let ρ_j : V_λ(A)* → A be evaluation at X^{k−j}Y^j; since e^{j+v} = 1 for e ∈ E(f), ρ_j makes the pulled-back local system on E(f)F_∞¹\F_∞⁺ constant. Ev^{a_y}_{f,j,1} : H^q_c(Y₁(𝔫), L₁(V_λ(A)*)) → A is η_f* followed by restriction to X_y via a_y, (ρ_j)_*, and integration over the oriented q-manifold. Ev_ϕ(φ) := Σ_{y∈Cl⁺_F(f)} ε_ϕϕ_f(a_y)Ev^{a_y}_{f,j,1}(φ) is independent of the representatives a_y (Lemma 5.2), satisfies Ev_ϕ(φ|ι) = ε_ϕ(ι)Ev_ϕ(φ) (Corollary 5.5), and kills the ε-parts with ε ≠ ε_ϕ (Corollary 5.6). The variant Ev^{a_y}_{f,j,2} on L₂-coefficients (pullback, untwisting by ζ_f, restriction, ρ_j) satisfies Ev_2(α(φ)) = π_f^{j+v}Ev_1(φ) (Lemma 10.1) with α : L₁ ≅ L₂, and Ev_{ϕ,2} := Σ ε_ϕϕ_f(a_y)Ev^{a_y}_{f,j,2}.
hypotheses: A any coefficient ring in which the integration makes sense (ℂ, a number field K, or L/ℚ_p).
π_f^{j+v} is the element of L attached to (π_f)_{v|p} with the fixed uniformisers; it equals N(f)^{[j+v]} up to a p-adic unit.
proofSteps: Construct each step as in BSW §4.2.1–4.2.3; integration is the isomorphism H^q_c(E(f)F_∞¹\F_∞⁺, A) ≅ A of an oriented connected q-manifold.
Lemma 5.2: changing a_y to a′_y = fa_yur multiplies Ev^{a_y} by f^{j+v} and ε_ϕϕ_f(a_y) by f^{−j−v}.
Proposition 5.4 and Corollaries 5.5–5.6 by functoriality of the Weyl action on local systems and orthogonality.

nodes.title: The integral formula for twisted L-values (BSW Theorem 4.6)
nodes.statement: Let Φ be a cuspidal eigenform of weight λ = (k, v) and level Ω₁(𝔫) over a number field F, and ϕ a Hecke character of conductor f and infinity type j + v with 0 ≤ j ≤ k. With representatives a_y of Cl⁺_F(f) having trivial infinite components, Σ_{y∈Cl⁺_F(f)} ϕ(a_y)Ev^{a_y}_{f,j,1}(φ_ℂ) = (−1)^{R(j,k)}·|D|·τ(ϕ)·2^{-r₂}·Λ(Φ, ϕ), where R(j, k) = Σ_{v∈Σ(ℂ)} k_v + Σ_{v∈Σ(ℝ)}(k_v + j_v) and D is the discriminant of F. Moreover (Theorem 4.7) if 𝔭 ∣ 𝔫 does not divide f, Σ_{x∈Cl⁺_F(f𝔭)} ϕ(a_x)Ev^{a_x}_{f𝔭,j,1}(φ_ℂ) = (ϕ(𝔭)λ_𝔭 − 1)Σ_y ϕ(a_y)Ev^{a_y}_{f,j,1}(φ_ℂ), so that (Corollary 4.8) for f′ = f∏_{𝔭∈B}𝔭 (B the primes above p unramified in ϕ) the two sums differ by ∏_{𝔭∈B}(ϕ(𝔭)λ_𝔭 − 1).
hypotheses: Φ a Hecke eigenform (for Theorem 4.7, an eigensymbol for all Hecke operators); p ∣ 𝔫 for Corollary 4.8.
proofSteps: Compute δ_y = τ_{a_y}*η_f*φ_ℂ through the Betti–de Rham comparison (Hida §2.5) and write it as Σ_j δ^j_y X^{k−j}Y^j.

For Re s ≫ 0 compute the Mellin-type integrals C^j_y(s) = ∫ δ^j_y(y)|y|^s over E(f)F_∞¹\F_∞⁺ by substituting the Fourier (Whittaker) expansion of Φ (GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer:R16.5/whittaker-integral-comparison) and splitting into archimedean local integrals.

Sum over y ∈ Cl⁺_F(f): the sum over ideals collapses through the Gauss sum identity (BSW Proposition 1.7) to L(Φ, ϕ|·|^s); continuation to s = 0 gives the critical value; C^j_y(0) = Ev^{a_y}_{f,j,1}(φ_ℂ).
Theorem 4.7: examine the Gauss sum at a level raised by 𝔭 and use the U_𝔭-eigenvalue.
acceptance: F = ℚ: the classical Birch–Manin formula Σ_a ϕ(a)φ({a/f} − {∞}) = (unit)·τ(ϕ)·Λ(f, ϕ) of ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions:L1/twisted-mellin-formula.
Corollary 4.8 at ϕ = 1 and f = (1): passing to f′ = ∏_{𝔭|p}𝔭 multiplies by ∏(λ_𝔭 − 1).

nodes.title: Algebraic critical-value formula (BSW Theorem 5.7)
nodes.statement: For a Hecke character ϕ of conductor f and infinity type j + v with 0 ≤ j ≤ k, Ev_ϕ(θ_K) = (−1)^{R(j,k)}·|D|·τ(ϕ)·Λ(Φ, ϕ)/(2^{r₂}Ω^{ε_ϕ}_Φ), an element of K(ϕ); and for the p-adic symbol θ_L, Ev_{ϕ,2}(θ_L) = π_f^{j+v}Ev_ϕ(θ_K) (Corollary 10.2). Each factor is a separate datum: the sign (−1)^{R(j,k)}, the discriminant |D|, the Gauss sum τ(ϕ), the power 2^{-r₂}, the period Ω^{ε_ϕ}_Φ and the completed value Λ(Φ, ϕ).
hypotheses: Representatives with trivial infinite components (then ε_ϕϕ_f(a_y) = ϕ(a_y)); conductor f arbitrary (no ramification condition at p).
proofSteps: Apply integral-formula to φ_ℂ, divide by the period after projecting to the ε_ϕ-part (classical-evaluation-maps, Corollary 5.6).
Algebraicity of the right-hand side is hida-period-algebraicity.
The p-adic version is Lemma 10.1 applied to θ_L.
acceptance: F = ℚ, ϕ = 1, j = 0: Ev(θ_K) = (−1)^{k}·Λ(f, 1)/Ω^{ε}, the period-normalised central-or-critical value.

sources.match: BSW state the algebraic critical-value formula for θ_K and its p-adic version with the extra factor π_f^{j+v}.

nodes.title: Agreement with rational modular symbols for F = ℚ
nodes.statement: For F = ℚ the BSW objects specialise to the rational ones: Y₁(N) is the modular curve, H¹_c(Y₁(N), L₂(V_λ(L)*)) is the space of modular symbols of ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions:L0, the cycle η_f(X_y) is the path {a/f} → {∞}, θ_K is φ⁺/Ω⁺ + φ⁻/Ω⁻ for the period lines of ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions:L1/period-lines, and Theorem 5.7 becomes the twisted Mellin formula of ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions:L1/twisted-mellin-formula. The comparison records: (a) orientation of the cycle (BSW integrate from 0 to ∞ in y = Im z); (b) BSW twist by ϕ(a_y) where the rational formula twists by ϕ^{-1}(a) or uses τ(ϕ̄) — the inversion is explicit; (c) the Gauss sum τ(ϕ) of gauss-sum-and-depleted-l-function against τ(ϕ̄) in the rational normalisation, related by τ(ϕ)τ(ϕ̄) = ϕ(−1)f; (d) period choices: Ω^ε_Φ of BSW and the integral period of ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions:L1/integral-period-lattices differ by an element of K^×, fixed by matching the two lines.
hypotheses: F = ℚ, Φ the adelisation of a newform (AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups:AF.5/gl2-dictionary).
proofSteps: Identify Y₁(N) and the local systems with the rational ones (AF.5/gl2-dictionary, ALS.0 for G = GL₂/ℚ).
Identify the cycle and the evaluation: η_f on X_y = ℝ_{>0}·a_y is y ↦ (y, a/f; 0, 1), whose image is the geodesic from a/f to i∞.
Compare the two critical-value formulas term by term; the scalar between them is a product of a sign, a Gauss-sum inversion and a period ratio, each in K(ϕ)^×.
acceptance: Weight two, ϕ = 1: Ev(θ_K) = −L(f, 1)/Ω⁺ in both normalisations after the sign convention for the path is matched.
A character ϕ of conductor 5: the two formulas differ exactly by ϕ(−1) and the Gauss-sum inversion.

nodes.title: Locally analytic coefficient modules A_λ(L), D_λ(L) for GL₂/F
nodes.statement: Let L/ℚ_p be finite, containing ι_p∘σ(F) for every σ ∈ Σ, and λ = (k, v) admissible. A(L) is the space of locally analytic L-valued functions on O_F ⊗ ℤ_p, with Banach stages A_n(L) of functions analytic on every coset a + p^n(O_F ⊗ ℤ_p). The semigroup Σ₀(p) = {(a b; c d) ∈ M₂(O_F ⊗ ℤ_p) : c ∈ p(O_F ⊗ ℤ_p), a ∈ (O_F ⊗ ℤ_p)^×, ad − bc ≠ 0} acts on the left on A_λ(L) := A(L) by (a b; c d)·f(z) = (ad − bc)^v(a + cz)^k f((b + dz)/(a + cz)), extending the action on V_λ(L) (polynomials of degree ≤ k, de-homogenised). D_λ(L) := Hom_cts(A_λ(L), L) with the right action (µ|γ)(f) = µ(γ·f); it is a nuclear Fréchet space, D_λ(L) = lim_n D_{n,λ}(L) with D_{n,λ} the dual of A_{n,λ}. Dualising V_λ(L) ⊂ A_λ(L) gives the Σ₀(p)-equivariant specialisation D_λ(L) ↠ V_λ(L)*.
hypotheses: L large enough to contain the embeddings; λ admissible; the Σ₀(p)-action uses the chosen identification O_F ⊗ ℤ_p ⊂ L^Σ through the embeddings.
proofSteps: A(L), its Banach stages on finitely many polydiscs of O_F ⊗ ℤ_p ≅ ℤ_p^{[F:ℚ]} and the compactness of A_n ↪ A_{n+1} are LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L0/multivariable-fixed-radius and L0/relatively-compact-restriction; the dual of the compact manifold is nuclear Fréchet by L0/locally-analytic-dual-nuclear and L0/compact-type-nuclear-duality.
The formula defines an action of Σ₀(p) because a + cz is a unit for z ∈ O_F ⊗ ℤ_p when c ∈ p and a is a unit; locally analytic functions are preserved (L0/locally-analytic-pullback).
Specialisation is the transpose of the inclusion of polynomials of degree ≤ k.
acceptance: F = ℚ: A_λ(L) is the space of locally analytic functions on ℤ_p with the weight-k action of Σ₀(p), and D_λ is ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions:L2/weight-k-distributions.

nodes.title: Overconvergent modular symbols over F and the operators U_𝔭
nodes.statement: The space of overconvergent modular symbols is H^q_c(Y₁(𝔫), L₂(D_λ(L))), q = r₁ + r₂, with the specialisation map ρ to H^q_c(Y₁(𝔫), L₂(V_λ(L)*)). For each prime 𝔭 | p fix a uniformiser π_𝔭 ∈ L (as an element of O_F ⊗ ℤ_p supported at 𝔭) and let U_𝔭 be the Hecke operator of the double coset of (1 0; 0 π_𝔭) at 𝔭; U_𝔭 acts on both spaces and ρ is equivariant. For a finite set of operators {U_𝔭 : 𝔭 | p} and h = (h_𝔭) ∈ ℚ^{{𝔭|p}}, M^{≤h} := ∩_𝔭 M^{≤h_𝔭, U_𝔭}. A different uniformiser π′_𝔭 = uπ_𝔭 changes U_𝔭 by the action of a unit and changes the normalisation of eigenvalues accordingly; the renormalised operator U′_𝔭 = π_𝔭^{−v_𝔭(λ)}U_𝔭 (v_𝔭(λ) = Σ_{σ∼𝔭}v_σ) preserves integral structures and shifts slopes by v_𝔭(λ)/e_𝔭.
hypotheses: The level 𝔫 is divisible by p; the centre acts trivially on D_λ(L) (BSW Definition 3.2).
proofSteps: Cohomology with compact supports of the arithmetic local system L₂(D_λ(L)) (ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces:ALS.1/betti-complexes); D_λ(L) is a right Ω₁(𝔫)-module through Ω₁(𝔫) → GL₂(O_F ⊗ ℤ_p) ∩ Σ₀(p).

Hecke operators at 𝔭 | p from the Hecke pair (Σ₀(p)-monoid, Ω₁(𝔫)) acting on (derived) invariants, ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces:ALS.3/hecke-action-on-invariants, realised as correspondences as in ALS.3/hecke-operator-formula; the double coset of (1 0; 0 π_𝔭) lies in Σ₀(p).
Equivariance of ρ is equivariance of the specialisation D_λ → V_λ*.
Change of uniformiser and the shift of slopes: U_𝔭 scaled by π_𝔭^{-v_𝔭(λ)} multiplies eigenvalues by an element of valuation −v_𝔭(λ)/e_𝔭.
acceptance: F = ℚ: the space of overconvergent modular symbols Symb_{Γ₀(N)}(D_k) with U_p of Pollack–Stevens (ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions:L2/control-theorem).

nodes.title: Compactness of the operators at p (corrected BSW Lemma 6.7)
nodes.statement: Let η ∈ GL₂(F) ∩ Σ₀(p) whose lower-right entry d lies in p(O_F ⊗ ℤ_p), for example η = (1 0; 0 p). Then the action of η on D_λ(L) is compact in the sense of BSW Definition 6.6: it factors through D_λ(L) → D_{n−1,λ}(L) → D_{n,λ}(L) for every n, because z ↦ (b + dz)/(a + cz) maps each closed disc of radius |p|^{n−1} into one of radius |p|^n. Consequently the lift of the operator U_p of the double coset of (1 0; 0 p) at all primes above p (which agrees with ∏_{𝔭|p} U_𝔭^{e_𝔭} up to the action of the unit p·∏_𝔭π_𝔭^{−e_𝔭} of O_F ⊗ ℤ_p) to a finite complex of copies of D_λ(L) computing H^•_c(Y₁(𝔫), L₂(D_λ(L))) is compact. An arbitrary element of GL₂(F) ∩ Σ₀(p), for example the identity, does not act compactly.
hypotheses: d ∈ p(O_F ⊗ ℤ_p) (radius improvement in every coordinate); for a single U_𝔭 the improvement is only in the 𝔭-coordinates.
proofSteps: For η with d ∈ p and c ∈ p, the map z ↦ (b + dz)/(a + cz) is analytic and contracts every coordinate disc by |p|, so pullback sends A_{n,λ} into A_{n−1,λ} and the transpose factors D_λ → D_{n−1,λ} → D_{n,λ} (LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L4/contracting-family-compactness, L4/compact-frechet-factorization).

The cellular chains C_• of ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces:ALS.1/finite-complex-model are bounded finite free over ℤ[G(F) × K], so Hom(C_•, D_λ(L)) computes the cohomology with terms finite sums of copies of D_λ(L) (only the finite freeness of C_• is used, not the finite-projective coefficient clause); lift U_p to it; each term’s action is a finite sum of compact maps.
The identity is not compact: the coefficient functionals of degree m have norm 1 on D_{0,λ} and |p|^{-m} on D_{1,λ}, so no continuous factorisation through D_{0,λ} → D_{1,λ} exists (sourceIssues E2).
acceptance: F = ℚ: (1 0; 0 p) acts compactly on D_k (Pollack–Stevens), the case used by ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions:L2/control-theorem.

nodes.title: Slope decompositions of overconvergent cohomology
nodes.statement: For admissible λ, every i and every h ∈ ℚ, H^i_c(Y₁(𝔫), L₂(D_λ(L))) has a slope ≤ h decomposition for U_p: M = M₁ ⊕ M₂ with M₁ finite-dimensional, det(1 − U_pX)|M₁ of slope ≤ h, and Q*(U_p) invertible on M₂ for every Q of slope ≤ h. Because the U_𝔭 commute with U_p, the finite-dimensional M^{≤h,U_p} decomposes further under each U_𝔭, giving M^{≤h} for h ∈ ℚ^{{𝔭|p}}. Slope decompositions are exact in short exact sequences of modules that admit them, and for a compact operator on a nuclear Fréchet space M = lim M_n, M^{≤h} ≅ M_n^{≤h} for every n (also for complexes and their cohomology).
hypotheses: The endpoint convention of LocallyAnalyticDistributions §4.16: the complement inverts every polynomial whose roots have valuation ≤ h, equality included.
proofSteps: Riesz theory for a compact operator on a nuclear Fréchet complex (LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L4/frechet-finite-slope, L4/finite-slope-summands) applied to the compact lift of U_p (up-compactness).
Pass to cohomology (L4/cohomology-slope-comparison).
Refine the finite-dimensional U_p-part by the commuting U_𝔭.
Exactness and independence of n: Urban’s Corollary 2.3.5 and Lemma 2.3.13 (BSW Lemma 8.1(i)–(ii)).
acceptance: F = ℚ: Pollack–Stevens’ slope decomposition of Symb(D_k).

sources.locator: Definitions 7.1–7.2, Theorem 7.3 and its proof sketch, pp. 22–23; Lemma 8.1(i)–(ii), pp. 23–24

nodes.title: Vanishing below the weight-shifted slope (corrected BSW Lemma 8.1(iii), Corollary 8.4)
nodes.statement: Let ν = (k, v) with k + 2v parallel (k_σ may be negative) and h ∈ ℚ^{{𝔭|p}} with h_𝔭 < v_𝔭(ν)/e_𝔭 for some 𝔭 | p. Then H^r_c(Y₁(𝔫), L₂(D_ν(L)))^{≤h} = 0 for all r, and the same holds for Σ₀(p)-stable submodules of D_ν(L) and quotients by them. The underlying lemma requires a bounded open O_L-lattice 𝓜 in the Banach module M = H^r_c(Y₁(𝔫), L₂(D_{ν,0}(L))), stable under the O_L-algebra generated by the renormalised operators U′_𝔭 = π_𝔭^{−v_𝔭(ν)}U_𝔭; then any vector of slope < 0 for some U′_𝔭 would generate an unbounded orbit inside 𝓜.
hypotheses: The lattice is bounded and open (absorbing); stability is under O_L[U′_𝔭], not under L-scalars (sourceIssues E3).
proofSteps: Take 𝓜 the image of H^r_c(Y₁(𝔫), L₂(D_{ν,0}(O_L))); it is bounded because the integral distributions have norm ≤ 1, and open because it spans after inverting p; U′_𝔭 preserves it.
If M^{≤h′} ≠ 0 with h′_𝔭 < 0, after a finite extension there is x with U′_𝔭x = αx, v_p(α) < 0; rescale x into 𝓜; then α^n x = U′_𝔭^n x ∈ 𝓜 for all n while ‖α^n x‖ → ∞, contradicting boundedness.
Pass from D_{ν,0} to D_ν by the Banach-stage comparison of slope-decomposition, and from U′_𝔭 to U_𝔭 by the slope shift h_𝔭 = h′_𝔭 + v_𝔭(ν)/e_𝔭.
Submodules and quotients by the long exact sequence and exactness.
acceptance: F = ℚ, ν = (k, v) with v = −1: nothing of slope < −1 for U_p.

nodes.title: Theta maps and partially overconvergent coefficients
nodes.statement: For σ ∈ Σ let λ_σ = (k′, v′) with k′_σ = −2 − k_σ, v′_σ = v_σ + k_σ + 1 and k′_τ = k_τ, v′_τ = v_τ for τ ≠ σ. The derivative (d/dz_σ)^{k_σ+1} defines Θ_σ : A_λ(L) → A_{λ_σ}(L), equivariant for Σ₀(p) but changing the U_𝔭-normalisation at 𝔭 = 𝔭(σ) by det^{k_σ+1}; Θ*_σ : D_{λ_σ}(L) → D_λ(L) is its dual. For J ⊂ Σ, A^J_ν(L) is the space of functions locally analytic in z_σ (σ ∉ J) and locally polynomial of degree ≤ max(k_σ, 0) in z_σ (σ ∈ J), and D^J_ν its dual. Ordering Σ = {σ₁, …, σ_d} and J_s = {σ₁, …, σ_s}, coker(Θ*_s) = D^{J_s}_λ and there is the exact sequence ⊕_σ D_{λ_σ}(L) → D_λ(L) → V_{λ,loc}(L)* → 0 (the last terms of Urban’s locally analytic BGG resolution), together with the short exact sequences 0 → D^{J_{s−1}}_{λ_{σ_s}} → D^{J_{s−1}}_λ → D^{J_s}_λ → 0.
hypotheses: λ admissible; the quotient D^{J_{s−1}}_{λ_{σ_s}} of D_{λ_{σ_s}} is the one making the sequence exact (BSW eq. (10)).
proofSteps: Θ_σ is well defined on locally analytic functions, expanding in local power series in the variable z_σ.
Equivariance: differentiating the weight-λ action k_σ + 1 times in z_σ gives the weight-λ_σ action (Urban Proposition 3.2.11).
Exactness of the BGG tail: a distribution not in the image of Θ*_1 is detected by a monomial of degree ≤ k_{σ₁} in z_{σ₁}; induction on s (Urban Proposition 3.2.12).
acceptance: F = ℚ: Θ = (d/dz)^{k+1} : A_k → A_{−2−k} and the exact sequence D_{−2−k} → D_k → V_k* → 0 of Stevens.

sources.locator: §8.2, eq. (8), Definition 8.5, Proposition 8.6, pp. 25–26; eq. (10), p. 27

nodes.title: BSW control theorem in small slope (Theorem 8.7)
nodes.statement: Let λ = (k, v) be admissible and h = (h_𝔭) ∈ ℚ^{{𝔭|p}}, with k⁰_𝔭 := min{k_σ : σ ∼ 𝔭} and v_𝔭(λ) := Σ_{σ∼𝔭} v_σ. If for every 𝔭 | p h_𝔭 < (k⁰_𝔭 + v_𝔭(λ) + 1)/e_𝔭, then for every r the specialisation ρ : H^r_c(Y₁(𝔫), L₂(D_λ(L)))^{≤h} → H^r_c(Y₁(𝔫), L₂(V_λ(L)*))^{≤h} is an isomorphism, the slope ≤ h subspaces being taken for the U_𝔭 normalised by the fixed uniformisers (with v_p(p) = 1). Renormalising U_𝔭 to U′_𝔭 shifts the bound by −v_𝔭(λ)/e_𝔭.
hypotheses: The level hypothesis p ∣ 𝔫 (Iwahori-type level at every 𝔭 | p); L contains the embeddings and the eigenvalues.
proofSteps: Replace V_λ(L)* by V_{λ,loc}(L)* using the Banach-stage comparison (Lemma 8.1(ii)): the slope ≤ h parts agree.

Lemma 8.8: for each s, specialisation D^{J_{s−1}}_λ → D^{J_s}_λ induces an isomorphism on slope ≤ h cohomology, because the kernel D^{J_{s−1}}_{λ_{σ_s}} has weight with v_{𝔭}(λ_{σ_s}) = v_𝔭(λ) + k_{σ_s} + 1 and negative-slope-vanishing kills its slope ≤ h cohomology when h_𝔭 < (k_{σ_s} + v_𝔭(λ) + 1)/e_𝔭 (theta-maps-partial-classicality, long exact sequence).
Induction on s from D^∅ = D_λ to D^Σ = V_{λ,loc}*.
acceptance: F = ℚ: Stevens’ control theorem for slope < k + 1 (ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions:L2/control-theorem).
F imaginary quadratic, weight (k, k), p split: slope < k + 1 at each prime above p (Williams Theorem 6.10).

sources.locator: Theorem 8.7, Lemma 8.8 and their proofs, pp. 26–27; small-slope definition in the introduction, p. 3
sources.match: BSW prove that specialisation is an isomorphism on slope ≤ h parts when h_𝔭 < (k⁰_𝔭 + v_𝔭(λ) + 1)/e_𝔭 for every 𝔭 | p.
Williams’ Bianchi control theorem with the slope bound at each prime above p.

nodes.title: Unique small-slope overconvergent eigenlift
nodes.statement: Let Φ be a cuspidal eigenform of weight λ and level Ω₁(𝔫) whose U_𝔭-eigenvalues λ_𝔭 satisfy v_p(λ_𝔭) < (k⁰_𝔭 + v_𝔭(λ) + 1)/e_𝔭 for every 𝔭 | p (small slope). Then the p-adic modular symbol θ_L of Φ lies in the small-slope part, and there is a unique Ψ_Φ ∈ H^q_c(Y₁(𝔫), L₂(D_λ(L))) with ρ(Ψ_Φ) = θ_L; Ψ_Φ is a Hecke eigensymbol with the same eigenvalues as Φ.
hypotheses: L contains the eigenvalues of Φ; small slope at every 𝔭 | p.
proofSteps: θ_L is an eigensymbol with U_𝔭-eigenvalue λ_𝔭, hence lies in the slope ≤ h part for h_𝔭 = v_p(λ_𝔭).
Apply control-theorem in degree q; the preimage of an eigenvector under a Hecke-equivariant isomorphism is an eigenvector with the same eigenvalues.
acceptance: F = ℚ: the Pollack–Stevens overconvergent lift of a small-slope p-stabilised newform (ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions:L2/overconvergent-lift).

sources.locator: Introduction p. 3; §9 opening p. 28; §11 opening p. 38

nodes.title: Overconvergent evaluation maps Ev^{a_y}_{f,†}
nodes.statement: For f ∣ p^∞ and Ψ ∈ H^q_c(Y₁(𝔫), L₂(D_λ(L))): pull back along η_f; untwist the action of units by ζ : µ ↦ µ * (1 −1; 0 (π_f)_{v|p}) (an element of Σ₀(p)), so that u ∈ U(f) acts by (u 0; 0 1); pull back to the component through τ_{a_y}, where now e ∈ E(f) acts by (e^{-1} 0; 0 1); restrict coefficients along ν : D_λ(L) → D^{f,+}_λ(L), the dual of A^{f,+}_λ(L) = {f ∈ A_λ(L) : (e 0; 0 1)·f = f for all e ∈ E(f)} = {f : f(ez) = e^{k+v}f(z)}, which makes the local system constant; integrate over the oriented q-manifold. The result is Ev^{a_y}_{f,†}(Ψ) ∈ D^{f,+}_λ(L); it depends on the representative a_y.
hypotheses: f ∣ p^∞; representatives a_y of Cl⁺_F(f) with trivial infinite components.
proofSteps: Each step is a map of local systems on X_f or on E(f)F_∞¹\F_∞⁺ (BSW §9.1.1–9.1.4); the untwisting matrix lies in Σ₀(p).
After restriction to D^{f,+}_λ the local system is constant, and integration identifies compactly supported top cohomology with the coefficients.
acceptance: F = ℚ, f = p^m: Ev^{a}_{f,†}(Ψ) is Ψ({a/p^m} − {∞}) up to the matrix (1 −1; 0 p^m).

nodes.title: Weighted inversion of unit-invariant test functions (BSW Definition 9.4)
nodes.statement: For ψ : O_F ⊗ ℤ_p → L supported on {z ∈ (O_F ⊗ ℤ_p)^× : z ≡ 1 mod f} with ψ(ez) = ψ(z) for e ∈ E(f), define ψ* ∈ A^{f,+}_λ(L) by ψ*(z) = z^{k+v}ψ(z^{-1}) on units and ψ*(z) = 0 otherwise. It is locally analytic when ψ is, and satisfies the covariance ψ*(ez) = e^{k+v}ψ*(z). The inversion z^{-1} (rather than z) makes the twist compatible with the contragredient change of evaluation maps under a change of representatives: for ũ ∈ U(f), ((ũ 0; 0 1)·ψ*)(z) = (ψ(ũ·))*(z).
hypotheses: ψ supported in the units, so extension by zero is continuous (the units are clopen in O_F ⊗ ℤ_p).
proofSteps: Define pointwise; local analyticity is preserved by multiplication by the analytic function z^{k+v} and by z ↦ z^{-1} on the units, and extension by zero along the clopen unit group (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L0/clopen-zero-extension for continuity, LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L0/locally-analytic-pullback for analyticity).
Covariance: ψ*(ez) = (ez)^{k+v}ψ(e^{-1}z^{-1}) = e^{k+v}z^{k+v}ψ(z^{-1}) using E(f)-invariance of ψ.
Translation formula: ((u 0; 0 1)·f)(z) = u^{k+v}f(u^{-1}z) for the weight-λ action, which gives the stated identity.
acceptance: F = ℚ, k + v = 2, ψ(z) = z³: ψ*(z) = z^{-1} on ℤ_p^×; at z = 2 (p ≠ 2) the value is 1/2, not 2 or 32.

nodes.title: The distribution µ^f_Ψ of a level f (BSW Definition 9.5)
nodes.statement: Let f ∣ p^∞ be divisible by every prime above p and A_f = {a_y} representatives of Cl⁺_F(f). For a locally analytic function ϕ on Cl⁺_F(p^∞) with fibre functions ϕ_{a_y}(z) = ϕ(a_y z) on G = {z ≡ 1 mod f}/Ē_+(f) (forward chart, sourceIssues E1), define µ^{A_f}_Ψ(ϕ) := Σ_{y∈Cl⁺_F(f)} Ev^{a_y}_{f,†}(Ψ)(ϕ*_{a_y}). This is a locally analytic distribution on Cl⁺_F(p^∞) (an element of D(Cl⁺_F(p^∞), L) of ray-class-distributions).
hypotheses: f divisible by all primes above p; representatives fixed.
proofSteps: Each summand is a continuous linear functional of ϕ: restriction to the fibre, inversion-weight-twist, then the distribution Ev^{a_y}_{f,†}(Ψ).
Finite sum over Cl⁺_F(f).
acceptance: F = ℚ, f = p: µ^p_Ψ(ϕ) = Ψ({0} − {∞}) evaluated at the twisted restriction of ϕ to 1 + pℤ_p plus the other residue classes, the Pollack–Stevens µ before normalisation.

nodes.title: Independence of class-group representatives (BSW Proposition 9.6)
nodes.statement: For fixed f, µ^{A_f}_Ψ does not depend on the representatives A_f; write µ^f_Ψ. Precisely, if a′_y = a_yγur with γ ∈ F^×, u ∈ U(f), r ∈ F_∞¹, then Ev^{a′_y}_{f,†}(Ψ) = Ev^{a_y}_{f,†}(Ψ) * (ũ^{-1} 0; 0 1) and, with the forward chart, ϕ_{a′_y}(z) = ϕ_{a_y}(ũz), so ϕ*_{a′_y} = (ũ 0; 0 1)·ϕ*_{a_y}; the two changes cancel in each summand.
hypotheses: Forward chart ϕ_a(z) = ϕ(az) (sourceIssues E1); ũ the image of u in U(f)/U(p^∞).
proofSteps: Describe τ_{a_y} on local systems: (γa_yur, µ) ↦ (r, µ * (ũ^{-1} 0; 0 1)), well defined by the computation in the proof of Proposition 9.6.
Compute the effect of the representative change on the fibre functions and on their weighted inversions (inversion-weight-twist, weightedInversion_translate).

nodes.title: The U_f-eigenvalue λ_f of a refined eigensymbol
nodes.statement: Let Ψ be an eigenclass for every U_𝔭, 𝔭 | p, with eigenvalues λ_𝔭 ∈ L^× (nonzero because Ψ has finite slope). For f = ∏_{𝔭|p} 𝔭^{n(𝔭)} put U_f := ∏_𝔭 U_𝔭^{n(𝔭)} and λ_f := ∏_𝔭 λ_𝔭^{n(𝔭)} ∈ L^×, the U_f-eigenvalue of Ψ. It depends on the chosen uniformisers through the normalisation of the U_𝔭.
hypotheses: Finite set of primes above p; λ_𝔭 nonzero.
proofSteps: Finite product in the commutative group L^×; U_f is well defined because the U_𝔭 commute.
acceptance: Monoid homomorphism from exponent vectors to L^×.

nodes.title: The norm relation µ^{f𝔭}_Ψ = λ_𝔭µ^f_Ψ (BSW Lemma 9.8, Proposition 9.9)
nodes.statement: Let f ∣ p^∞ be divisible by every prime above p and 𝔭 | p. (i) The trace X_{f𝔭} → X_f intertwines U_𝔭: ζ_*η_f^*(Ψ|U_𝔭) = Tr(ζ_*η_{f𝔭}^*Ψ). (ii) With representatives A_{f𝔭} = {a_yu_r} built from A_f and u_r ∈ U(f) running over U(f)/E(f)U(f𝔭), Ev^{a_yu_r}_{f𝔭,†}(Ψ) * (ũ_r 0; 0 1) = Ev^{a_y}_{f,†}(Ψ|U_𝔭) restricted to G_r = {z : ez ≡ u_r mod f𝔭 for some e ∈ E(f)}. (iii) If Ψ is an eigensymbol for U_𝔭 with eigenvalue λ_𝔭, then µ^{f𝔭}_Ψ = λ_𝔭µ^f_Ψ.
hypotheses: f divisible by every prime above p (this is where the hypothesis enters).
proofSteps: (i) is Barrera Salazar’s Lemme 5.2 for the Hilbert case, whose proof works for any F: the trace along the finite covering of cycles X_{f𝔭} → X_f (L1/automorphic-cycles, cycleTrace) matches the trace in U_𝔭 viewed as a correspondence on Y₁(𝔫) (ALS.3/level-trace).
(ii) follows from (i) and the commutative diagram of the trace with the restriction to G_r, using the representative change of overconvergent-evaluation.
(iii) For ϕ on Cl⁺_F(p^∞), ϕ*_{a_y}|_{G_r} = (ũ_r^{-1} 0; 0 1)·ϕ*_{a_yu_r}; sum (ii) over r ∈ R and y and replace Ψ|U_𝔭 by λ_𝔭Ψ.
acceptance: F = ℚ: µ^{p^{m+1}} = αµ^{p^m}, the distribution property of Pollack–Stevens’ µ before normalisation.

sources.locator: §9.4, Lemma 9.8 and Proposition 9.9 with proofs, pp. 33–34
sources.match: BSW relate the evaluation at level f𝔭 to the evaluation of Ψ|U_𝔭 at level f through the trace and deduce µ^{f𝔭}_Ψ = λ_𝔭µ^f_Ψ for an eigensymbol.

nodes.title: The BSW p-adic L-function µ_Ψ = λ_f^{-1}µ^f_Ψ (Theorem 9.10, Definition 9.11)
nodes.statement: For a U_𝔭-eigenclass Ψ (all 𝔭 | p) and any f ∣ p^∞ divisible by every prime above p, µ_Ψ := λ_f^{-1}µ^f_Ψ ∈ D(Cl⁺_F(p^∞), L). For Ψ = Ψ_Φ the small-slope eigenlift of a cuspidal eigenform, µ_Φ := µ_{Ψ_Φ} is the p-adic L-function of Φ. It depends on the fixed uniformisers at the primes above p and on the periods Ω^ε_Φ, and on nothing else.
hypotheses: Ψ an eigenclass with nonzero U_𝔭-eigenvalues.
proofSteps: Scalar multiple of the distribution µ^f_Ψ by the unit λ_f^{-1}.
Independence of f and of the representatives is normalised-evaluation-common-level and finite-evaluation-representative.
acceptance: F = ℚ: µ_Ψ is the Pollack–Stevens p-adic L-function α^{-m}µ^{p^m}.

tests.statement: With one prime above p, λ_𝔭 = 2 and µ^{𝔭^n} = 7·2^n·δ: normalisation gives 7δ at every n ≥ 1.

tests.name: normalise_two_incomparable
tests.statement: With λ_{𝔭₁} = 2, λ_{𝔭₂} = 3 and µ^f = 5·2^{n₁}3^{n₂}δ: the incomparable levels (1, 2) and (2, 1) give the same µ = 5δ.

tests.name: normalise_excluded_zero_level
tests.statement: A family with µ^{(1)} = 3δ and µ^{𝔭^n} = 2^nδ for n ≥ 1 satisfies every relation between admissible levels, yet λ_{(1)}^{-1}µ^{(1)} = 3δ ≠ δ; level (1) is not admissible.

nodes.title: Independence of the level (BSW Theorem 9.10)
nodes.statement: If Ψ is an eigenclass for every U_𝔭 (𝔭 | p), then λ_f^{-1}µ^f_Ψ = λ_{f′}^{-1}µ^{f′}_Ψ for all f, f′ ∣ p^∞ each divisible by every prime above p. The conclusion does not extend to levels missing a prime above p.
hypotheses: The admissible levels are exactly those divisible by every prime above p; no comparability of f and f′ is assumed.
proofSteps: By norm-relation, λ_{f𝔭}^{-1}µ^{f𝔭} = λ_f^{-1}λ_𝔭^{-1}λ_𝔭µ^f = λ_f^{-1}µ^f for each admissible f and 𝔭 | p.
For admissible f ∣ h, induct on the total exponent difference, raising one deficient prime at a time (each intermediate level stays admissible).
For arbitrary admissible f, f′ compare both with h = lcm(f, f′); this is the instance of L0/conditional-evaluation-principle’s independence clause.
acceptance: Two primes above p: levels 𝔭₁𝔭₂² and 𝔭₁²𝔭₂ both compare with 𝔭₁²𝔭₂².

sources.match: BSW deduce from Proposition 9.9 that λ_f^{-1}µ^f_Ψ is independent of f among levels divisible by every prime above p.

nodes.title: Compatibility of classical and overconvergent evaluations (BSW Proposition 10.3, Corollary 10.4)
nodes.statement: For Ψ ∈ H^q_c(Y₁(𝔫), L₂(D_λ(L))), evaluation at z^{k−j} of Ev^{a_y}_{f,†}(Ψ) equals Ev^{a_y}_{f,j,2}(ρ(Ψ)). Consequently, if φ is a small-slope Hecke eigensymbol with U_f-eigenvalue λ_f and eigenlift Ψ, then for every Hecke character ϕ of infinity type j + v (0 ≤ j ≤ k) and conductor f ∣ p^∞ divisible by every prime above p, µ_Ψ(ϕ_{p-fin}) = λ_f^{-1}Ev_{ϕ,2}(φ).
hypotheses: f divisible by every prime above p for the corollary.
proofSteps: At steps 1–3 of the construction the specialisation commutes with η_f, ζ_f and τ_{a_y} on local systems.
At step 4, V_λ(L)* ↪ A_λ(L) by P(X, Y) ↦ P(z, 1), so restriction to D^+_λ followed by evaluation at z^{k−j} equals evaluation of the classical coefficient at X^{k−j}Y^j.
Combine with BSW eq. (13) for µ_Ψ(ϕ_{p-fin}).
acceptance: F = ℚ: µ(χz^j) equals the twisted classical modular-symbol sum divided by α^m, Pollack–Stevens’ interpolation step.

sources.locator: Proposition 10.3 and Corollary 10.4, p. 37; eq. (13), p. 35
sources.match: BSW show the overconvergent and classical evaluation maps commute with specialisation and deduce µ_Ψ(ϕ_{p-fin}) = λ_f^{-1}Ev_{ϕ,2}(φ) at characters ramified at every prime above p.

nodes.title: Interpolation of critical L-values (BSW Theorem 11.1)
nodes.statement: Let Φ be a small-slope cuspidal eigenform over F of weight λ = (k, v), level Ω₁(𝔫) with p ∣ 𝔫, and µ_Φ its p-adic L-function. For every Hecke character ϕ of conductor f ∣ p^∞ and infinity type j + v with 0 ≤ j ≤ k, with B the set of primes above p not dividing f: µ_Φ(ϕ_{p-fin}) = (−1)^{R(j,k)}·|D|·τ(ϕ)·π_f^{j+v}·(2^{r₂}λ_fΩ^{ε_ϕ}_Φ)^{-1}·∏_{𝔭∈B}Z_𝔭·Λ(Φ, ϕ), where Z_𝔭 = ϕ_{p-fin}(π_𝔭)(1 − λ_𝔭^{-1}ϕ(𝔭)^{-1}), R(j, k) = Σ_{v∈Σ(ℝ)}(j_v + k_v) + Σ_{v∈Σ(ℂ)}k_v, D the discriminant of F, τ(ϕ) the Gauss sum, λ_f the U_f-eigenvalue and Ω^{ε_ϕ}_Φ the period. Each factor is a named quantity: sign, discriminant, Gauss sum, uniformiser power, power of 2, refined eigenvalue, period, Euler-type factor at each unramified 𝔭 | p, completed L-value.
hypotheses: Small slope at every 𝔭 | p; Φ’s eigenlift Ψ_Φ; fixed uniformisers and periods.
proofSteps: Characters ramified at every 𝔭 | p: classical-overconvergent-compatibility plus critical-value-formula (with Corollary 10.2’s π_f^{j+v}).
General f (Lemma 10.5): pass to f′ = f∏_{𝔭∈B}𝔭, use integral-formula’s change of conductor (Corollary 4.8) and the identity π_𝔭^{j+v} = ϕ_{p-fin}(π_𝔭)ϕ(𝔭)^{-1} to turn ∏(ϕ(𝔭)λ_𝔭 − 1) into ∏λ_𝔭Z_𝔭.
acceptance: F = ℚ, ϕ = 1 (f = (1), B = {p}, λ_(1) = 1, ε_ϕ = +): µ_Φ(1) = (−1)^{k}·(1 − λ_p^{-1})·Λ(Φ, 1)/Ω⁺_Φ, the factor (1 − α^{-1}) at the trivial character; Λ(Φ, 1) is the L-value of the level-𝔫 eigenform Φ itself, so for the p-stabilisation of a newform of level prime to p it already contains the second Euler factor (1 − β/p), and the product is Mazur–Tate–Teitelbaum’s (1 − α^{-1})(1 − β/p).
F imaginary quadratic: compare Williams Theorem 7.4 (formula with 2ψ_f(x_f)λ_f^{-1}/(ψ(x_f)Dwτ(ψ^{-1}))).

sources.locator: Lemma 10.5 and eq. (15), p. 38; Theorem 11.1, pp. 38–39
sources.match: BSW prove the interpolation formula at all characters of p-power conductor, with the factors Z_𝔭 at the primes above p where ϕ is unramified.
Williams’ Bianchi interpolation formula, the imaginary quadratic instance in his normalisation.

nodes.title: Choice-independence over a general number field and its limits
nodes.statement: For F an arbitrary number field, µ_Φ is independent of the class-group representatives and of the admissible level f, depending only on Φ, the periods and the uniformisers at the primes above p (Proposition 9.6, Theorem 9.10). BSW prove no growth (admissibility) bound for general F: a growth notion on Cl⁺_F(p^∞) adapted to the available critical characters is not known in general, and when Cl⁺_F(p^∞) has dimension r₂ + 1 + δ_{F,p} larger than the number of independent infinity-type directions (for example F = ℚ(∛2), dimension 2 but only parallel types), interpolation cannot determine µ_Φ. Per-place growth for general F is an open statement, not a target of this layer.
hypotheses: F arbitrary; Φ small slope.
proofSteps: Independence: finite-evaluation-representative and normalised-evaluation-common-level.

Non-uniqueness mechanism: by leopoldt-dimension-formula the ray-class limit has dimension r₂ + 1 + δ, while by locally-algebraic-characters the avatars of critical characters only vary in the directions of admissible infinity types (one direction if F has a real place); the conditional-evaluation-principle’s uniqueness clause needs avatars spanning the test functions of the growth degree in every chart direction.
acceptance: F = ℚ(∛2): the critical characters lie in the parallel direction while the group has dimension 2 (if the Leopoldt defect is zero).

sources.match: BSW explain that admissibility gives uniqueness for F totally real or imaginary quadratic, that over a general field the right growth notion on Cl⁺_F(p^∞) is unclear (with Loeffler’s cubic-field example), and that they settle for independence of choices.

nodes.title: Growth and uniqueness when F is totally real or imaginary quadratic
nodes.statement: (a) F imaginary quadratic, Φ of weight (k, k) with U_𝔭-eigenvalues a_𝔭, v(a_𝔭) < (k + 1)/e_𝔭 for every 𝔭 | p: the p-adic L-function is (h_𝔭)_{𝔭|p}-admissible with h_𝔭 = v_p(a_𝔭), and hence is the unique such distribution with the interpolation values (Williams, Theorem 7.4). (b) F totally real, (π, α) a non-critical p-refinement of a cohomological cuspidal representation (unramified principal series at 𝔭 | p): the p-adic L-function L^ε_p(π, α) has growth bounded by Σ_{v|p}e_v v_p(α_v) + Σ_σ (κ_σ − w)/2, and if the Leopoldt defect of F at p is zero it is uniquely determined by its support, growth, interpolation and variation properties (Bergdall–Hansen, Theorem 1.1.2(c),(f)); with vanishing defect the group is one-dimensional, so in small slope a distribution of the same growth is already determined by its critical values (Amice–Vélu, Bergdall–Hansen §1.8). In case (a) the BSW distribution µ_Φ is Williams’ (BSW §12), so it is unique. In case (b) µ_Φ equals L^ε_p(π, α) under vanishing defect once µ_Φ is known to have growth below the critical range; that growth bound for the overconvergent-cycle construction over totally real F is due to Barrera Salazar (cited by BSW §12 and Bergdall–Hansen §1.8), is proved neither by BSW nor by Bergdall–Hansen, and is a recorded gap here. The slope conditions are those of the cited theorems.
hypotheses: (a): F imaginary quadratic, parallel weight, small slope at each prime above p.
(b): F totally real, Leopoldt defect zero for uniqueness, non-critical refinement (implied by small slope); the growth bound for µ_Φ itself is the gap on Barrera Salazar’s admissibility.
proofSteps: (a) Admissibility of slope-h eigensymbol values (Williams Definition 5.10 and Proposition 5.13; Definition 6.14 and Proposition 6.15 when p splits) and Amice–Vélu–Vishik uniqueness in the two-dimensional group (LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L2/tensor-multidegree-extension).
(b) Growth from the period maps of Bergdall–Hansen §7.4; uniqueness from Amice–Vélu in the one-dimensional group given by Leopoldt (LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L2/amice-velu-vishik).

Agreement with µ_Φ: in (a) µ_Φ is Williams’ distribution (the cycle is the path from 0 to ∞); in (b) both satisfy the interpolation of bsw-interpolation, and once µ_Φ has the growth bound (Barrera Salazar, gap) uniqueness (L0/conditional-evaluation-principle) identifies BSW’s evaluation-map construction with Bergdall–Hansen’s period-map construction; Bergdall–Hansen leave this identification open without Leopoldt (§1.8).
acceptance: F = ℚ(i), p split, weight (0, 0), ordinary at both primes: µ is a measure, unique.

sources.locator: Definition 5.10 p. 28; Definition 6.14 and Proposition 6.15, p. 35; Theorem 7.4 p. 40
sources.match: Williams proves that his Bianchi p-adic L-function is (h_𝔭)-admissible with h_𝔭 = v_p(a_𝔭) and hence unique.

Bergdall–Hansen give the growth bound and uniqueness under vanishing Leopoldt defect for Hilbert modular forms, and note that without Leopoldt the comparison with other constructions is not settled, while attributing the correct growth of the overconvergent-cycle construction over totally real F to Barrera Salazar’s thesis.
BSW point to the totally real and imaginary quadratic cases as those where admissibility gives uniqueness.

nodes.title: Specialisations: ℚ, Hilbert and Bianchi
nodes.statement: (a) F = ℚ: µ_Φ equals the Pollack–Stevens p-adic L-function of ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions:L2/p-adic-l-function for the same refinement, once the periods are matched as in L1/rational-modular-symbol-comparison. (b) F totally real: weights λ = (k, v) with k + 2v parallel include nonparallel k (Hilbert forms of nonparallel weight satisfying the parity condition), and the small-slope condition reads h_𝔭 < (min_{σ∼𝔭}k_σ + v_𝔭(λ) + 1)/e_𝔭; µ_Φ is the Hilbert p-adic L-function. (c) F imaginary quadratic: weight (k, k), q = 1, and µ_Φ is Williams’ Bianchi p-adic L-function. In each case the factor dictionary (signs, Gauss sums τ(ϕ) versus τ(ϕ^{-1}), discriminant powers, periods) is stated explicitly.
hypotheses: The rational, Hilbert and Bianchi constructions use their own period normalisations, recorded in the comparison.
proofSteps: (a) Identify the overconvergent symbols and evaluation at {a/p^m} − {∞} with Pollack–Stevens’ (BSW §9 opening), then compare the interpolation formulas.
(b) Specialise BSW’s weights and slope bound to F totally real; agreement with Bergdall–Hansen follows from growth-uniqueness-totally-real-imaginary-quadratic under Leopoldt.
(c) Compare with Williams Theorem 7.4, matching (−1)^{k+q+r}2ψ_f(x_f)λ_f^{-1}/(ψ(x_f)Dwτ(ψ^{-1})) with BSW’s factors.
acceptance: F = ℚ, an ordinary weight-2 form: µ_Φ is the Mazur–Swinnerton-Dyer measure up to the period normalisation.

sources.locator: Introduction pp. 1–3; Definition 1.8 p. 8; §9 opening p. 28
sources.match: BSW present their construction as generalising Pollack–Stevens over ℚ, Barrera Salazar’s Hilbert and Williams’ Bianchi constructions, with admissible weights allowing nonparallel k.
Williams’ Bianchi interpolation formula and normalisation.

nodes.title: Values of partial zeta functions at negative integers as distributions
nodes.statement: Let F be a totally real field (F ≠ ℚ allowed and ℚ as the base case), f a nonzero integral ideal and G_f the narrow ray class group modulo f. For ε : G_f → ℂ, L(s, ε) := Σ_{𝔞 ⊂ O_F prime to f} ε(𝔞)N𝔞^{-s} (Re s > 1), continued meromorphically with at most a simple pole at s = 1. For k ≥ 1 and ε with values in a ℚ-vector space V, L(1 − k, ε) ∈ V is defined by linearity once Siegel–Klingen rationality is known. For an ideal f′ divisible by every prime above p and G := lim_n G_{f′p^n} = Cl⁺_F(f′p^∞), every locally constant V-valued ε on G factors through some G_{f′p^n}, and ε ↦ L(1−k, ε) (Euler factors at the primes dividing f′p removed) is a V-valued distribution T_k on G, independent of the level used. For c ∈ G define Δ_c(1 − k, ε) := L(1 − k, ε) − N(c)^k L(1 − k, ε_c), with ε_c(g) := ε(cg) and N : G → ℤ_p^× the norm character.
hypotheses: F totally real; f′ divisible by every prime above p (so that the Euler factors at p are removed); ε locally constant.
proofSteps: Continuation of L(s, ε) for characters of G_f: AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.1/hecke-l-functional-equation; for a general function ε decompose into characters after extending coefficients.
Independence of the level: pulling ε back from G_{f′p^n} to G_{f′p^{n+1}} does not change L(s, ε) because the primes dividing p are already excluded.
ℚ-rationality of the values is siegel-klingen-rationality.
acceptance: F = ℚ, f′ = (p): T_k(ε) = −(1/k)·p^{n(k−1)}Σ_a ε(a)B_k(a/p^n) for ε of level p^n, the Bernoulli-polynomial formula of Deligne–Ribet (1.3)–(1.4).

sources.locator: §0, pp. 230–231; §8, (8.1) and the paragraph after it, pp. 277–278
sources.match: Deligne–Ribet define L(s, ε) for functions on G_f, recall Siegel’s rationality, extend values to V-valued functions, view ε ↦ L(1−k, ε) as a distribution on G and define Δ_c(1−k, ε).
For K = ℚ the values are given by Bernoulli polynomials, which serves as definition in any ℚ-vector space.

nodes.title: Cusps, normalised Fourier coefficients and nebentypus for Hilbert modular forms
nodes.statement: For F totally real with different d, narrow class representatives t_λ and an integral ideal n, put Γ_λ(n) = {(a b; c d) ∈ GL₂⁺(F) : a, d ∈ O_F, c ∈ t_λ d n, b ∈ (t_λ d)^{-1}, ad − bc ∈ O_F^×, d ≡ 1 mod n}; cusps(n) = ⊔_λ Γ_λ(n)\P¹(F). For a cusp [A] with A = (a b; c d) attached to λ put b_A = aO_F + c(t_λ d)^{-1} and c_A = (c)(t_λ d b_A)^{-1} (integral, depending only on [A]). The cusps above ∞ are C_∞(b, n) = {[A] : b | c_A} and those above 0 are C_0(b, n) = {[A] : gcd(b, c_A) = 1}; both sets are stable under the diamond operators S(m). The normalised Fourier coefficients of f at A are c_A(b, f) = a_A(b)(Nt_λ)^{-k/2}(Nb_A)^{-k}(N det A)^{k/2}, from the expansion f_λ|_k A(z) = a_A(0) + Σ_{b ∈ 𝔞, b ≫ 0} a_A(b)e_F(bz); at ∞ they are c_λ(0, f) and c(m, f) for m = (b)t_λ^{-1}. A form has nebentypus ψ if f|S(a) = ψ(a)f, and M_k(n) = ⊕_ψ M_k(n, ψ), S_k(n) = ⊕_ψ S_k(n, ψ).
hypotheses: F totally real; parallel weight k; n integral.
proofSteps: Γ_λ(n)\GL₂⁺(F)/B ≅ Γ_λ(n)\P¹(F) (DK (87)); b_A and c_A are independent of the matrix representing [A] (DK §7.2.3–7.2.5).
Stability under S(m): the diamond operators permute the Γ_λ(n) and preserve c_A up to the ideal action.
Nebentypus decomposition: S(m) for m prime to n factors through the finite group G_n⁺ acting semisimply over a field containing its character values.
acceptance: F = ℚ, t = 1: Γ(n) is Γ₁(n) (with d = ℤ), cusps above ∞ are those with denominator divisible by n, and c(m, f) are the usual q-expansion coefficients.
