nodes.title: Hilbert Eisenstein series G_{k,ε} and E_k(ψ, 1)
nodes.statement: Let k ≥ 1 and ε : I → ℂ a Schwartz function on the finite ideles with parity (−1)^k, supported on Â and defined modulo the conductor f. There is a Hilbert modular form G_{k,ε} ∈ M_k(Γ₀₀(f), ℂ) whose q-expansion at the cusp determined by α ∈ K̂^× is, for k > 1, N𝔞^k times the series with constant term 2^{-r}L(1−k, ε_c) and q^µ-coefficient (µ ≫ 0) the finite sum over ideals x ⊆ 𝔅𝔞² of ε_c(µx^{-1})N(µx^{-1})^{k−1}, with 𝔞 = (α) and c ∈ G the class defined by α (DR (2.23)), and for k = 1 the constant term is 2^{-r}(L(0, ε_c) + L(0, ε̃_c)) with ε̃ the modification of ε. In Dasgupta–Kakde’s normalisation, for k ≥ 1 odd and ψ a totally odd character of conductor dividing n, the S-stabilised Eisenstein series E_k(ψ_S, 1) ∈ M_k(n, Frac O, ψ) has c(m, E_k(ψ_S, 1)) = Σ_{r|m} ψ_S(m/r)Nr^{k−1}, eigenvalue ψ(l) + Nl^{k−1} for T_l (l ∤ n) and Nl^{k−1} for U_l (l | n), and, for k > 1, constant terms c_λ(0) = 0 at the cusps (1, λ) when the level n is not (1) and c_λ(0) = 2^{−[F:ℚ]}ψ^{-1}(λ)L(ψ^{-1}, 1 − k) when n = (1) (DK write n both for [F:ℚ] and for the level); for k = 1 they are 2^{−[F:ℚ]}L(ψ_S, 0) if n ≠ (1) and 2^{−[F:ℚ]}(L(ψ, 0) + ψ^{-1}(λ)L(ψ^{-1}, 0)) if n = (1) (DK (98)); the group-ring version E_k(ψ, 1) has coefficients Σ_{r|m,(m/r,n)=1}ψ(m/r)Nr^{k−1} in R.
hypotheses: F totally real of degree r (= n in DK); ε has parity (−1)^k; for DK’s version k ≥ 1 odd and ψ totally odd.
proofSteps: Construct G_{k,ε} as a function of lattices with polarisation and Γ₀₀(f)-structure by the Hecke–Siegel sum (DR (6.3)) Σ_{𝓜⊂𝓛′} Tε(𝓜 → K/𝔇^{-1})/(vol 𝓜)^k|vol 𝓜|^s at s = 0, continued analytically for k = 1, 2.
Compute its q-expansion at each cusp through the Fourier transform of ε (DR §3) — this is where the constant term L(1 − k, ε_c) appears.
DK’s E_k(ψ_S, 1) is the ψ-isotypic linear combination of such series, normalised as in DK §7.3; the Hecke eigenvalues follow from the coefficient formula.
The forms are geometric Hilbert modular forms in the sense of AutomorphicBundles:B5/hilbert-cusp-expansion, by the analytic–algebraic comparison there.
acceptance: F = ℚ, ψ = 1, k > 2 even (with the parity adjusted): E_k is the classical Eisenstein series with constant term ζ(1−k)/2, ModularForms layer 0.

nodes.title: Constant terms of Hilbert Eisenstein series at every cusp (Dasgupta–Kakde Proposition 8.4)
nodes.statement: Let ψ be a totally odd character, c its conductor with c₀ its part prime to the primes in P, m a divisor of t. The normalised constant terms c_A(0) of E_k(ψ_P, 1)|m ∈ M_k(n, ψ) are: for k > 1, zero unless [A] ∈ C_0(c, n), and at [A] ∈ C_0(c, n) equal to τ(ψ)/Nc₀^k · sgn(N(−c))ψ(c_A) · L(ψ^{-1}, 1−k)/2^{[F:ℚ]} · ∏_{𝔭|P}(1 − ψ(𝔭)/N𝔭^k) · ∏_{l∈J_m}Nl^{-k} · ∏_{l∈J_m^c}ψ^{-1}(l); for k = 1, the constant term vanishes outside C_0(c, n) ∪ C_∞(c₀, n), and on C_0(c, n) ∩ C_∞(c₀, n) (possible only when c₀ = 1), on C_∞(c₀, n) \ C_0(c, n) and on C_0(c, n) \ C_∞(c₀, n) it is given by the corresponding sums of the two terms involving L(ψ^{-1}, 0) and L(ψ, 0) (Dasgupta–Kakde eq. (100) and the three k = 1 formulas; Dasgupta–Kakde write 2^n with n = [F:ℚ], and use n also for the level). Here τ(ψ) is the Gauss sum of Dasgupta–Kakde’s Acta Arithmetica paper and J_m, J_m^c are the sets of Definition 8.3.
hypotheses: Notation of DK §8.1 (P a set of primes above p, t, J_m).
proofSteps: Dasgupta–Kakde Acta Arith. 200 (2021), Theorem 4.7, applied to E_k(ψ_P, 1)|m: compute the expansion at each cusp from the Fourier transform of the defining Schwartz function, using b_A and c_A.
Separate the cusps according to gcd(c, c_A) and c₀ | c_A (hilbert-cusp-combinatorics).
acceptance: k > 1 and the cusp ∞ when n = 1: recovers the constant term (1/2^n)ψ^{-1}(λ)L(ψ^{-1}, 1−k) of hilbert-eisenstein-series.

sources.locator: Proposition 8.4 and eq. (100), pp. 51–52; Definition 8.3, p. 51
sources.match: Dasgupta–Kakde state the normalised constant terms of E_k(ψ_P, 1)|m at every cusp, for k > 1 and the three k = 1 cases, citing Theorem 4.7 of their Acta Arithmetica paper for the proof and its Definition 4.1 for τ(ψ).

nodes.title: Siegel–Klingen rationality of L(1 − k, ε)
nodes.statement: If F is totally real and ε : G_f → ℚ, then L(1 − k, ε) ∈ ℚ for every integer k ≥ 1. Consequently L(1 − k, ε) ∈ V is well defined for ε with values in any ℚ-vector space V, and for ε with values in a number field E it lies in E and is Galois-equivariant: σ(L(1 − k, ε)) = L(1 − k, σ∘ε).
hypotheses: F totally real; ε ℚ-valued (or E-valued).
proofSteps: The constant term of G_{k,ε} at ∞ is 2^{-r}L(1 − k, ε) (hilbert-eisenstein-series), while every non-constant coefficient is a finite sum of values of ε times integer powers of norms, hence rational.

By the q-expansion principle over subrings (AutomorphicBundles:B5/hilbert-expansion-principle: rationality of all non-constant coefficients at one cusp forces the form to be defined over ℚ up to a constant), the constant term is rational as well (Deligne–Ribet: (8.1) follows from (0.1) and the Eisenstein computations).
Galois equivariance by applying σ to the q-expansion.

sources.locator: §8, (8.1) and the remark after it, p. 277; §0, p. 230 ((0.1), Rapoport)
sources.match: Deligne–Ribet state Siegel’s rationality theorem as (8.1) and remark that it follows from Rapoport’s q-expansion principle (0.1) in view of the Eisenstein series calculations.

nodes.title: p-adic Hilbert modular forms on the ordinary Igusa tower and p-adic q-expansions
nodes.statement: Let F be totally real, N ≥ 4 prime to p (Deligne–Ribet allow N ≥ 3; smaller N by descent from an auxiliary level), 𝒫 an invertible O_F-module with positivity and R a p-adic ring. V(Γ₀₀(N), R) is the ring of R-valued functions on the ordinary Igusa tower: compatible systems of functions on triples (X, λ, ε) of an ordinary Hilbert–Blumenthal abelian variety X/S (S a p-adically complete R-algebra), a 𝒫-polarisation λ and a trivialisation ε : O_F ⊗ µ_{p^∞} ≅ X[p^∞]° of the multiplicative part (equivalently the Igusa torsors of HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups:T5/igusa-torsor over the ordinary locus), together with the Γ₀₀(N)-structure. A p-adic cusp is a triple (𝔞, 𝔟, ε) with ε a trivialisation of the Tate object; the q-expansion of F ∈ V at it is F(𝔞, 𝔟, ε) ∈ R[[q^µ]]. For each k there is a map π_k : M_k(Γ₀₀(N), R) → V(Γ₀₀(N), R) (evaluating a form on (X, λ, ε) with the differential induced by ε) such that the q-expansion of π_kF at the p-adic cusp of α ∈ K̂^* is N α_p^{-k}F_α, with α_p the component of α at p. For R flat over ℤ_p, V(Γ₀₀(N), E) := V(Γ₀₀(N), R) ⊗ ℚ_p.
hypotheses: p unramified in F is not required for the definition; the ordinary locus is the invertibility locus of the Hasse invariant (HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves:H2/hilbert-hasse-ideal).
proofSteps: The ordinary locus and its Rapoport geometry: HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves:H2/ordinary-rapoport, H2/hilbert-hasse-ideal, over the Deligne–Pappas model H2/dp-integral-model.

The formal and mod-p^n ordinary Igusa tower of trivialisations O_F ⊗ µ_{p^n} ≅ X[p^n]° over the ordinary locus of the Deligne–Pappas model is requested from HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves:H2 (as RT-AREA-langlands-1/8 directs); its generic fibre is compared by Cartier duality with the tower of trivialisations of the dual canonical subgroup of HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups:T5/igusa-torsor (ε = 0).

Define V as functions on the tower compatible with base change; q-expansions at p-adic cusps are the p-adic limits of the algebraic q-expansions over the Noetherian rings O/p^n at the Tate object (AutomorphicBundles:B5/hilbert-cusp-expansion).
π_k and the formula for its q-expansion: DR (5.10)–(5.12), (5.15).
acceptance: F = ℚ: Katz’s ring V(N; R) of generalised p-adic modular functions (PadicFamilies:L0/katz-padic-modular-functions), with π_k the inclusion of weight-k forms and the factor α_p^{-k} the effect of changing the trivialisation.

sources.match: Deligne–Ribet define p-adic Hilbert modular forms as functions on the covering of the ordinary locus by trivialisations, p-adic cusps (𝔞, 𝔟, ε), the map π_k and the q-expansion formula N α_p^{-k}F_α at the p-adic cusp of α.
Katz develops p-adic Hilbert modular forms and their q-expansions at p-adic cusps in Chapter I (§1.9–1.11).

nodes.title: Geometric irreducibility of the Igusa covering (Deligne–Ribet (4.5))
nodes.statement: Let N ≥ 3 be prime to p, 𝒫 an invertible O_F-module with positivity, 𝓜° the ordinary locus of the reduction modulo p of the moduli space 𝓜_N[𝒫] of Hilbert–Blumenthal abelian varieties with 𝒫-polarisation and level N, and 𝓘 = 𝓘[𝒫, N, p^n] → 𝓜° the finite étale (O_F/p^n)^×-torsor of isomorphisms O_F ⊗ µ_{p^n} ≅ (X_{p^n})°. Then 𝓘 is geometrically irreducible over each geometric connected component of 𝓜°: for every algebraic closure F̄ of F_p, 𝓘 restricts to an irreducible covering of each connected component of 𝓜° ⊗ F̄.
hypotheses: N ≥ 3 prime to p; ordinary locus; p arbitrary.
proofSteps: Reduce to the surjectivity of the monodromy character ρ : π₁(𝓜°₁, m) → (O/p^nO)^* on each geometric connected component, after a finite extension F_q of F_p (DR p. 256); GL(2, O/NO) permutes the components, so the level-N structure can be handled by enlarging N.
At a closed point x over F_{q^b} the Frobenius endomorphism of the formal group of X_x is q^b·u with u ∈ (O ⊗ ℤ_p)^*, and ρ of the Frobenius element at x is the image of u in (O/p^nO)^* (DR p. 256).

It therefore suffices to produce, for each ū ∈ (O/p^nO)^*, an ordinary HBAV over some F_{q^b} with a level-N structure, Frobenius unit mapping to ū and prescribed polarisation module. DR construct it from Deligne’s equivalence between ordinary abelian varieties over a finite field and lattices with a Frobenius endomorphism (Deligne 1969, cited by DR as [4]; recorded gap: no layer of the atlas plans it): take the O-lattice of K[x]/(x² + cx + d) with Frobenius x, where d = q^b, c² − 4q^b is totally negative, c is a p-adic unit and N | (2 + c), N² | (1 + q^b + c); then u^{-1} ≡ −c mod q^b, and the polarisation module is corrected by an isogeny (DR p. 257).

Choosing c by approximation realises every ū, so ρ is surjective on every component and the covering is geometrically irreducible. Chebotarev density enters DR’s text only as a heuristic for why the theorem should hold, not as an input.
acceptance: F = ℚ: Igusa’s theorem that the Igusa curve over the ordinary locus of X(N)_{F_p} is irreducible.

sources.match: Deligne–Ribet prove that the covering 𝓘[𝒫, N, p^n] of 𝓜°[𝒫, p] is geometrically irreducible, reducing to surjectivity of the monodromy character, computing it at Frobenius elements of ordinary points and constructing the needed ordinary points through Deligne’s description of ordinary abelian varieties over finite fields (p. 257).

nodes.title: The p-adic q-expansion principle (Deligne–Ribet (5.13), (5.14), (0.2), (0.3))
nodes.statement: Let F ∈ V(Γ₀₀(N), E) with E = R ⊗ ℚ_p, R a flat ℤ_p-module, and (𝔞, 𝔟, ε) a p-adic cusp. Then the q-expansion F(𝔞, 𝔟, ε), a priori in E[[q^µ]], has coefficients in R if and only if F ∈ V(Γ₀₀(N), R). Consequently (5.14): if F has one cusp at which every non-constant coefficient lies in R, then the difference between the constant terms of its q-expansions at any two cusps lies in R. For forms F_k of weight k ≥ 0 (all but finitely many zero) with rational q-expansion coefficients, if S(α) = Σ_k N α_p^{-k}F_{k,α} has coefficients in ℤ_p for one α, it has them for all α (0.2); and if its non-constant coefficients are in ℤ_p for one α, the same holds for all β and the constant terms differ by elements of ℤ_p (0.3).
hypotheses: R flat over ℤ_p; the cusps range over all p-adic cusps of Γ₀₀(N).
proofSteps: Irreducibility of the Igusa tower on each component (igusa-irreducibility) and the formal-local q-expansion at one cusp of each component determine F modulo p^m on that component (reduce modulo p^m: a function on an irreducible scheme vanishing on the formal neighbourhood of a cusp vanishes).
Components are reached by the cusps (𝔞, 𝔟, ε) as α varies, through the action of the idele class group.
(5.14): apply (5.13) to F − t with t the constant term at the given cusp, viewed as a weight-0 form.
(0.2)–(0.3) are the special cases with F = Σπ_kF_k, using π_k’s q-expansion formula.
acceptance: F = ℚ: Katz’s p-adic q-expansion principle for V(N; R) (PadicFamilies:L0/katz-padic-modular-functions).
(0.3) applied to Eisenstein series gives the Kummer congruences over ℚ.

sources.match: Deligne–Ribet prove the p-adic q-expansion principle (5.13), its corollary on constant terms (5.14), and deduce the integrality statements (0.2) and (0.3).

nodes.title: The Deligne–Ribet measures and Eisenstein congruences ((0.4), (0.5), (8.2), (8.4), (8.11))
nodes.statement: Let F be totally real of degree r, f′ divisible by every prime above p, G = Cl⁺_F(f′p^∞) and c ∈ G. (Main theorem (8.2)) µ_c : ε ↦ Δ_c(0, ε) is a measure on I (equivalently on G) with values in Ẑ, and for every Schwartz function ε and k ≥ 1, ∫ε·N^{k−1}dµ_c = Δ_c(1 − k, ε); in particular µ_{c,k} := (ε ↦ Δ_c(1 − k, ε)) is a ℤ_p-valued measure with µ_{c,k} = N^{k−1}µ_{c,1} (0.5). (Integrality (0.4)) If ε₁, ε₂, … are ℚ_p-valued locally constant functions on G, finitely many nonzero, with Σ_k ε_k(𝔵)N𝔵^{k−1} ∈ ℤ_p for every prime-to-f′p ideal 𝔵, then Σ_k Δ_c(1 − k, ε_k) ∈ ℤ_p. (Eisenstein congruences (8.4)) the same for ℚ-valued Schwartz ε_k of parity (−1)^k with Σε_kN^{k−1} ℤ̂-valued. (2-adic refinement (8.11)) for φ : I → ℤ̂ odd, continuous, compactly supported, ∫φdµ_c ∈ 2^{r−1}ℤ̂, and in 2^rℤ̂ unless F is exceptional and δ(φ) = 1.
hypotheses: F totally real, f′ divisible by every prime above p; c ∈ G arbitrary (for p odd one may take c with N(c) of order p − 1).
proofSteps: For each k form G_{k,ε_k} (hilbert-eisenstein-series) and the p-adic form Σ_kπ_kG_{k,ε_k}; its non-constant q-expansion coefficients at the cusp of α are Σ_kε_k(…)N(…)^{k−1}·α_p-power, integral by hypothesis.

By padic-q-expansion-principle (5.14), the constant terms at two cusps differ by an element of ℤ_p; the two constant terms are 2^{-r}Σ_kL(1−k, ε_k) and 2^{-r}Σ_kN(c)^kL(1−k, ε_{k,c}), giving Δ_c ∈ 2^{-r}ℤ_p, and the extra powers of 2 are recovered by the parity argument (8.3), (8.8)–(8.10).
The measure statement: integrality of Δ_c(0, ε) for ℤ̂-valued ε is (0.4) with k = 1; the moment formula is (8.4) applied to εN^{k−1} ≡ εη^{k−1} mod m with η odd and ≡ N mod m.
(8.11): compare φ with an odd Schwartz function congruent modulo 2^r and use (8.8)–(8.10).
acceptance: F = ℚ: µ_c is the classical regularised Bernoulli (Mazur) measure, (0.4) the Kummer congruences.

sources.match: Deligne–Ribet state the integrality theorem (0.4), the measure µ_{c,k} = N^{k−1}µ_{c,1} (0.5), the main theorem (8.2) that µ_c is a ℤ̂-valued measure with moments Δ_c(1 − k, ε), the Eisenstein congruences (8.4) and the 2-adic statement (8.11).
Dasgupta–Kakde quote the integrality Θ_{S,T} ∈ ℤ[G] of Deligne–Ribet and Cassou-Noguès under the smoothing condition (1).

nodes.title: The Deligne–Ribet pseudo-measure and p-adic L-functions of totally real fields
nodes.statement: With λ_c := N^{-1}µ_{c,1}, viewed in the ring Λ_G of ℤ_p-valued measures on G (the completed group ring), and c chosen so that 1 − c is not a zero divisor, λ := λ_c/(1 − c) in the total quotient ring of Λ_G is independent of c ((1 − c′)λ_c = (1 − c)λ_{c′}) and is a pseudo-measure: (1 − g)λ ∈ Λ_G for every g ∈ G. For k ≥ 1 and ε locally constant, ∫εN^k dλ = L(1 − k, ε). For a finite-order character ψ of G and the decomposition G = Δ × Γ (Γ ≅ ℤ_p^{1+δ}; ≅ ℤ_p under Leopoldt), for a finite-order character χ of G the p-adic L-function L_p(χω, s) := ∫χω⟨N⟩^{1−s}dλ (⟨N⟩ = Nω^{-1}) is meromorphic in s ∈ ℤ_p, analytic unless χ = ω^{-1}, and satisfies L_p(χω, n) = L*(χω^n, n) for every integer n ≤ 0 (k = 1 − n in the moment formula). On the cyclotomic quotient it is a quotient G_ψ(u^s − 1)/H_ψ(u^s − 1) with G_ψ ∈ O_ψ[[T]] and H_ψ = 1 unless ψ factors through the cyclotomic ℤ_p-extension, in which case H_ψ is the linear polynomial clearing the pole at the trivial character.
hypotheses: F totally real; G = Cl⁺_F(f′p^∞) with f′ divisible by the primes above p; ω the Teichmüller character; u = N(γ) for a generator γ of the cyclotomic part.
proofSteps: Pseudo-measure: (1 − c′)λ_c = (1 − c)λ_{c′} follows from the defining formula of Δ_c; then use PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L3/pseudomeasures and L3/independence-of-clearing-factor.
Moments: ∫εN^kdλ_c = Δ_c(1−k, ε) = L(1−k, ε) − N(c)^kL(1−k, ε_c), and dividing by (1 − c) gives L(1 − k, ε) (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L3/admissible-evaluation).

The cyclotomic specialisation and the power-series form: push forward along G → Gal(F(µ_{p^∞})/F) and use the Iwasawa algebra ℤ_p[[Γ]] ≅ ℤ_p[[T]] (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L1); the denominator comes from clearing the pole of λ at the trivial character only.
acceptance: F = ℚ: λ is the Kubota–Leopoldt pseudo-measure; L_p(ω, s) has a simple pole at s = 1.
For χ totally odd, L_p(χω, 0) = L*(χ, 0) = L(χ, 0)∏_{𝔭|p}(1 − χ(𝔭)) (DKV).

sources.match: Deligne–Ribet define λ_c = N^{-1}µ_{c,1} in Λ_G, the pseudo-measure λ = λ_c/(1 − c), independent of c, whose integral against εN^k is L(1 − k, ε), and obtain the p-adic L-functions by integrating characters.
Dasgupta–Kakde–Ventullo characterise L_p(χω, s) by L_p(χω, n) = L*(χω^n, n) for n ≤ 0, analytic unless χ = ω^{-1}, crediting Deligne–Ribet, Cassou-Noguès and Barsky.

nodes.title: The rational case: Deligne–Ribet against Kubota–Leopoldt
nodes.statement: For F = ℚ and f′ = N p with p ∤ N, the Deligne–Ribet pseudo-measure on Cl⁺_ℚ(Np^∞) = (ℤ/N)^× × ℤ_p^× equals the arithmetic Kubota–Leopoldt pseudo-measure of DirichletPadicLFunctions:L1/arithmetic-pseudomeasure and its tame-character components DirichletPadicLFunctions:L2, under the identification of the class of the ideal (a) with a (and of a unit u at p with u^{-1}, ray-class-tower) and with identical normalisations: same smoothing (the class c ↔ the smoothing parameter), same Euler factors removed at p and at N, and same character conventions (primitive values computed at the primitive conductor, DirichletPadicLFunctions:L2/primitive-integral-interpolation).
hypotheses: F = ℚ; the identification of Cl⁺_ℚ(Np^∞) is the one fixed in ray-class-tower.
proofSteps: Both pseudo-measures are characterised by their moments against εN^k for k ≥ 1 (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L3/actual-pseudomoment-separation), and both moments are L(1 − k, ε) with the Euler factors at Np removed (deligne-ribet-pseudomeasure; DirichletPadicLFunctions:L1/arithmetic-positive-interpolation).
Match the regular smoothing parameter of DirichletPadicLFunctions L1 with the class c, and track the inversion between ideal and idelic coordinates.

Dasgupta–Kakde–Ventullo characterise L_p(χω, s) by L_p(χω, n) = L*(χω^n, n) for n ≤ 0; taking F = ℚ in this characterisation gives the Kubota–Leopoldt interpolation (our specialisation, not stated there).

nodes.title: p-ordinary CM types and polarisation data
nodes.statement: Let M be a CM field with maximal totally real subfield F, and Σ a CM type of M (ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocity:CM.0/cm-type), i.e. Σ ⊔ cΣ = Hom(M, ℂ). Fix ι_∞ and ι_p. Σ is p-ordinary if the p-adic places Σ_p of M induced by ι_p∘ι_∞^{-1}∘σ (σ ∈ Σ) and their conjugates Σ_p^c partition the places of M above p; this forces every prime of F above p to split in M. The polarisation data is δ ∈ M with δ^c = −δ and Im σ(δ) > 0 for σ ∈ Σ, such that the alternating form ⟨x, y⟩ = Tr_{M/F}(x^c y/(2δ)) identifies O_M ∧ O_M with c^{-1}d^{-1} for an ideal c (Katz’s c, Hsieh’s polarisation ideal c(O_M) = D_F^{-1}(2δD_{M/F})) prime to p.
hypotheses: M a CM field (Mathlib NumberField.IsCMField); p a prime; embeddings fixed.
proofSteps: Σ is a CM type of the CM algebra M (CM.0/cm-type); p-ordinarity is a condition on the induced p-adic places.
If Σ is p-ordinary, each prime of F above p splits, since its two places in M are distinguished by Σ_p and Σ_p^c.
Existence of δ with c prime to p: choose δ by weak approximation (Katz (5.3.3), Hsieh p. 711).
acceptance: M imaginary quadratic: Σ = {σ} is p-ordinary iff p splits in M.
M = F·K with K imaginary quadratic and p split in K: the CM type induced from K is p-ordinary.

nodes.title: CM points of Hilbert modular varieties and their p-adic trivialisations
nodes.statement: For a fractional ideal 𝔞 of M prime to p, the complex torus ℂ^Σ/Σ(𝔞) with the polarisation given by δ and level structure defines an HBAV x(𝔞) with CM by O_M over a number field, with good reduction at p (ShimuraVarieties:V5/cm-potential-good-reduction after a finite extension). When Σ is p-ordinary its reduction is ordinary, and over W = Ŵ(F̄_p) (or the ring of integers of a p-adic field) the decomposition O_M ⊗ ℤ_p = O_{Σ_p} × O_{Σ_p^c} gives a canonical trivialisation of the multiplicative part X[p^∞]° ≅ O_F ⊗ µ_{p^∞}, so x(𝔞) defines a point of the Igusa tower over W: the p-adic CM point. The Galois action on CM points is given by the main theorem of complex multiplication (Shimura reciprocity), and the ideles of M act on the set of CM points through the reciprocity map.
hypotheses: Σ p-ordinary; 𝔞 prime to p and to the level.
proofSteps: The CM abelian variety and its complex uniformisation: ShimuraVarieties:V5/cm-abelian-variety and V5/cm-number-field-model, viewed as a point of the Hilbert PEL moduli space (HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves:H1/hilbert-pel-instance).
Ordinary reduction from p-ordinarity: the p-divisible group splits according to O_{Σ_p} × O_{Σ_p^c}, the first factor being multiplicative.
Trivialisation: the Σ_p-part identifies with O_F ⊗ µ_{p^∞} after choosing generators, giving a W-point of the formal ordinary Igusa tower (requested from HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves:H2).
Shimura reciprocity for the Galois action: ShimuraVarieties:V5/main-cm.
acceptance: M imaginary quadratic, F = ℚ: Heegner/CM points x(𝔞) on the modular curve, with Serre–Tate canonical trivialisation at a split p (HeegnerPointEulerSystems:HE.1 for the classical CM points).

nodes.title: Complex and p-adic CM periods (Ω_∞, Ω_p)
nodes.statement: Let A/O (O the ring of integers of a number field containing the reflex field, localised at p) be an abelian variety with CM by O_M of type Σ and good ordinary reduction, with a nowhere-vanishing invariant differential ω(O_M) on A over O ⊗ D_p. The complex period Ω_∞ = (Ω_{∞,σ})_{σ∈Σ} ∈ (ℂ^×)^Σ compares ω(O_M) with the differential coming from the complex uniformisation (ω_trans), and the p-adic period Ω_p = (Ω_{p,σ}) ∈ (W^×)^Σ compares it with the differential ω_can coming from the canonical trivialisation of the formal group: ω(O_M) = Ω_∞·ω_trans = Ω_p·ω_can. Replacing ω(O_M) by λω(O_M), λ ∈ (O ⊗ D_p)^×, replaces (Ω_∞, Ω_p) by (λΩ_∞, λΩ_p), so the ratio Ω_∞/Ω_p (under ι_∞, ι_p) is canonical; Hsieh writes Ω_K = (2πi)^{-1}Ω_∞. For an elliptic curve with CM by O_K at a split prime these are the classical Ω_∞ and the Serre–Tate period Ω_p ∈ W^×.
hypotheses: Σ p-ordinary; the differential is nowhere vanishing over the integral base.
proofSteps: Existence of ω(O_M): the Lie algebra is free of rank one over O_M ⊗ O after a finite extension.
Ω_∞: compare with the complex uniformisation of cm-points-and-canonical-trivialisations; Ω_p: compare with the canonical trivialisation of the multiplicative formal group.
Dependence on the differential is the scaling rule (Katz remark after (5.3.7)).
acceptance: M = ℚ(i), p ≡ 1 mod 4: Ω_∞ is a nonzero algebraic multiple of Γ(1/4)²/√(2π) (the lemniscate period), and Ω_p a p-adic unit.

sources.locator: Theorem (5.3.0), the choice of ω(𝒪_L) and of Ω ∈ (K ⊗ ℂ)^×, c ∈ (𝒪 ⊗ D_p)^× by (5.1.46)–(5.1.48), p. 274; remark after (5.3.7), p. 275

nodes.title: Maass–Shimura and Katz p-adic differential operators on Hilbert modular forms
nodes.statement: For d = Σ_σ d(σ)σ ∈ ℤ[Σ] with all d(σ) ≥ 0 there are: (i) C^∞ operators ϑ(d, C^∞) on C^∞ Hilbert modular forms, built from the Gauss–Manin connection and the Kodaira–Spencer isomorphism with the antiholomorphic (Hodge) splitting, taking weight χ to χ + 2d (Maass–Shimura δ^m_k in Hida–Tilouine’s notation); (ii) p-adic operators ϑ(d, p-adic) = ∏_σ ϑ(σ, p-adic)^{d(σ)} on p-adic Hilbert modular forms, built with the unit-root splitting instead (Katz (2.5.7)), which mutually commute, act as derivations of degree two on the graded ring of p-adic forms, and take ω(χ)(p-adic) to ω(χ + 2d)(p-adic) (Katz (2.5.8)–(2.5.12)). On q-expansions at a p-adic cusp, θ(σ) multiplies the coefficient of q^β by σ(β) (θ^m multiplies by β^m), Katz Corollary (2.6.25)–(2.6.27).
hypotheses: F totally real; R₁ an O^{gal}[1/d_K]-algebra separated for the p-adic topology for (ii).
proofSteps: Define ϑ(σ, C^∞) as in Katz (2.3.3)–(2.3.7) with the Hodge splitting, and ϑ(σ, p-adic) by replacing it with the unit-root splitting of H¹_dR over the Igusa tower (Katz (2.5.1)–(2.5.7)).
Commutation, Leibniz rule and weight change: Katz (2.5.8)–(2.5.12), as in the C^∞ case (2.3.8).
q-expansion formula from the Tate object, where the unit-root splitting is the canonical one.
acceptance: F = ℚ: ϑ(p-adic) is Serre’s θ = q d/dq on p-adic modular forms and ϑ(C^∞) is the Maass–Shimura operator δ_k = (1/2πi)(d/dz + k/(2iy)).

nodes.title: Algebraicity and p-adic comparison of CM values of derivatives (Katz (2.4.5), (2.6.7))
nodes.statement: Let R ⊂ ℂ be an O^{gal}[1/d_K]-algebra, x = (X, λ, i) an R-valued point of the moduli space of HBAVs with a nowhere-vanishing differential ω whose Hodge filtration has an R-rational splitting Split(x) that becomes the antiholomorphic subspace over ℂ (as for CM points). For f ∈ M(c, Γ₀₀(N), χ; R) and d ≥ 0, (ϑ(d, C^∞)f)(X, λ, ω, i) lies in R (Katz (2.4.5)). If in addition R ↪ R₀ (p-adic completion) and Split(x) ⊗ R₀ is the unit-root subspace (as for CM points of a p-ordinary type), then (ϑ(d, p-adic)f(p-adic))(X, λ, ω, i)_{R₀} lies in R₁[1/d_K] and equals ϑ(d, x, ω, Split(x))f (Katz (2.6.7)–(2.6.8)). For CM points with the periods of cm-periods: θ^m f(x(𝔞))/Ω_p^{k+2m} = δ^m f(x(𝔞))/Ω_K^{k+2m} (Katz (2.4.6), (2.6.8), (2.6.33), as used by Hsieh).
hypotheses: The splitting condition (2.4.2) at x, and (2.6.3) for the p-adic statement; d(σ) ≥ 0.
proofSteps: The C^∞ derivative at x is computed algebraically from the Gauss–Manin connection and the splitting, so it lies in R when the splitting is R-rational (Katz (2.4.5), essentially Shimura’s generalisation of Damerell).
The p-adic operator uses the unit-root splitting; when the two splittings coincide at x the two computations agree (Katz (2.6.7)–(2.6.8)).
At CM points of a p-ordinary type the Hodge splitting by CM is rational and coincides p-adically with the unit-root splitting; translate the differential by the periods.
acceptance: F = ℚ, M imaginary quadratic: Shimura–Katz algebraicity of δ_k^r f at CM points and its equality with θ^r f there after dividing by Ω_∞ and Ω_p.

sources.match: Katz proves that C^∞ derivatives at points with a rational splitting of the Hodge filtration are rational, and that the p-adic derivative at points where that splitting is the unit-root one gives the same number.
Hsieh uses Katz (2.4.6), (2.6.8), (2.6.33) to identify θ^m f at CM points divided by Ω_p^{k+2m} with δ^m f divided by Ω_K^{k+2m}.

nodes.title: Katz’s Eisenstein measure
nodes.statement: For a fractional ideal c of F prime to p, the inverse constructions H(x, y) = N(x)^{-1}F(1/x, y), F(x, y) = N(x)^{-1}H(1/x, y) (Katz (4.2.1)) identify continuous functions F on (O_F ⊗ ℤ_p)^× × (O_F ⊗ ℤ_p)^× with F(e^{-1}x, ey) = N(e)F(x, y) for e ∈ E and continuous functions H on G := (O_F ⊗ ℤ_p)^× × (O_F ⊗ ℤ_p)^×/closure of E (diagonal). The Eisenstein measure µ_c is the V(c, ℤ_p)-valued measure on G with ∫H dµ_c = G_{1,F}, the p-adic Eisenstein series of weight one attached to F (Katz §3.4), so that integrating N(x)^k-type characters gives the p-adic avatars of the Eisenstein series G_{k,F} of Katz §3.2 (Hilbert Eisenstein series with partial Fourier transforms). It interpolates the q-expansions of these Eisenstein series as p-adic Hilbert modular forms.
hypotheses: F totally real; c prime to p; values in p-adic Hilbert modular forms V(c, ℤ_p).
proofSteps: Construct the Eisenstein series G_{k,F} for functions F of the above type (Katz §3.1–3.3), with their q-expansions; take their p-adic versions (§3.4).

Verify the abstract Kummer congruences for the family of q-expansions (Katz §4.0, (4.0.6)–(4.0.8)) using the explicit coefficients; then the measure exists by Katz’s criterion (4.1) and the p-adic q-expansion principle.
acceptance: F = ℚ: the Eisenstein measure on ℤ_p^× × ℤ_p^× whose moments are the p-depleted Eisenstein series E_k(φ₁, φ₂); compare DirichletPadicLFunctions:L4.

nodes.title: Katz’s p-adic L-function for CM fields (Theorem (5.3.0))
nodes.statement: Let M be a CM field with p-ordinary CM type Σ, δ as in cm-type-p-ordinary, and ω(O_M), Ω ∈ (F ⊗ ℂ)^×, c ∈ (O ⊗ D_p)^× the periods of cm-periods (Katz writes K for the totally real field F and L for M). There is a D_p-valued p-adic measure µ on Gal(M(p^∞)/M) (M(p^∞) the maximal abelian extension unramified outside p) such that for every A₀-Grössencharacter χ of M of conductor dividing p^∞ and infinity type −kΣ_σσ − Σ_σd(σ)(σ − σ̄) with k ≥ 1 and all d(σ) ≥ 0: (A) L_µ(χ_p)/∏_σc(σ)^{k+2d(σ)} lies in incl(p)(ℚ̄); (B) Local(χ, Σ, δ)·[O_M^×:O_F^×]·∏_𝔓((1 − χ̌(𝔓̄))(1 − χ(𝔓̄))) (χ̌ the dual character of (5.3.7), χ̌(𝔄) = 1/(χ(𝔄̄)N(𝔄)), so χ̌(𝔓̄) = 1/(χ(𝔓)N(𝔓)))·(−1)^{kg}(π)^{Σd(σ)}∏_σΓ(k + d(σ))/(√d_F∏_σIm(σ(δ))^{d(σ)}∏_σΩ(σ)^{k+2d(σ)})·L_∞(χ) lies in incl(∞)(ℚ̄); and (A) = (B) under incl(p)^{-1} and incl(∞)^{-1}. Here L_µ(χ_p) = ∫χ_pdµ, the product is over the primes 𝔓 of Σ_p, and Local(χ, Σ, δ) is Katz’s local term at p (§5.2).
hypotheses: (ord): Σ p-ordinary; conductor of χ dividing p^∞ (tame conductor 1); the critical range k ≥ 1, d(σ) ≥ 0.
Not asserted for nonordinary primes or outside this infinity-type range.
proofSteps: Identify Gal(M(p^∞)/M(1)) with (O_M ⊗ ℤ_p)^× modulo the closure of E(M) (Katz (5.4.2)–(5.4.6), ray-class-unit-sequence).

Pull back the Eisenstein measure of the maximal totally real subfield along the CM points (cm-points-and-canonical-trivialisations), after applying θ^d (katz-differential-operators), and sum over ideal classes (Katz §5.4).

Evaluate moments: the C^∞ value at CM points of δ^d of the Eisenstein series is the Hecke L-value L_∞(χ) times explicit factors (Katz §5.5, the explicit formulas), and katz-cm-algebraicity transfers it to the p-adic side.
The local term and Euler factors at Σ_p come from the p-depletion of the Eisenstein series (Katz §5.2, formula (5.2.30)).
acceptance: M imaginary quadratic, p split: the two-variable Katz p-adic L-function of M, interpolating L(χ, 0) at characters of infinity type (−k − d, d).

sources.match: Katz states the existence of the D_p-valued measure on Gal(L(p^∞)/L) with the interpolation (A) = (B) at A₀-grossencharacters of conductor dividing p^∞ and the stated infinity types, and constructs it from the Eisenstein measure.

nodes.title: The functional equation of Katz’s p-adic L-function ((5.3.7))
nodes.statement: For every continuous ρ : Gal(M(p^∞)/M) → D_p^×, with ρ̌ defined by ρ̌(𝔄) = 1/(ρ(𝔄̄)N_{M/ℚ}(𝔄)), L_µ(ρ̌) = N_{F/ℚ}(c)·ρ(c)·L_µ(ρ). The constants Ω and c and the measure depend on the choice of ω(O_M) only through simultaneous rescaling (λΩ, λc), which does not affect (5.3.5).
hypotheses: As in katz-padic-l-function.
proofSteps: Both sides are measures in ρ; compare at a dense set of characters through (A) = (B) and the complex functional equation of Hecke L-functions (AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.1/hecke-l-functional-equation); Katz §5.6.
acceptance: M imaginary quadratic: L_µ(ρ̌) = N(c)ρ(c)L_µ(ρ), the symmetry exchanging the two variables.

sources.locator: (5.3.7) and the following remark, p. 275; table of contents §5.6, p. 200
sources.match: Katz states the functional equation L_µ(ρ̌) = N_{K/ℚ}(c)ρ(c)L_µ(ρ) and the effect of rescaling the differential, proved in §5.6.

nodes.title: The Katz–Hida–Tilouine measure with tame conductor
nodes.statement: Fix an O_M-ideal C prime to p, decomposed C = 𝔉𝔉^c𝔍 with 𝔉𝔉^c split and 𝔍 inert or ramified over F, and δ satisfying (d1)–(d2) with c prime to pCC^c. There is a unique measure φ on the ray class group Z(C) of M modulo Cp^∞ such that for every Hecke character λ modulo Cp^∞ whose conductor is divisible by every prime factor of 𝔉 and whose infinity type is kΣ + κ(1 − c) with κ = Σκ_σσ and either k > 0, κ ≥ 0 or k ≤ 1, κ ≥ 1 − k: ∫λ̂ dφ/Ω_p^{kΣ+2κ} = (O^×:O_F^×)W_p(λ)·(−1)^{kΣ}π^κΓ_Σ(kΣ + κ)/(√|D_F|·Im(δ)^κ·Ω_∞^{kΣ+2κ})·∏_{𝔏|C}(1 − λ(𝔏))·∏_{𝔓∈Σ_p}(1 − λ(𝔓^c))(1 − λ*(𝔓^c))·L(0, λ), with W_p(λ) the root number at Σ_p of (1.2), λ*(x) = λ(x^c)^{-1}|x|_{A_M} the dual character, λ(𝔏) = 0 for 𝔏 dividing the conductor of λ, and L the primitive L-function. It satisfies a functional equation relating φ on Z(C) and φ^c on Z(C^c) with the factor N(c^{-1})W′(λ). For C = 1 it is Katz’s measure.
hypotheses: Σ p-ordinary; C prime to p; the hypotheses (i)–(ii) on λ.
proofSteps: Hida–Tilouine extend Katz’s construction to tame level C by the same Eisenstein-measure method with a level-C Eisenstein series and partial Fourier transforms at 𝔉 (Hida–Tilouine 1993, as restated in Hida 2010, (1.3)).
Uniqueness: the interpolated characters, times finite-order characters, are dense (Hida 2010, p. 45).
acceptance: C = 1: Katz’s theorem (5.3.0) in Hida’s normalisation.
M imaginary quadratic: the Katz measure with tame conductor used by Castella–Grossi–Lee–Skinner (Theorem 2.1.2).

sources.match: Hida restates the measure φ on Z(C) constructed with Tilouine (following Katz for C = 1), characterised by the interpolation formula (1.3), and its functional equation.
Castella–Grossi–Lee–Skinner use the Katz p-adic L-function as extended by Hida–Tilouine, with its interpolation property.

nodes.title: Group-ring valued Hilbert Eisenstein families (Dasgupta–Kakde §§7.2.8, 8.1–8.4)
nodes.statement: Let H/F be a finite abelian CM extension of conductor dividing n with Galois group G, R a quotient of O[G] by a product of character ideals (DK §7.1), Ψ the characters of R and 𝛙 : G_n⁺ → R^× the canonical character. (i) A family (f_ψ)_{ψ∈Ψ}, f_ψ ∈ M_k(n, O, ψ), whose Fourier coefficients c(m, f_ψ) = ψ(c(m)) and constant terms c_λ(0, f_ψ) = ψ(c_λ(0)) come from elements c(m), c_λ(0) ∈ R, glues to a unique group-ring form f ∈ M_k(n, R, 𝛙) (Lemma 7.2, via Silliman’s characterisation of M_k(n, R)). (ii) The group-ring Eisenstein series E_k(𝛙, 1) has coefficients c(m) = Σ_{r|m, (m/r, n) = 1}𝛙(m/r)Nr^{k−1} ∈ R, and the modified series W_k(𝛙, 1) (specialising to W_k(ψ_P, 1) of DK Definition 8.2 for every ψ) has all non-constant coefficients in R for every odd k ≥ 1 (Proposition 8.14). (iii) For k ≡ 1 mod (p−1)p^N the ordinary projector satisfies e^ord_p W_k(𝛙, 1) = z·W_k(𝛙, 1_p) with z = ∏_{𝔭|p}𝛙(𝔭)/(𝛙(𝔭) − N𝔭^{k−1}) ≡ 1 mod p^m for N large (DK proof of Corollary 8.19). (iv) For such k, Θ_{S_∞}(1−k)/Θ_{S_∞}(0) lies in R and is ≡ ∏_{𝔭|p}(1 − χ(𝔭)^{-1}) mod m_R (Lemma 8.16), a consequence of the p-adic continuity of the depleted values supplied by the Deligne–Ribet pseudo-measure.
hypotheses: Notation of DK §§7–8: n, P, R, Ψ, 𝛙; case 1 (gcd(n, p) = 1) for (iii)–(iv) as in DK.
proofSteps: (i) Silliman’s Corollary 7.28 and Remark 7.29 (as quoted by DK) identify M_k(n, R) inside M_k(n, ∏_ψO) by integrality of coefficients; the q-expansion principle (AutomorphicBundles:B5/hilbert-expansion-principle) gives uniqueness.
(ii) Write W_k(𝛙, 1) as an R-linear combination of level-raised E_k(𝛙_m, 1) (DK proof of Proposition 8.14) and check integrality coefficientwise.
(iii) U_𝔭 acts on E_k(ψ, 1) through the Hecke eigenvalues of hilbert-eisenstein-series; the ordinary projector picks the 𝛙(𝔭)-eigencomponent.
(iv) Kummer-type congruence Θ(1 − k) ≡ Θ(0) from deligne-ribet-pseudomeasure.
acceptance: H = F (trivial G): R = O and the family is a single Eisenstein series.

sources.locator: §7.2.8 and Lemma 7.2, pp. 47–48; §7.3 eqs. (98)–(99), p. 49; Definition 8.2, p. 51; Proposition 8.14, p. 57; Lemma 8.16, p. 59; proof of Corollary 8.19, p. 61
sources.match: Dasgupta–Kakde glue character-wise forms into group-ring forms, define the group-ring Eisenstein series and the modified series W_k(𝛙, 1) with integral non-constant coefficients, compute the ordinary projector on them, and prove the congruence for Θ(1 − k)/Θ(0).

uses.how: DK §8.2–8.5 build the cusp forms F_k(𝛙) congruent to Eisenstein series from these families (Propositions 8.11–8.12, Corollary 8.19)

nodes.title: Hsieh’s anticyclotomic Rankin–Selberg setting
nodes.statement: Let F be totally real of degree d, M/F a CM extension (Hsieh’s K), π an irreducible cuspidal automorphic representation of GL₂(A_F) with unitary central character ω and infinity type k = Σk_σσ ∈ ℤ_{>0}[Σ] (discrete series or limit of discrete series of weight k_σ), π_M its base change, and λ a unitary Hecke character of M with λ|_{A_F^×} = ω^{-1} and infinity type (k/2, −k/2), so that π_M ⊗ λ is conjugate self-dual. Write n = n⁺n⁻ for the conductor of π (n⁺ divisible only by primes split in M, n⁻ by inert or ramified ones), ε*(π_{M,v}, λ_v) := ε(1/2, π_{M,v} ⊗ λ_v, ψ_v)ω_v(−1) the normalised local root number, Γ⁻ = Gal(M⁻_{p^∞}/M) the Galois group of the maximal anticyclotomic ℤ_p^{[F:ℚ]}-extension, Λ = ℤ_p[[Γ⁻]], and X_p^crit the locally algebraic p-adic characters of Γ⁻ of weight (m, −m), m ∈ ℤ_{≥0}[Σ] (avatars, through Hsieh’s geometrically normalised reciprocity). The hypotheses are: (ord) the CM type Σ is p-ordinary; Hypothesis A: ε*(π_{M,v}, λ_v) = +1 for every v | n⁻; (sf) n⁻ is squarefree; p odd. The p-adic multiplier is e_{Σ_p}(π, χ) = ∏_{𝔓∈Σ_p, 𝔭=𝔓𝔓̄} ε(1/2, π_𝔭 ⊗ χ_𝔓, ψ_𝔭)L(1/2, π_𝔭 ⊗ χ_𝔓)^{-2}χ_𝔓^{-2}(−2δ). Ordinarity of Σ says nothing about ordinarity of π.
hypotheses: The hypotheses are data of the setting, not consequences; each theorem lists those it uses.
proofSteps: π_M is Jacquet’s base change (GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer, quadratic base change), cuspidal unless π is induced from M.
Root numbers: local ε-factors of AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors and GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer:R16.3/conductor-epsilon-comparison.
Γ⁻ and its critical characters: the anticyclotomic quotient of the ray-class limit of M (L0/evaluation-norm-twist-maps), avatars by L0/hecke-character-avatar in Hsieh’s geometric normalisation.
acceptance: n⁻ = (1) satisfies Hypothesis A and (sf) vacuously.
F = ℚ, π attached to a newform of weight k: the BDP/Castella–Hsieh setting with Heegner hypothesis when n⁻ = 1.

sources.match: Hsieh fixes π, its base change π_K, the character λ with λ|_{A_F^×} = ω^{-1}, the normalised root numbers, Hypothesis A, the p-ordinary CM type, the anticyclotomic tower Γ⁻ with Λ, the critical specialisations and the p-adic multiplier e_{Σ_p}(π, χ).

nodes.title: Explicit Waldspurger formula for toric periods (Hsieh Proposition 2.1, Theorem 3.14)
nodes.statement: For ϕ₁, ϕ₂ ∈ A(π) with factorisable Whittaker functions normalised at almost all places and χ a Hecke character of M with χ|_{A_F^×} = ω^{-1}, the toric periods P_χ(ϕ) = ∫_{A_F^×M^×\A_M^×}ϕ(ι(t))χ(t)dt satisfy P_χ(ϕ₁)P_χ(ϕ₂) = Λ(1/2, π_M ⊗ χ)·∏_{v∈S}L(1/2, π_{M,v} ⊗ χ_v)^{-1}P(W_{1,v}, W_{2,v}, χ_v) for every large finite S (Proposition 2.1). For Hsieh’s normalised toric form ϕ_χ (toric-test-vectors) and the operator V^{e+m}: P_χ(π(ς)V^{e+m}ϕ_χ)² = Γ_Σ(k+m)Γ_Σ(m+1)/(4π)^{k+2m+1·Σ}·e_{Σ_p}(π, χ)·L(1/2, π_M ⊗ χ)·|D_M|_ℝ^{-1/2}·C′_π(χ)N(π, χ)² (Theorem 3.14), with explicit constants C′_π(χ), N(π, χ).
hypotheses: Hypothesis A at v | n⁻ (otherwise the period vanishes identically by Saito–Tunnell); (sf) for the explicit local computations.
proofSteps: Proposition 2.1: combine Waldspurger’s formulas (proved through the Shimizu theta lift; GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.5 owns the Waldspurger period formula) into a decomposition of the global toric period into local Whittaker period integrals; Hypothesis A is the Saito–Tunnell condition for nonvanishing of the local toric functionals (GZ.4).
Theorem 3.14: compute each local integral for the chosen toric Whittaker function W_{χ,v} (Hsieh §§3.3–3.8: unramified, ramified, inert and split places, archimedean place, places above p).
acceptance: F = ℚ, n⁻ = 1: a Gross–Zagier/Waldspurger-type formula for the square of the CM period of a weight-k newform twisted by an anticyclotomic character.

sources.match: Hsieh decomposes products of toric periods into local Whittaker period integrals and computes them for his toric forms, obtaining the explicit formula for P_χ(π(ς)V^{e+m}ϕ_χ)² in terms of L(1/2, π_K ⊗ χ) and the p-adic multiplier.

nodes.title: Hsieh’s normalised toric forms
nodes.statement: A Whittaker function W ∈ W(π_v, ψ_v) is toric of character χ_v if π(ι_ς(t))W = χ_v^{-1}(t)W for t ∈ T_v (Definition 3.1). Hsieh chooses at each place a toric Whittaker function W_{χ,v} (archimedean: V^{e+m}W_k; finite places: explicit new and test vectors; places above p: p-modified functions W♭_{χ,v}, Definition 3.12), shows they are toric (Lemma 3.2), and forms the automorphic form ϕ_χ (Lemma 3.13) and the normalised Hilbert modular form f*_χ = N(π, χ)^{-1}|det ς_f|^{-k_mx/2}f_χ (Definition 5.1). The normalised local Fourier coefficients a*_{χ,v} (Definition 3.16) take values in a finite extension O of O_{L_π}, are 1 at unramified v ∉ B(χ) and at v ∈ A(χ), and µ_p(Ψ_{π,χ,v}) = 0 for v ∈ B(χ) iff some a*_{χ,v}(η_v) is a p-unit (Proposition 3.19).
hypotheses: Hsieh’s setting; ς the chosen embedding of M^× into GL₂(F) at the relevant places.
proofSteps: Local choices place by place (Hsieh §§3.3–3.8), checked toric by direct computation (Lemma 3.2).
Global form: the product of the local Whittaker functions defines ϕ_χ ∈ A(π) (Lemma 3.13); f_χ and f*_χ by (5.1).
Integrality and nonvanishing modulo p of the normalised coefficients: Proposition 3.19.
acceptance: n⁻ = 1, F = ℚ: f*_χ is the p-depleted, χ-toric newform used by Bertolini–Darmon–Prasanna.

sources.locator: Definition 3.1, Lemma 3.2 p. 727; Definition 3.12, Lemma 3.13 pp. 736–737; Definition 3.16 p. 739; Proposition 3.19 p. 742; Definition 5.1 p. 749
sources.match: Hsieh defines toric Whittaker functions, chooses them place by place including the p-modified ones, forms the toric automorphic form and its normalised Hilbert modular form, and proves integrality and the mod-p criterion for the normalised local Fourier coefficients.

nodes.title: Hsieh’s square-root anticyclotomic distribution L_{Σ_p}(π, λ)
nodes.statement: There is a unique p-adic distribution F_{λ,c} : C(Γ⁻) → V(c, M, ℤ_p) (p-adic Hilbert modular forms) supported on the image Γ′ of the relevant ideles, with F_{λ,c}(φ̂) = θ^m f*_{λφ,c} for every φ̂ ∈ X_p^crit of weight (m, −m) (Proposition 5.5); its q-expansion measure has coefficient a_β(f*_λ, c)ϕ(rec_{Σ_p}(β)) at q^β. The anticyclotomic distribution L_{Σ_p}(π, λ) ∈ Λ is the weighted sum of the evaluations of F_{λ,c} at the CM points x(a) (with the ideal classes and the twisting operators |[a] of Definition 5.6), divided by the p-adic period: a measure, the square root of the anticyclotomic p-adic L-function L_{Σ_p}(π, λ)².
hypotheses: Hsieh’s setting with (ord); c a prime-to-p polarisation ideal; the evaluation at CM points uses cm-points-and-canonical-trivialisations.
proofSteps: Define the q-expansion measure F_{λ,c}(q); by the p-adic q-expansion principle (L3/padic-q-expansion-principle) and the integrality of the normalised Fourier coefficients (toric-test-vectors) it is a measure with values in p-adic Hilbert modular forms; its moments are θ^m f*_{λφ,c} by Katz’s θ on q-expansions (L3/katz-differential-operators).
Evaluate at CM points with canonical trivialisations and sum over the anticyclotomic class group with the twisting operators (Hsieh §5.4).
acceptance: M imaginary quadratic, F = ℚ, n⁻ = 1: the Bertolini–Darmon–Prasanna / Castella–Hsieh measure (comparison bdp-castella-hsieh-specialisation).

sources.locator: Proposition 5.5 and its proof, p. 753; Definition 5.6, p. 754; §5.4
sources.match: Hsieh constructs the unique distribution F_{λ,c} on Γ⁻ with values in p-adic modular forms interpolating θ^m f*_{λφ,c}, and obtains L_{Σ_p}(π, λ) by evaluating it at CM points.

nodes.title: Interpolation of central Rankin–Selberg values (Hsieh Theorem A, Theorem 5.7)
nodes.statement: Assume (ord), Hypothesis A and (sf). For every φ̂ ∈ X_p^crit of weight (m, −m), φ̂(L_{Σ_p}(π, λ))²/Ω_p^{2(k+2m)} = Γ_Σ(k+m)Γ_Σ(m+1)/((Im δ)^{k+2m}(4π)^{k+2m+1·Σ})·e_{Σ_p}(π, λφ)·L(1/2, π_M ⊗ λφ)/Ω_M^{2(k+2m)}·[O_M^×:O_F^×]²·φ(𝔉^{-1}), with Ω_M = (2πi)^{-1}Ω_∞, (Im δ) = (Im σ(δ))_σ, and 𝔉 the split part of the decomposition 𝔑⁺ = 𝔉𝔉̄ of the prime-to-p conductor. Equivalently (Theorem 5.7), (L_{Σ_p}(π, λ)(φ̂)/Ω_p^{k+2m})² = [O_M^×:O_F^×]²·e_{Σ_p}(π, λφ)L^{alg}(1/2, π_M ⊗ λφ)·φ^{-1}(𝔉). Each factor (Γ-values, Im δ, (4π)-power, p-adic multiplier, unit index, φ(𝔉^{-1}), periods) is a separate datum. If π is induced from a Hecke character of M, L_{Σ_p}(π, λ) is, up to a unit of Λ, a product of two Katz–Hida–Tilouine p-adic L-functions.
hypotheses: (ord), Hypothesis A, (sf), p odd; the CM-type ordinarity does not assume π ordinary.
proofSteps: Evaluate the CM-point sum of θ^m f*_{λφ,c} (anticyclotomic-distribution); convert θ^m to δ^m at CM points with the periods (L3/katz-cm-algebraicity).
The sum of δ^m f* over CM points is the toric period P_{λφ}(π(ς)V^{e+m}ϕ_{λφ}); square it with explicit-waldspurger (Theorem 3.14).
Collect constants; the factor φ(𝔉^{-1}) comes from the choice of the split part of the level.
acceptance: m = 0: the value of L_{Σ_p}(π, λ) at the trivial character squared is the algebraic central value L(1/2, π_M ⊗ λ) times explicit factors.
F = ℚ, n⁻ = 1: BDP Theorem 5.4 / Castella–Hsieh Proposition 3.8 up to normalisation (bdp-castella-hsieh-specialisation).

sources.locator: Theorem A, p. 712; Theorem 5.7 and its proof, p. 754
sources.match: Hsieh proves the interpolation of the square of L_{Σ_p}(π, λ) at critical characters with the stated Γ-, period, multiplier and unit factors, and notes the induced case factors as two Katz–Hida–Tilouine functions.

nodes.title: The µ-invariant from Fourier coefficients at CM cusps (Hsieh Theorem 6.1)
nodes.statement: Assume p unramified in F (with the setting of theorem-a). The µ-invariant µ⁻_{π,λ,Σ} := inf{r ∈ ℚ_{≥0} : p^{-r}L_{Σ_p}(π, λ) ≢ 0 mod m_pΛ} equals inf_{(a,u)∈D₁×D₀, β∈F_+} v_p(a_β(f*_{λ,u}, c(a))), the minimum valuation of the Fourier coefficients of the forms f*_{λ,u} at the cusps (a, b) for which ab^{-1} is the polarisation of an abelian variety with CM by O_M.
hypotheses: p unramified in F; Hida’s linear independence (hida-linear-independence) is the input that requires this.
proofSteps: Write L_{Σ_p}(π, λ) as a finite sum over (u, a) of the p-adic avatars F_{u,a}|[a] evaluated along the CM points (Hsieh §6).

Reduce modulo p: by Hida’s linear independence of the translates a_i(f_ij) modulo p under the automorphisms of the Igusa tower (Hida 2010 Theorem 3.20, Corollary 3.21) and the q-expansion principle, the reduction vanishes iff each F_{u,a} vanishes modulo p, i.e. iff all its Fourier coefficients do.
acceptance: F = ℚ: µ vanishes iff some Fourier coefficient of the toric form at the cusp ∞ is a p-unit.

sources.locator: Theorem 6.1 and its proof, p. 756; Introduction, pp. 715–716
sources.match: Hsieh proves that the µ-invariant equals the infimum of p-adic valuations of Fourier coefficients of the toric forms at the CM cusps, reducing the question by Hida’s method.

nodes.title: Vanishing of the anticyclotomic µ-invariant (Hsieh Theorem B, Theorem 6.2)
nodes.statement: Assume (ord), Hypothesis A, (sf), p unramified in F and (aiK) the residual representation ρ̄_p(π_M) := ρ_p(π)|_{G_M} mod m_p is absolutely irreducible. Then µ⁻_{π,λ,Σ} = 0 if and only if Σ_{v|c_λ⁻}µ_p(Ψ_{π,λ,v}) = 0, with the local invariants of (3.30) (Theorem 6.2). In particular (Theorem B) µ⁻_{π,λ,Σ} = 0 when moreover p ∤ ∏_{v(c⁻_λ)=1}#(∆_{λ,v}), ∆_{λ,v} = λ(O_{M_v}^×) for v | c_λ⁻ (Remark 6.4: this local condition gives the vanishing of the local invariants).
hypotheses: The three extra hypotheses p ∤ D_F, (aiK) and the local image-order condition, in addition to those of theorem-a.

The Galois representation ρ_p(π) is imported for k_σ ≥ 2 (AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations:R19.2); Hsieh also allows limits of discrete series (k_σ = 1), whose Galois representations (Rogawski–Tunnell, Jarvis) are not planned in the atlas, so the weight-one case is outside this node.
proofSteps: If some µ_p(Ψ_{π,λ,v}) > 0 then every a_β(f*_{λ,u}, c(a)) ≡ 0 mod m_p (Proposition 5.3 with Proposition 3.19), so µ > 0 by cm-integrality-criterion.

Conversely, if all local invariants vanish, a nonzero coefficient modulo p exists by Proposition 3.19; relate the Fourier coefficients at the CM cusps to traces of Frobenius of ρ_p(π) (Hecke eigenvalues) and use (aiK) with the group-theoretic Lemma 6.3 to find β with a_β ≢ 0.
Theorem B from Theorem 6.2 and Remark 6.4.
acceptance: n⁻ = 1 and λ unramified at the non-split primes: the local invariants vanish and µ = 0 under (aiK).

sources.locator: Theorem B, p. 713; Theorem 6.2 and proof, Lemma 6.3, Remark 6.4, pp. 757–758
sources.match: Hsieh characterises µ = 0 by the vanishing of local invariants under absolute irreducibility of the residual representation restricted to G_K, and deduces Theorem B under the character-image condition.

nodes.title: Mod-p nonvanishing of central values with ℓ-power anticyclotomic twists (Hsieh Theorem C, Theorem 7.1)
nodes.statement: Let ℓ ≠ p be a prime, 𝔩 a prime of F above ℓ, Γ⁻_𝔩 the Galois group of the anticyclotomic pro-ℓ extension in the ray class field of M of conductor 𝔩^∞, X⁰_𝔩 its finite-order characters, and χ a Hecke character of infinity type (k/2 + m, −k/2 − m) and conductor c_χ. Assume (ord), (sf), Hypothesis A, p unramified in F, (pl, n c_χ D_{M/F}) = 1, ρ̄_p(π_M) absolutely irreducible, and p ∤ ∏_{v(c⁻_χ)=1}#∆_{χ,v} (Theorem 7.1: µ_p(Ψ_{π,χ,v}) = 0 for v | c⁻_χ). Then for almost all φ ∈ X⁰_𝔩, [O_M^×:O_F^×]²·Γ_Σ(k+m)Γ_Σ(m+1)/((Im δ)^{k+2m}(4π)^{k+2m+1·Σ})·L(1/2, π_M ⊗ χφ)/Ω_M^{2(k+2m)} ≢ 0 mod m_p. ‘Almost all’ means all but finitely many φ if dim_{ℚ_ℓ}F_𝔩 = 1, and a Zariski-dense subset if dim_{ℚ_ℓ}F_𝔩 > 1.
hypotheses: The conductor conditions of Theorem C, separate from those of Theorem B, and p unramified in F, which Theorem C as printed omits but Theorem 7.1 (through Theorem 6.2) assumes (sourceIssues E6); the index c⁻_χ in the local condition follows Theorem 7.1 (sourceIssues E7); the two meanings of ‘almost all’ are distinct and must be kept.
proofSteps: Hida’s method (Hsieh §7.1): express the algebraic L-values as a p-adic measure on the ℓ-adic anticyclotomic class group Cl⁻_{𝔩^∞} given by evaluating the toric form at CM points (Hsieh’s Proposition 7.3, Lemma 7.4).

Non-vanishing modulo p for almost all φ follows from the Zariski density of CM points in the Igusa tower modulo p and linear independence (hida-cm-density, hida-linear-independence), together with the nonvanishing modulo p of some Fourier coefficient at a CM cusp (Proposition 3.19 and (aiK)).
acceptance: F = ℚ: ℓ-power anticyclotomic twists of a newform have p-unit algebraic central values for all but finitely many characters (a Vatsal-type statement).

sources.locator: Theorem C, p. 713; Theorem 7.1 and §7.1, pp. 759–760
sources.match: Hsieh proves the nonvanishing modulo p of algebraic central values twisted by ℓ-power anticyclotomic characters, for almost all characters with the two meanings of ‘almost all’, following Hida’s method.

nodes.title: The F = ℚ, n⁻ = 1 specialisation: the BDP / Castella–Hsieh measure
nodes.statement: For F = ℚ, M an imaginary quadratic field in which p splits, π attached to a newform f of weight k and level N with every prime dividing N split in M (n⁻ = 1, so Hypothesis A and (sf) hold), and λ of infinity type (k/2, −k/2), Hsieh’s L_{Σ_p}(π, λ) is the anticyclotomic measure of Bertolini–Darmon–Prasanna (recovering BDP Theorem 5.4 under their extra assumptions p ∤ N and n⁻ divisible only by ramified primes) and the measure L_{p,ψ}(f) of Castella–Hsieh on Γ̃ = Gal(M_{p^∞}/M) used by GeneralizedHeegnerCycles, GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights and RankZeroOneBSD. The comparison records: the change of variable φ̂ ↦ λ^{-1}φ^{-1}|·|^{k/2} between Hsieh’s X_p^crit and BDP’s Σ_cc^{(2)}(N), the opposite infinity-type conventions, the factor φ(𝔉^{-1}), the unit index, the periods Ω_p, Ω_∞, and the Euler factor at the prime above p fixed by ι_p for p-new f.
hypotheses: F = ℚ, M imaginary quadratic, p split, Heegner hypothesis for N; for p-new f the extra Euler factor is recorded, not hidden.
proofSteps: Specialise theorem-a; translate characters and infinity types as in Hsieh’s Remark on p. 712.
Match with the interpolation formula of Castella–Hsieh Proposition 3.8 as quoted by Castella–Grossi–Lee–Skinner (§2.1.2), factor by factor.
acceptance: The square of the specialisation at the trivial character is L^{alg}(1/2, π_M ⊗ λ) times the explicit factors.

sources.match: Hsieh notes that for F = ℚ his construction recovers BDP Theorem 5.4 under extra assumptions, describes the change of variables to BDP’s set of characters and that their infinity-type conventions are opposite.
Castella–Grossi–Lee–Skinner use the measure L_E built from Castella–Hsieh’s Proposition 3.8 for the BDP p-adic L-function.

nodes.title: Mod-p nonvanishing of anticyclotomic L-values (sub-layer L3m)
nodes.statement: This node collects the mod-p inputs that L3h’s Theorems B and C and the congruence consumers need, as one sub-layer: (i) Hida’s linear independence modulo p of translates of mod-p modular forms under the automorphisms of the Igusa tower at a CM point (hida-linear-independence); (ii) Hida’s Zariski density of CM points in the Hilbert modular Igusa tower modulo p (hida-cm-density); (iii) Hida’s µ = 0 theorem for anticyclotomic Katz–Hida–Tilouine p-adic L-functions (hida-katz-mu-vanishing); (iv) Hsieh’s mod-p nonvanishing of Hecke L-values twisted by ℓ-power anticyclotomic characters (hsieh-hecke-nonvanishing); (v) Finis’ divisibility of anticyclotomic Hecke L-values by p-adic valuation of local invariants (finis-divisibility). Statement: under the hypotheses of the respective theorems, the central L-values of the corresponding families are p-adic units for almost all characters (in the sense of each theorem).
hypotheses: Each part keeps its own hypotheses (p > 2 unramified in F, ordinary CM type, root-number and residual conditions).
proofSteps: Assemble (i)–(v); the dependencies are the five nodes of this sub-layer.
acceptance: Skinner–Urban’s Klingen-Eisenstein nonvanishing modulo p uses (v) and Vatsal’s theorem through this node; Castella–Liu–Wan’s §5.6 uses (iv).

sources.locator: Introduction, p. 713 (the list [Vat03], [Hid04a], [Fin06], [Hsi12]) and pp. 713–714 (applications to Eisenstein congruences)
sources.match: Hsieh places his Theorem C among the mod-p nonvanishing results of Vatsal, Hida, Finis and Hsieh and explains their role in Eisenstein-congruence arguments (Skinner–Urban use Finis and Vatsal).

nodes.title: Hida’s linear independence modulo p at a CM point (Hida 2010 Theorem 3.20, Corollary 3.21)
nodes.statement: Let F̄ be the residue field of W (an algebraic closure of F_p), x ∈ Ig(F̄) a closed point of the Hilbert modular Igusa tower fixed by the action of T(ℤ_(p)) (a CM point), and let a ∈ T(ℤ_p) = O_p^× act on the formal completion Ô_{Ig,x} by t ↦ t^a on the canonical Serre–Tate coordinate. If a₀, …, a_n ∈ T_x(ℤ_p) satisfy a_ia_j^{-1} ∉ T_x(ℚ) for i ≠ j and, for a fixed parallel weight κ, the mod-p modular forms {H_κ, f_ij}_j are linearly independent over F̄ for each i in a subset I, then {a_i(f_ij)}_{i∈I,j} are linearly independent over F̄ in Ô_{S,y}/F̄ (Corollary 3.21; Theorem 3.20 is the corresponding statement for the stalks).
hypotheses: p unramified in F (needed where the corollary is applied in §5); F̄ an algebraic closure of F_p.
proofSteps: Hida’s proof (§3): a Zariski-closed subscheme of a product of copies of the Igusa tower stable under the torus action is a union of ‘diagonal’ subschemes given by isogenies (Proposition 3.11, Corollary 3.16, via Chai’s rigidity of formal tori); a linear relation among the a_i(f_ij) would produce such a subscheme contradicting a_ia_j^{-1} ∉ T_x(ℚ).
Corollary 3.21 by dividing by a(H_κ), which is 1 at t.
acceptance: F = ℚ: translates of mod-p modular forms by distinct elements of ℤ_p^× modulo ℚ^× are linearly independent at a CM point (the one-dimensional case).

sources.match: Hida proves linear independence modulo p of translates of modular forms under the torus action at a CM point of the Igusa tower, through rigidity of the Serre–Tate coordinates.
Hsieh uses Hida’s Theorem 3.20 and Corollary 3.21 with the q-expansion principle for p-adic modular forms.

nodes.title: Hida’s Zariski density of CM points modulo p (as used by Hsieh)
nodes.statement: For a CM field M with p-ordinary CM type, ℓ ≠ p and 𝔩 | ℓ a prime of F, the CM points of conductor 𝔩^n (n ≥ 0) attached to the anticyclotomic class groups Cl⁻_{𝔩^n} are Zariski dense in the Igusa tower over the Hilbert modular variety modulo p (in each irreducible component, of dimension [F:ℚ]), in the strong form that a function on the Igusa tower modulo p that vanishes at almost all such points (outside finitely many if dim_{ℚ_ℓ}F_𝔩 = 1, outside a non-Zariski-dense set otherwise) vanishes identically. This is the input that converts ‘a Fourier coefficient at some cusp is a p-unit’ into ‘the measure on Cl⁻_{𝔩^∞} is nonzero modulo p for almost all characters’.
hypotheses: p > 2 unramified in F; p-ordinary CM type; ℓ ≠ p.
proofSteps: Hida, ‘Non-vanishing modulo p of Hecke L-values’ (Geometric aspects of Dwork theory, 2004), Theorems 3.2 and 3.3 — not read here (not freely available); statement taken from Hsieh 2014 §7 (p. 760) and the definition of ‘almost all’ ([Hid04a, p. 737] quoted by Hsieh, p. 713). The proof uses the irreducibility of the Igusa tower (L3/igusa-irreducibility) and Chai’s rigidity of Hecke-stable subvarieties.
acceptance: F = ℚ: Heegner points of ℓ-power conductor are dense modulo p in the Igusa curve (Vatsal’s setting).

sources.locator: §7.1 and the proof of Theorem 7.1, pp. 759–760 (citing [Hid04a, Thm. 3.2 and Thm. 3.3]); Theorem C and the meaning of ‘almost all’, p. 713
sources.match: Hsieh reduces the nonvanishing of L-values modulo p to the nonvanishing of a Fourier coefficient at some cusp via Hida’s density theorems, and quotes Hida’s meaning of ‘almost all’.

nodes.title: Hida’s µ = 0 for anticyclotomic Katz–Hida–Tilouine p-adic L-functions (Hida 2010 Theorem I) and Hsieh’s refinement
nodes.statement: Let φ be the measure of L3/katz-hida-tilouine-tame on Z(C) with branch character ψ and anticyclotomic projection φ⁻_ψ on Γ⁻. If p > 2 is unramified in F/ℚ and the inert-or-ramified part 𝔍 of C is trivial, then µ(φ⁻_ψ) = 0 unless the condition (V) holds; when (V) holds µ(φ⁻_ψ) is finite and positive; (V) is equivalent to (M1) M/F unramified at every finite place, (M2) the strict ideal class of the polarisation ideal c in F is not a norm class from M, (M3) a ↦ (ψ(a)N_{F/ℚ}(a) mod m_W) is the quadratic character of M/F (Hida 2010 Theorem I and Lemma 5.2). For self-dual characters with root number +1, Hsieh computes µ = Σ_{v|C⁻}µ_p(χ_v) (Hsieh 2012/2014 Theorem A) and proves µ = 0 when the local invariants vanish and χ is not residually self-dual (Theorem B).
hypotheses: p > 2, p unramified in F/ℚ, I = 1 for Hida’s Theorem I; p ∤ D_F for Hsieh’s refinement; ordinary CM type.
proofSteps: Hida 2010: split the Katz measure by branch characters, compute its q-expansion at good representatives (§5.1–5.3), and conclude by linear independence (hida-linear-independence) and the q-expansion principle (Theorem 5.1).
Hsieh’s refinement: same strategy with self-dual characters and the local invariants µ_p(χ_v) (Hsieh, ‘On the µ-invariant of anticyclotomic p-adic L-functions for CM fields’, Theorems A, B, 6.5).
acceptance: M imaginary quadratic, p split, ψ a branch character not satisfying (V): µ = 0, as used by Castella–Grossi–Lee–Skinner for the Eisenstein branch.

sources.match: Hida proves the vanishing of the anticyclotomic µ-invariant of the Katz–Hida–Tilouine measure for p > 2 unramified in F with I = 1, unless (V), where it is positive.

sources.locator: Theorems A and B, p. 2; Theorem 6.5 p. 23
sources.match: Hsieh computes µ for self-dual characters with root number +1 as the sum of local invariants and proves µ = 0 for non-residually-self-dual characters with vanishing local invariants.

sources.locator: Introduction p. 4; Theorem 2.2.2 and proof, p. 15
sources.match: Castella–Grossi–Lee–Skinner deduce µ(L_E) = 0 from the Eisenstein congruence and Hida’s theorem for the Katz p-adic L-functions of the two characters.

nodes.title: Mod-p nonvanishing of Hecke L-values with ℓ-power anticyclotomic twists (Hsieh 2012 Theorems A, B)
nodes.statement: Assume (unr) p > 2 unramified in F, (ord) Σ p-ordinary, and (pℓ, D_{M/F}C) = 1. Let χ be a Hecke character of M. (Theorem B) If µ_p(χ_v) = 0 for every v | C⁻ and χ is not residually self-dual, then (NV) holds for (χ, 𝔩): the algebraic Hecke L-values L(0, χφ) are p-adic units for almost all ℓ-power anticyclotomic characters φ. (Theorem A) If χ is self-dual with µ_p(χ_v) = 0 for v | C⁻, global root number W(χ|·|_{A_M}^{-1/2}) = 1, R squarefree, and 𝔩 split in M, then (NV) holds for (χ, 𝔩) (the squarefreeness can be removed, Remark 6.9).
hypotheses: (unr), (ord), (pℓ, D_{M/F}C) = 1; the extra conditions of each theorem.
proofSteps: Hida’s method for Katz–Hida–Tilouine measures on the ℓ-adic anticyclotomic class group, with Hsieh’s computation of the local invariants and the mod-p nonvanishing of Fourier coefficients at CM cusps, then hida-cm-density and hida-linear-independence.
acceptance: M imaginary quadratic: nonvanishing modulo p of L(0, χφ) for almost all ℓ-power anticyclotomic φ, used in Castella–Liu–Wan §5.6 and by Wan for U(3,1) Fourier–Jacobi coefficients.

sources.locator: Introduction pp. 1–3 (hypotheses (unr), (ord), Theorems A and B); Theorem 6.8 and Remark 6.9, pp. 23–24
sources.match: Hsieh proves the mod-p nonvanishing (NV) for ℓ-power anticyclotomic twists of Hecke characters under the stated hypotheses, for non-residually-self-dual characters (Theorem B) and for self-dual characters with root number one (Theorem A).
Hsieh lists [Hsi12] among the earlier mod-p nonvanishing results (p. 713) and explains that his Theorem C is used by Wan for Fourier–Jacobi coefficients on U(3,1) (p. 714).

nodes.title: Finis’ divisibility of anticyclotomic L-values and Vatsal’s nonvanishing
nodes.statement: Let M be imaginary quadratic, p an odd prime split in M, ℓ an odd prime different from p, k, d positive integers and Ω_∞ a complex CM period. (1) If ℓ splits in M, then for all but finitely many anticyclotomic Hecke characters λ of M of conductor dividing dD_Mp^∞, infinity type (−k, k − 1) and global root number W(λ) = +1, v_ℓ(Ω_∞^{1−2k}(k−1)!(2π/√D)^{k−1}W_ℓ(λ)L(0, λ)) = Σ_{q inert}µ_ℓ(λ_q), where W_ℓ(λ) = N(l)^{−e(l)}G(δ, λ_l) is the ℓ-adic root number (l the prime of M above ℓ fixed by i_ℓ, e(l) the exponent of l in the conductor) and µ_ℓ(λ_q) the local invariant at an inert q. (2) If ℓ is inert or ramified and k = 1, v_ℓ(Ω_∞^{-1}D^{1/4}L(0, λ)) = Σ_{q ≠ ℓ inert}µ_ℓ(λ_q) + b_ℓ(λ_ℓ, w(λ)) for all but finitely many such λ of infinity type (−1, 0). For every anticyclotomic λ of these infinity types the left side is at least the right side, except possibly for M = ℚ(√−3) and ℓ = 3. Vatsal’s nonvanishing of central L-values of weight-two forms twisted by anticyclotomic characters modulo p (Duke 116 (2003)) is the GL₂ counterpart; it is not read here and is recorded as an import for the consumers.
hypotheses: M imaginary quadratic, p odd split, ℓ odd ≠ p (Finis’ ℓ plays the role of the residue characteristic of the valuation).
proofSteps: Finis’ proof: theta functions with complex multiplication and their reduction modulo ℓ, Shintani representation and the nonvanishing of theta functions in characteristic ℓ (Theorem 4.1), combined with Hida’s method.
acceptance: k = 1, ℓ split: the ℓ-adic valuation of the algebraic L-value equals the sum of local invariants at the inert primes for almost all characters.

sources.match: Finis proves the equality of valuations of algebraic anticyclotomic Hecke L-values with sums of local invariants for almost all characters, using nonvanishing of theta functions in characteristic ℓ.
Hsieh records that Skinner–Urban use the results of Finis and Vatsal to show the nonvanishing modulo p of Klingen–Eisenstein series on U(2,2).

nodes.title: The EHLS unitary setting and its doubling datum
nodes.statement: Let K be a CM field with maximal totally real subfield K⁺, p a prime unramified in K such that every place of K⁺ above p splits in K, V an n-dimensional hermitian space over K with signatures (a_σ, b_σ) at the archimedean places, G₁ = GU(V) its similitude group with the unitary PEL datum of PELModuli:M5/unitary-pel-datum and Shimura variety Sh(V), and −V the same space with the negated form. The doubling space is W = V ⊕ (−V) with the form ⟨·,·⟩_V ⊕ −⟨·,·⟩_V, maximally isotropic, so U(W) has the Siegel parabolic P with Levi GL_n(K); G₃ ⊂ G(V) × G(−V) is the pair of groups with equal similitude and G₄ = GU(W). The embedding G₃ ↪ G₄ (doubling embedding) matches the PEL data and induces a morphism of Shimura varieties Sh(V) × Sh(−V) → Sh(W) that restricts to the ordinary loci. A cuspidal anti-holomorphic representation π of G₁ is ordinary of type (κ, K_r) if it is holomorphic of type (κ, K_r) for −V and its image meets the ordinary forms S^κ_ord(K_r, R).
hypotheses: p unramified in K, every place of K⁺ above p split in K; level K = K^pK_p with K_p of Iwahori type of depth r at p.
proofSteps: The PEL data, Shimura varieties, canonical models and integral models at p come from PELModuli:M5/unitary-pel-datum with ShimuraCompactifications:C5/integral-toroidal-space for compactifications; the hermitian space −V and the doubled space W are linear algebra over K.

The doubling embedding of groups and of PEL data (EHLS §3, ‘PEL data and restriction of forms’) and its compatibility with ordinary loci follow from the decomposition of the p-divisible groups at split places.
Ordinarity of π is the condition of EHLS §6.6 on the image of π in the ordinary forms.
acceptance: n = 1: G₁ = GU(1) is a torus and the doubling construction reduces to Katz’s CM setting (EHLS History §1.2).
n = 2, signature (1, 1) at one place: unitary Shimura curves.

sources.locator: §1.4 notation, p. 11 (hypotheses on p); §1 introduction pp. 5–7 (doubling space, Garrett map); §3 pp. 35–40 (PEL data and restriction of forms); §6.6, p. 104 (ordinary of type (κ, K_r))
sources.match: EHLS fix p unramified in K with every place of K⁺ above p split, the hermitian space V with its signatures, the doubled space W = V ⊕ (−V) and the doubling embedding of Shimura varieties, and define ordinary anti-holomorphic representations of type (κ, K).

uses.how: the doubling integral lives on G₃ ⊂ G₄
the hypotheses on π
Skinner–Urban use the U(2,2) instance

nodes.title: Ordinary p-adic forms, the ordinary Hecke algebra and congruence ideals (EHLS §§6–7)
nodes.statement: For the datum of ehls-unitary-datum: the ordinary projector e on p-adic modular forms on the Igusa tower over the ordinary locus of Sh(V) (in characteristic zero and over O, built from the canonical and subcanonical extensions of the automorphic bundles), the spaces S^κ_ord(K_r, R), the ordinary Hecke algebra T_{K_r,κ,R} generated by the normalised U_{w,j,κ} at p and the T(g) away from p, its connected component T_π at the maximal ideal of an ordinary π, the Λ-adic module of ordinary forms with control (EHLS Theorem 7.3.1: T_π is finite free over Λ^o_π), the congruence ideal C(π) of Definition 6.7.2 (annihilator of the quotient of ordinary cohomology cut out by π), and the R-lattices Î_π, Î_{π♭} of test vectors.
hypotheses: Characteristic-zero lifts of the special-fibre Igusa tower are constructed here from the canonical trivialisation over the ordinary locus; IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration:IG.1 supplies only the special-fibre and finite-level geometry.
proofSteps: Automorphic bundles and canonical/subcanonical extensions: AutomorphicBundles:B2, B3; Fourier–Jacobi/q-expansion principle: AutomorphicBundles:B5/vector-expansion-principle; Koecher on the ordinary locus: ShimuraCompactifications:C5/ordinary-koecher.

Igusa tower over the ordinary locus in characteristic zero: trivialisations of the multiplicative part of the p-divisible group of the universal abelian scheme at split places (the mixed-characteristic lift that IG.1 does not supply).
Ordinary projector e = lim U_p^{n!} and Hida’s control theorem in this PEL setting (EHLS §§7.1–7.3; PadicFamilies supplies the general family formalism).
Congruence ideal and the test-vector lattices (EHLS §§6.7, 8.4–8.5).
acceptance: n = 1: the ordinary Hecke algebra of a CM torus is a group ring and C(π) is trivial.

sources.locator: §6.6, the ordinary Hecke algebra T_{K_r,κ,R}, p. 98; Hypothesis 6.6.4, p. 99; Definition 6.7.2, p. 105; Definition 6.7.9, p. 106; Theorem 7.3.1, p. 110

nodes.title: The EHLS hypotheses: Gorenstein, global multiplicity one, minimality
nodes.statement: For π ordinary of type (κ, K): Hypothesis 7.3.2 (Gorenstein): T̂_π := Hom_{Λ^o_π}(T_π, Λ^o_π) is free of rank one over T_π (an isomorphism G_π : T̂_π ≅ T_π), and Hom_{O_π}(lim_r S^κ_ord(K_rp, O_π), O_π)_{m_π} is free over T_π. Hypothesis 7.3.3 (global multiplicity one): every π′ ∈ S(K^p, π) occurs with multiplicity one in the cuspidal spectrum of G. Proposition–Hypothesis 7.3.5 (minimality): for every (κ₁, r₁) there is an isomorphism of T_{K_1^p,κ₁,O,π}-modules T_{K^p_1,κ₁,O,π} ⊗ Î_π ≅ Hom(S^{κ₁}_ord(K^p_1r₁, O)_{m_π}, O). These are propositions about π, not properties of every ordinary component; each consumer states which it assumes.
hypotheses: Stated as propositions (Prop-valued) on the datum; no constructor asserts them.
proofSteps: Each is a property of the objects of ehls-ordinary-forms-hecke; EHLS discuss when they can be verified (Taylor–Wiles methods for Gorenstein, Remark 9.3.1; the stronger multiplicity-one Hypothesis 6.6.4 is expected when the bad places split and the base change is cuspidal, p. 100; Hypothesis 7.3.3 is noted on p. 110 to follow from Mok and Kaletha–Mínguez–Shin–White, whose proofs rest partly on announced results of Arthur, so it stays a stated hypothesis here).
acceptance: When the residual Galois representation has large image, Gorenstein can often be verified by Taylor–Wiles (Remark 9.3.1); it is certainly not valid in complete generality.

sources.locator: Hypotheses 7.3.2–7.3.3, p. 110; Proposition 7.3.5, p. 112; Remark 9.3.1, p. 145

nodes.title: p-adic and C^∞ differential operators on unitary forms (Eischen)
nodes.statement: On the Igusa tower over the ordinary locus of the doubled Shimura variety, Eischen’s p-adic differential operators θ^{(κ,a,b)} use the unit-root splitting of the de Rham bundle in place of the Hodge splitting; the C^∞ operators D(κ, χ) = δ(r̃_σ, s̃_σ) use the Hodge splitting (EHLS Corollary 4.4.9, Proposition 4.4.11). For critical (κ, χ) the C^∞ operator applied to the holomorphic Siegel Eisenstein section gives the section needed by the doubling integral, and the p-adic operator θ^{(κ,a,b)} realises it p-adically; at ordinary CM-type points their values agree up to periods (EHLS Proposition 8.1.1).
hypotheses: Critical pairs (κ, χ) as in EHLS (95)–(97).
proofSteps: Construct the operators from the Gauss–Manin connection, Kodaira–Spencer and the chosen splitting (Eischen 2012, 2016, quoted in EHLS §§4.4, 8.1).
Holomorphic projection and comparison at ordinary points as in Katz’s case (L3/katz-differential-operators, L3/katz-cm-algebraicity).
acceptance: n = 1: the operators of Katz for CM tori.

sources.locator: §4.4.10, Corollary 4.4.9, Proposition 4.4.11, pp. 73–75; Proposition 8.1.1, p. 121; p. 125
sources.match: EHLS define the C^∞ operators D(κ, χ) for critical pairs and the p-adic operators θ^{(κ,a,b)} via the unit-root splitting, following Eischen, and compare them.

nodes.title: The EHLS Siegel Eisenstein measure (Theorem 8.2.2)
nodes.statement: There is a measure Eis_{a,b} on X_p × T_H(ℤ_p) (X_p the p-adic characters of the relevant ray-class group of K, T_H the torus at p) with values in the space of p-adic modular forms on G₄ such that ∫χ̃ψ·ρ^υ dEis_{a,b} = θ^{(κ,a,b)}(G_{k,ν,χ_unitary,ψ}) for (χ, c = ψρ^υ) in the set Y^H_class of classical points, where G_{k,ν,χ,ψ} is the holomorphic Siegel Eisenstein series on U(W) attached to the factorisable Siegel section f(χ, c) chosen in §4 (with the p-adic sections designed for the local zeta integral). It is an axiomatic Eisenstein measure in the sense of Definition 5.3.2 with shift (1, χ) (Corollary 8.2.4).
hypotheses: Classical points in Y^H_class; Siegel sections chosen as in EHLS §4.2–4.3 at p and §4.5 at ∞.
proofSteps: Construct the Siegel Eisenstein series and their Fourier coefficients (EHLS §4.1–4.2, after Eischen 2015); verify the Kummer congruences of the coefficient family and apply θ^{(κ,a,b)} (ehls-differential-operators).
The q-expansion principle (AutomorphicBundles:B5/vector-expansion-principle) gives a measure with values in p-adic forms.
acceptance: n = 1: Katz’s Eisenstein measure restricted to CM points (L3/katz-eisenstein-measure).
