nodes.title: The doubling integral identity (EHLS Theorem 4.6.1)
nodes.statement: Let ϕ ∈ π and ϕ♭ ∈ π♭ be factorisable test vectors, chosen as in EHLS (48) with the local components at p and ∞ given by (49)–(50), unramified outside S = S_π, and f a factorisable Siegel section. Writing χ = ‖·‖^mχ_u, D(χ)·I(ϕ, ϕ♭, f, s) = ⟨ϕ, ϕ♭⟩·I_p(χ, κ)·I_∞(χ, ρ^υ)·I_S·L^S(s + 1/2, π, χ_u), where I(ϕ, ϕ♭, f, s) = ∫_{[U(V)×U(−V)]}E(χ, s, f, (g₁, g₂))ϕ(g₁)ϕ♭(g₂)χ^{-1}(det g₂)dg₁dg₂, I_p = L_p(s, ord, π, χ)·∏_w[V_w⟨φ_w, φ̃_w⟩] and I_∞ the archimedean zeta integral; the integral vanishes identically unless ϕ♭ lies in the contragredient.
hypotheses: Test vectors as in EHLS (48)–(50); s in the range of convergence, then by continuation.
proofSteps: Unfold the Eisenstein series on U(W) against the doubled cusp form (Piatetski-Shapiro–Rallis, Garrett): the orbit filtration of the doubled principal series (MetaplecticAutomorphicForms:MP.3/doubling-filtration) leaves only the open orbit, and the integral factors into the local doubling zeta integrals of MetaplecticAutomorphicForms:MP.6/local-doubling-integral (EHLS §4.1).
Unramified places give L(s + 1/2, π_v, χ_v) (Piatetski-Shapiro–Rallis computation).
Places above p: local-zeta-at-p; archimedean place: archimedean-zeta-integral.
acceptance: n = 1: the identity reduces to Hecke’s integral representation of L(s, χ) through a CM torus.

sources.match: EHLS state the doubling method’s unfolding and prove the global identity expressing the doubling integral of their test vectors as ⟨ϕ, ϕ♭⟩ times local factors at p, ∞, S and the partial standard L-function.

nodes.title: Local doubling zeta integrals at p (EHLS Theorem 4.3.10)
nodes.statement: At a place w | p (split, K_w = K_{v}^+ × K_{v}^+, U(V)(K⁺_v) ≅ GL_n(K⁺_v)), for the ordinary vectors φ_w and the Siegel section designed in EHLS §4.3, the local integral factors as I₁·I₂ with I₁ = L(s + 1/2, π_{b,w} ⊗ χ_{2,w})/(ε(s + 1/2, π_{b,w} ⊗ χ_{2,w})L(−s + 1/2, π̃_{b,w} ⊗ χ_{2,w}^{-1}))·Vol(X(4))·⟨φ_{b,w}, φ̃_{b,w}⟩ and I₂ = ε(−s + 1/2, π_{a,w} ⊗ χ_{1,w})L(1/2 + s, π̃_{a,w} ⊗ χ_{1,w}^{-1})/L(−s + 1/2, π_{a,w} ⊗ χ_{1,w})·Vol(X(1))·⟨φ_{a,w}, φ̃_{a,w}⟩, where π_{a,w}, π_{b,w} are the GL_{a_w} and GL_{b_w} constituents determined by the ordinary condition and the signatures; together I_w = L(s + 1/2, ord, π_w, χ_w)·V_w·⟨φ_w, φ̃_w⟩, a modified Euler factor of the shape predicted by Coates and Perrin-Riou.
hypotheses: w | p split; π_w ordinary of the type given by the signatures at the places above p.
proofSteps: Reduce the doubling integral at a split place to Godement–Jacquet zeta integrals for GL_a × GL_b blocks; apply the Godement–Jacquet local functional equation (AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.2/godement-jacquet-functional-equation) to the ordinary vector data (EHLS §4.3, ‘The main local theorem’).
acceptance: n = 1: the local factor is (1 − χ(𝔓)…)(1 − χ̌(𝔓)…), Katz’s Euler factors at Σ_p.

sources.match: EHLS compute the local zeta integral at places above p for their ordinary data as a quotient of Euler factors times an ε-factor, volumes and local pairings, using the Godement–Jacquet functional equation.
The local factor at p has the expected Coates–Perrin-Riou shape; its denominator arises from the Godement–Jacquet functional equation.

nodes.title: The archimedean zeta integral is a nonzero algebraic number (EHLS Propositions 4.5.5–4.5.6)
nodes.statement: For each archimedean place σ, with ϕ_σ = ϕ_{κ_σ,−}, ϕ♭_σ = ϕ_{κ♭_σ,−} and the Siegel section f_σ of EHLS (107), the local zeta integral I_σ(χ_σ, κ_σ) = I_σ(ϕ_σ, ϕ♭_σ, f_σ, m) is a nonzero algebraic number. It is not evaluated explicitly in general (only for scalar or half-scalar weight, by Shimura and Garrett); it depends only on the weights.
hypotheses: Critical pairs (κ, χ); the section f_σ obtained by applying D(κ, χ) to the holomorphic section.
proofSteps: Garrett’s method: compute the integral against the anti-holomorphic vectors via the explicit section; nonvanishing by Proposition 4.5.5, algebraicity by Proposition 4.5.6.

AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups:AF.4/holomorphic-ds-sp2n-unn supplies the scalar-weight holomorphic discrete series of U(n,n) on the doubled side only; the vector weights of π and the zeta integral itself are EHLS §4.5’s computation.
acceptance: Scalar weight: Shimura’s explicit formula.

sources.match: EHLS prove that the archimedean local zeta integral of their data is a nonzero algebraic number, leaving it unspecified in general.

nodes.title: The EHLS p-adic L-function (Main Theorem 9.2.2)
nodes.statement: Let π be a cuspidal anti-holomorphic automorphic representation of G₁ ordinary of type (κ, K), T = T_π its component of the ordinary Hecke algebra, and ϕ, ϕ♭ elements of R-bases of Î_π, Î_{π♭}. Assume Hypothesis 7.3.2 (Gorenstein), Hypothesis 7.3.3 (global multiplicity one) and Proposition–Hypothesis 7.3.5 (minimality). Then there is a unique L(Eis, ϕ ⊗ ϕ♭) ∈ Λ_{X_p,R} ⊗̂ T such that for every classical χ = ‖·‖^mχ_u : X_p → R^× and every π′ ∈ S(K_{r₁}, κ₁, π), its image under the character χ ⊗ λ_{π′} is c(π′, χ)·Ω_{π′,χ}(ϕ, ϕ♭)·I_∞(χ, κ₁)·I_S·L_p(m, ord, π′, χ_u)·L^S(m + 1/2, π′, χ_u)/P_{π′,χ}, where Ω_{π′,χ}(ϕ, ϕ♭) = ⟨ϕ, ϕ♭χ⟩_χ/(Vol(I⁰_{r₁,V} ∩ I⁰_{r₁,−V})·Q[π′, χ]) is independent of r₁, p-integral and a p-unit for suitable ϕ, ϕ♭, P_{π′,χ} = Q^{-1}_{π′,χ} and c(π′, χ) generates the congruence ideal. The element lies in the completed tensor product of the character Iwasawa algebra with the Hecke algebra; it is not asserted to exist without the three hypotheses (without Gorenstein one obtains meromorphic functions on the components, Remark 9.3.1).
hypotheses: All three hypotheses; π ordinary of type (κ, K); p as in ehls-unitary-datum.
proofSteps: Pair the Eisenstein measure with the Hida family through the Gorenstein duality (EHLS §7.4, Proposition 7.4.15): the linear form defined by ϕ ⊗ ϕ♭ on ordinary forms on G₃ is T-valued under Gorenstein and minimality.
Corollary 9.1.8: the pairing at classical points is the doubling integral, evaluated by doubling-global-identity with local-zeta-at-p and archimedean-zeta-integral.
Corollary 9.2.1 and the rewriting Q[π′, χ] = c(π′, χ)Q_{π′,χ} (Lemma 6.7.7); the volume factors cancel (Remark 4.6.2); p-integrality and unit property of Ω (Lemma 8.5.3).
acceptance: n = 1: Katz’s p-adic L-function for the CM field K (with T a group ring).
U(1,1) over an imaginary quadratic field: Hida’s ordinary p-adic L-function of a GL₂ form twisted by Hecke characters of K.

sources.locator: Corollaries 9.1.8 and 9.2.1, Main Theorem 9.2.2 and proof, pp. 144–145; Remark 9.3.1, p. 145
sources.match: EHLS state and prove the existence and uniqueness of L(Eis, ϕ ⊗ ϕ♭) in Λ_{X_p,R} ⊗̂ T with the interpolation formula, under the Gorenstein, multiplicity-one and minimality hypotheses.

nodes.title: Disegni–Liu’s Siegel hermitian varieties Σ_m(K) and their line bundles
nodes.statement: Let E/F be a CM extension, p a prime and m ≥ 1. The Siegel hermitian variety Σ_m(K) of genus m and level K over ℚ_p (more precisely over the p-adic field of definition) is the quotient Σ^δ_m(K, K_T)^♭ of the moduli space Σ^δ_m(K, K_T) of quadruples (A₀, i₀, λ₀, η₀) and their hermitian enhancements, and ω_m is the descent of the line bundle ω^δ_m := det_O det_{O⊗E}Lie(A)^∨ of automorphy; ω_m does not depend on the auxiliary choices K_T, δ and the orbit Σ^δ_0(K_T). Disegni–Liu relate Σ_m(K) to PEL-type Shimura varieties for the similitude group G̃_m of W̃_m = E^{2m} with the pairing Tr_{E/ℚ}∘⟨·,·⟩ in order to import algebraic q-expansions.
hypotheses: E/F CM, p any prime; level K neat.
proofSteps: Construct the moduli problem and its quotient (DL §2.2); the line bundle by descent of ω^δ_m; independence of choices.
Relation with PEL data (DL §2.3) through PELModuli:M5/unitary-pel-datum; q-expansions through AutomorphicBundles:B5/vector-expansion-principle.
acceptance: m = 1: a unitary Shimura curve-type variety attached to E/F with its Hodge line bundle.

nodes.title: Degenerate principal series, big-cell sections and U_p-translation (Disegni–Liu Lemmas 3.10–3.11)
nodes.statement: On the doubling space of an even-dimensional hermitian space (n = 2r), for a character χ_p at p, the degenerate principal series I^□_{r,p}(χ_p) carries the sections f^{[e]}_{χ_p} indexed by e ∈ Z_P (supported on the big cell, built from regularised Whittaker functionals); each is invariant under the subgroup P̃e_{r,r}(ℤ_p) (Lemma 3.10), and the U_p-operators act on them by translation: (U^{e₁}_p × U^{e₂}_p)(f^{[e]}_{χ_p}) = f^{[e + e₁^c + e₂]}_{χ_p} for e₁, e₂ ∈ N_P (Lemma 3.11).
hypotheses: n = 2r even; P the set of places above p; notation of DL §3.1.
proofSteps: Construct the sections on the big cell from the regularised Whittaker functionals of DL §3.1; invariance and the translation formula are direct computations (DL proofs of Lemmas 3.10–3.11).
acceptance: r = 1: sections of the degenerate principal series of U(1,1) supported on the big cell.

sources.match: Disegni–Liu construct the big-cell sections f^{[e]} of the degenerate principal series and show their invariance and that the U_p-operators act on them by translation.

nodes.title: The analytic Eisenstein family and rationality of its diagonal pullback (Disegni–Liu Proposition 3.13)
nodes.statement: For ‖e‖ > 0 and a section f ∈ I^□_r(χ), the diagonal pullback h̃_{r,r}D̃^{[e]}_♢(−, χ, f) of the Siegel hermitian Eisenstein series built from the big-cell sections is σ-equivariant: for every σ ∈ Aut(ℂ/ℚ), h̃_{r,r}D̃^{[e]}_♢(−, σχ, σf) = σ(h̃_{r,r}D̃^{[e]}_♢(−, χ, f)). Hence the family is rational over the field of definition and gives an analytic family Ẽ^{[e]}_♢ of p-adic forms.
hypotheses: ‖e‖ > 0; sections in I^□_r(χ)^{∞p}.
proofSteps: Compute Fourier coefficients of the Siegel hermitian Eisenstein series for big-cell sections; rationality of q-expansions plus the q-expansion principle on the Siegel hermitian variety (dl-siegel-hermitian-varieties).
acceptance: r = 1: rationality of the pullback of a U(2,2) Eisenstein series to U(1,1) × U(1,1).

nodes.title: Panchishkin unramified representations and their eigenlines (Disegni–Liu §3.3)
nodes.statement: Let π be a relevant representation (DL Definition 1.1) and v a place of F above p, u ∈ P_v the places of E above v. With P_{π_u}(T) = T^n + Σ_sβ_{u,s}q_v^{s(s−1)/2}T^{n−s} the Satake polynomial (β_{u,s} ∈ O_L) and A(π_u, m) ⊂ ℤ_p the multiset of valuations, π_v is Panchishkin unramified if π_u is unramified for u ∈ P_v and β_{u,r} ∈ O_L^× (n = 2r). Equivalently (Lemma 3.22) A(π_u, r) contains a unique element of O_L^× for some u. Then: the eigenspace π^+_v of T^+_u for the unit eigenvalue α(π_u) ∈ A(π_u, r) ∩ O_L^× is one-dimensional and independent of u, likewise π^-_v for T^-_u (Lemma 3.23, Notation 3.24); there is a unique divisor Q_{π_u}(T) = T^r + γ_{u,1}T^{r−1} + … + γ_{u,r}q_v^{r(r−1)/2} of P_{π_u} with γ_{u,r} ∈ O_L^×; π̲_u denotes the unramified principal series of GL_r(F_v) with Satake polynomial Q_{π_u}(T); and there is a unique locally constant matrix coefficient ξ_{π_v} of π^-_v with ξ_{π_v}(w_r) = 1, bi-I_v-invariant, with ξ_{π_v}(m(a)w_r) = ∏_{u∈P_v}⟨π̲_u(a_{u^c})φ_u, φ_u^∨⟩ for spherical vectors (Proposition 3.25).
hypotheses: π relevant (tempered cuspidal, holomorphic discrete series of the given Harish-Chandra parameter at ∞); v | p with π_v unramified.
proofSteps: Newton polygon of the Satake polynomial: the unit root count (Lemma 3.19).
Hecke eigenvalues of T^±_u on the Iwahori invariants are A(π_u, r) and A(π_u^c, r) (Lemma 3.20).
Uniqueness of the unit-root eigenline by multiplicity one of the unit root (Lemmas 3.22–3.23), and the factorisation of P_{π_u} by the unit roots (Proposition 3.25).
acceptance: n = 2, r = 1: π_v Panchishkin unramified iff the Satake parameters at v have one unit and one non-unit, i.e. π_v is ordinary.

nodes.title: The p-adic local doubling integral (Disegni–Liu Proposition 3.32)
nodes.statement: If v | p and π_v is Panchishkin unramified, then for every embedding ι : L → ℂ, ∫_{G_r(F_v)}ιξ_{π_v}(g)·(f^{[0]}_{χ_v})^{χ_v}(w_r(g, 1_{2r}))dg = q_v^{d_v r²}·∏_{u∈P_v}γ((1+r)/2, ιπ̲_u ⊗ χ_v, ψ_{F,v})^{-1}, with π̲_u the unramified principal series of GL_r(F_v) with Satake polynomial Q_{π_u} (Proposition 3.25(3)): a local doubling zeta integral that produces the product of inverse γ-factors of the unit-root part. At places outside V_F^{(p)} with unramified data the integral is L(1/2, BC(ιπ_v) ⊗ (χ_v∘Nm))/b_{2r,v}(χ) (Lemma 3.31, Piatetski-Shapiro–Rallis).
hypotheses: π_v Panchishkin unramified; the section f^{[0]} and ξ_{π_v} of the preceding nodes.
proofSteps: Unfold the doubling integral on the big cell and reduce to Godement–Jacquet/Tate integrals for the Levi, using ξ_{π_v} and the unit-root factorisation (DL §3.4).
acceptance: r = 1, π_v ordinary: π̲_u is the unramified character with Satake parameter the unit root, and the integral is q_v^{d_v}γ(1, ιπ̲_u ⊗ χ_v)^{-1}.

sources.match: Disegni–Liu compute the p-adic local doubling zeta integral against ξ_{π_v} as q_v^{d_v r²} times the product over u of γ((1+r)/2, ιπ̲_u ⊗ χ_v)^{-1}, and the unramified integral by Piatetski-Shapiro–Rallis.

nodes.title: Disegni–Liu’s cyclotomic p-adic L-function (Theorem 3.37, Theorem 1.4)
nodes.statement: Let π be a relevant L-representation of G_r(A^∞_F) (n = 2r) with π_v Panchishkin unramified for every v | p, and ♢ ⊇ {∞, p} a finite set of places outside which π is unramified. The distribution L^♢_p(π) on Γ_{F,p} (the Galois group of the maximal abelian extension of F unramified outside p∞), defined by Ω ↦ (∏_{u∈P}α(π_u))^{-1}⟨φ₁ ⊗ φ₂, D_♢(−, Ω)⟩_{π,π̂}, is a p-adic measure, depending on ♢ only, and for every finite character χ : Γ_{F,p} → ℚ̄_p^× and every embedding ι : ℚ̄_p → ℂ, ιL^♢_p(π)(χ) = (P^ι_π)^{-1}·Z_r^{[F:ℚ]}/b^♢_{2r}(1)·∏_{v∈V_F^{(p)}}∏_{u∈P_v}γ((1+r)/2, ι(π̲_u ⊗ χ_v), ψ_{F,v})^{-1}·L(1/2, BC(ιπ^♢) ⊗ (ιχ^♢∘Nm_{E/F})), with P^ι_π the period of Lemma 3.17, b^♢_{2r} the normalising product of abelian L-values, and Z_r = (−1)^r2^{−2r²}·2^{r²−r}π^{r²}·Γ(1)⋯Γ(r)/(Γ(r+1)⋯Γ(2r)). Equivalently L^♢_p(π) is a bounded analytic function on the character space X_{F,p} ⊗ L, defined over the p-adic field of definition of π and interpolating along all embeddings ι.
hypotheses: π relevant, Panchishkin unramified at every v | p; finite-order χ only (cyclotomic variable).
proofSteps: Pair the analytic Eisenstein family (dl-eisenstein-family) with φ₁ ⊗ φ₂ through the doubling integral; boundedness from U_p-translation (dl-big-cell-sections) and the unit eigenvalues α(π_u).
Interpolation: global doubling identity with the p-adic local integral of dl-local-doubling-at-p, the unramified computation of Piatetski-Shapiro–Rallis and the archimedean constant Z_r (DL §3.5).
Rationality along all ι: Aut(ℂ)-equivariance of the family.
acceptance: F = ℚ, r = 1, E imaginary quadratic: a p-adic L-function for U(1,1) interpolating L(1/2, BC(π) ⊗ χ∘Nm) at finite-order cyclotomic characters.

sources.locator: Definition 3.36 and Theorem 3.37, p. 35; Theorem 1.4 and Remark 1.5, pp. 4–5
sources.match: Disegni–Liu define the distribution L^♢_p(π) and prove it is a measure interpolating central values of the base change twisted by finite characters along every embedding, with inverse γ-factors at p and an explicit archimedean constant.

nodes.title: Parity of the order of vanishing (Disegni–Liu Proposition 3.39)
nodes.statement: The vanishing order of L^♢_p(π) at the trivial character 1 has the same parity as r[F:ℚ] + (1 − ϵ(π))/2, where ϵ(π) = ∏_{v finite}ϵ(π_v) and ϵ(π_v) := ϵ(BC(π_v) ⊗ ιχ_v∘Nm_{E_v/F_v}) is independent of the finite character χ. The vanishing order at 1 does not depend on ♢, and L^♢_p(π) = L^♢_p(π̂).
hypotheses: As in dl-padic-l-function.
proofSteps: Compare L^♢_p(π) with the analytic functions L_p(π_v) interpolating the local factors at v ∈ ♢ \ {∞, p}, which have neither zeros nor poles at the relevant characters; reduce to the functional equation of the interpolated central values, whose sign is ϵ(π)·(−1)^{r[F:ℚ]} (DL proof of Proposition 3.39).
acceptance: If ϵ(π) = −1 and r[F:ℚ] is even, L^♢_p(π) vanishes at 1.

nodes.title: The Eischen–Wan setting: definite unitary groups, unramified principal series and stabilised vectors
nodes.statement: Let p be an odd prime, K an imaginary quadratic field in which p splits as v₀v̄₀, and GU(r, 0) the definite unitary similitude group of a diagonal matrix ζ with i^{-1}ζ positive definite and entries in O_K prime to p, so that GU(r,0)(ℚ_p) ≅ GL_r(ℚ_p) × ℚ_p^×. Let π be an irreducible cuspidal automorphic representation of GU(r, 0) of weight k = (a₁ ≥ … ≥ a_r ≥ 0), tempered, with π_p ≅ π(χ₁, …, χ_r) an unramified principal series with the χ_i pairwise distinct, and ϕ ∈ π^{K₀(p)} an eigenvector for all the Hecke operators U_{t_i} at p (a p-stabilised vector with eigenvalues χ₁⋯χ_i(p^{-1})p^{κ₁+…+κ_i}, finite slope allowed). Let ξ₀ be an auxiliary Hecke character of K with ξ₀|·|^{-(r−1)/2} of finite order, and Σ a finite set of primes containing those above p and those where ξ₀, π or K/ℚ ramify. The auxiliary character, finite-slope refinement, coefficient module L(k) and integral local sections are part of the datum. Temperedness is used only for the explicit pullback calculation (EW p. 34) but is carried as a hypothesis until a separate argument removes it.
hypotheses: p odd, split in K; π_p unramified principal series with pairwise distinct χ_i (regular p-stabilisation); π tempered; the datum is not asserted to extend to a CM field without separate checks.
proofSteps: The definite unitary group and its automorphic forms: AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups:AF.5/algebraic-modular-forms (forms on groups compact at infinity).

Stabilised vectors: Eischen–Wan Propositions 4.7–4.8 (eigenvectors for U_{t_i} in the principal series; uniqueness of the stabilisation needs the χ_i pairwise distinct, regular in the sense of Casselman).
acceptance: r = 1: GU(1, 0) is a torus and π a Hecke character of K.
r = 2: definite unitary forms of rank two, the case of the constant-term divisibility.

sources.locator: §1.3, p. 3 (setting); Theorem 1.2, p. 4 (hypotheses); §2.2 p. 5; Propositions 4.7–4.8, p. 25; unlabelled remark on temperedness, p. 34; Remark 1.1 and footnote 1, p. 3

nodes.title: The Eischen–Wan Siegel Eisenstein measures (Proposition 5.5)
nodes.statement: There are p-adic measures E_{D,Sieg} and E′_{D,Sieg} on Γ_K ≅ ℤ_p × ℤ_p (the Galois group of the ℤ_p²-extension of K) with values in the spaces of p-adic automorphic forms on U(r+1, r+1) and U(r, r) respectively, such that ∫φ̂ dE_{D,Sieg} = Ê_{D,φ}(f_{Sieg,φ}, z_{κ_φ}, −) for φ in the set X of arithmetic points used for the Siegel family (EW Remark 5.1), with the Siegel sections f_{Sieg,φ} chosen in §4 (unramified, ℓ-adic, p-adic and archimedean) and the differential operators of EW §2.11.
hypotheses: The arithmetic points X of EW §5.1; the local sections of §4.
proofSteps: Siegel Eisenstein series on GU_n (EW §3.2) with explicit Fourier coefficients (§§4.2.2, 4.3, 4.4); action of the differential operators on q-expansion coefficients (§5.2, Proposition 5.3–5.4); Kummer congruences and the q-expansion principle give the measure (§5.3).

nodes.title: Pullback formula and local computations (Eischen–Wan Proposition 3.4, §4)
nodes.statement: For a unitary idele class character τ of A_K^× and f′ ∈ I_r(τ), the pullback integral F_{ϕ′}(f′; s, g) = ∫E(f′; s, S′^{-1}(g, g₁h)S′)τ̄(det g₁h)ϕ(g₁h)dg₁ converges absolutely and uniformly on compacta in Re(s) > r and is a Klingen section (Proposition 3.4). The local factors are computed: at unramified places the pullback section is L(π̃, τ̄^c, s + 1)/(…)·F_{ρ,s} (Lemma 4.2); at ℓ ∤ p (Lemmas 4.4–4.6); at p for the stabilised vector of a regular unramified principal series (Propositions 4.11–4.12, Lemmas 4.13–4.14); at ∞ (Lemma 4.15, Definitions 4.16, 4.19, Lemma 4.17, Proposition 4.18).
hypotheses: EW setting; τ unitary; s in the convergence range; the p-adic computation uses pairwise distinct χ_i.
proofSteps: Unfold the Siegel Eisenstein series of U(r+1, r+1) along the embedding of U(r, 0) × U(1, 1)-type subgroups (Shimura’s pullback formula), then compute local integrals place by place (EW §§3.3, 4.1–4.4).
acceptance: r = 1: the classical pullback of a U(2,2) Siegel Eisenstein series to U(1,1) × U(1,0).

sources.locator: §3.3 and Proposition 3.4, p. 21; §4: Lemmas 4.1–4.2 p. 23, Lemmas 4.4–4.6 p. 24, Propositions 4.7, 4.8, 4.11, 4.12 with Remark 4.9 and Definition 4.10, pp. 25–27, Lemmas 4.13–4.15 pp. 27–28, Definitions 4.16, 4.19, Lemma 4.17, Proposition 4.18 p. 29
sources.match: Eischen–Wan prove the pullback formula and compute the pullback sections at unramified, ℓ-adic, p-adic and archimedean places.

nodes.title: The vector-valued Klingen Eisenstein family (Eischen–Wan Definition 5.6, Theorem 1.2(ii))
nodes.statement: Pulling the Siegel measure E_{D,Sieg} back along U(r, 0) × U(1, 1)-type embedding, twisting by τ^{-1}(det g₁)ψ^{-1}(det g₁) and pairing with ϕ gives the Klingen measure E_{D,Kling}; composing with the Fourier–Jacobi map defines the family E_{ϕ,ξ₀} of formal q-expansions. For a Zariski-dense set of arithmetic points φ, φ(E_{ϕ,ξ₀}) is the Fourier–Jacobi expansion of the projection to the highest weight vector of the holomorphic Klingen Eisenstein series E(f_{Kling,φ}, z_{κ_φ}, −) on GU(r+1, 1), an eigenvector for U_{t⁺} with nonzero eigenvalue.
hypotheses: EW setting; the arithmetic points X^{pb} of EW §5.1.
proofSteps: Define Ẽ_D = τ^{-1}(det g₁)ψ^{-1}(det g₁)(E_{D,Sieg} ∘ i), pair with ϕ to get E_{D,Kling} (EW §5.4.1).
Identify specialisations with Klingen Eisenstein series by the pullback formula and the local computations (ew-pullback-and-local-computations, Lemma 3.2).
acceptance: r = 1: a family of Klingen Eisenstein series on GU(2, 1) (Picard modular), the setting of Wan’s Rankin–Selberg main conjecture work.

nodes.title: The Eischen–Wan p-adic L-function (Theorem 1.2(i))
nodes.statement: There are a constant C_{ϕ,p} and an element L^Σ_{ϕ,ξ₀} ∈ Λ_{K,O_L} such that for a Zariski-dense set of arithmetic points φ ∈ Spec Λ_{K,O_L}, φ(L^Σ_{ϕ,ξ₀}) = C_{ϕ,p}·c_{φ,π}·L^Σ(π̃, ξ_φ, 0), where L^Σ(π̃, ξ_φ, 0) is the L-function of the contragredient π̃ twisted by the Hecke character ξ_φ attached to φ with the factors at Σ removed and c_{φ,π} an explicit parameter depending on φ and π.
hypotheses: EW setting (including pairwise distinct χ_i and temperedness).
proofSteps: Pair the Siegel measure with ϕ ⊗ ϕ along the doubling-type embedding and evaluate at arithmetic points by the pullback formula; the archimedean, p-adic and ℓ-adic local factors of §4 give c_{φ,π} and the Euler factors (EW §5.4).

nodes.title: Constant-term divisibility for r = 2 (Eischen–Wan Theorem 5.8, Corollary 5.9)
nodes.statement: Suppose r = 2. For arithmetic points φ ∈ X^{pb}: (i) for all k_φ, κ_φ with L(π̃_φ, τ̄^c_φ, z_{κ_φ} + 1) in the range of absolute convergence, c(k_φ, 0, κ_φ) = c′(k_φ, 0, κ_φ) (Definitions 4.16, 4.19); (ii) F_ϕ(f_{Sieg,φ}, z_{κ_φ}, g₀) = F′_ϕ(f_{Sieg,φ}, z_{κ_φ} + 1/2, g′₀)·φ(L^Σ_{τ̄′}). Consequently (Corollary 5.9 = Theorem 1.2(iii)) the constant terms a_{t[g]}(0) of E_{ϕ,ξ₀} are divisible by L^Σ_{ϕ,ξ₀}·L^Σ_{τ̄′}, where L^Σ_{τ̄′} is the Kubota–Leopoldt p-adic L-function of a Dirichlet character. The conclusion is proved only for r = 2 and is not extrapolated to other r.
hypotheses: r = 2; EW setting.
proofSteps: (i) is archimedean: choose an auxiliary prime ℓ split in K at which π is ordinary (by Sato–Tate), where the scalar-weight case is known (Wan, Lemma 4.1.2); compare (EW proof pp. 36–37).
(ii) follows from (i) for p and π.

Corollary 5.9 from Theorem 5.8, Lemma 4.17 (cited in the text as ‘Proposition 4.17’, sourceIssues E5), Lemma 3.2 and the local pullback calculations, looking at the Fourier–Jacobi coefficient at β = 0.
acceptance: The constant term along the Klingen parabolic is a product of the EW L-function and a Kubota–Leopoldt L-function, the input to the Eisenstein ideal argument of AutomorphicCongruences:L2.

nodes.title: Euler factors at primes away from p as elements of the Iwasawa algebra
nodes.statement: Let G be a ray-class limit Cl⁺_F(𝔫p^∞) (or a quotient, such as an anticyclotomic group), O a coefficient ring, and for a finite place w ∤ p with Frobenius class γ_w ∈ G (the image of the uniformiser through Art) let P_w(T) ∈ O[T] be a local Euler polynomial (for instance det(1 − Frob_w T | V^{I_w}) of a Galois representation, or 1 − χ_w(ϖ)T for a character). The Euler-factor element is e_w := P_w(N(w)^{-1}·[γ_w]) ∈ O[[G]] in the convention of the consumer (evaluation of the character at ℓ^{-1}γ_w), and for a finite set S the S-imprimitive version of a measure µ is E_S(µ) := ∏_{w∈S} e_w ⋆ µ (convolution). For every character χ of G unramified at w, χ(e_w) = P_w(χ(γ_w)N(w)^{-1}), so E_S(µ) interpolates the S-imprimitive values whenever µ interpolates the primitive ones (AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.5/finite-euler-correction). Primitive and imprimitive normalisations of all constructions in this roadmap are related by these elements; inertia coinvariants V_{I_w} and the arithmetic/geometric Frobenius convention are part of the datum.
hypotheses: w ∤ p; P_w with coefficients in O; the Frobenius convention (arithmetic in this roadmap) is fixed and recorded.
proofSteps: e_w is a polynomial in the group element [γ_w] ∈ O[[G]] (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L1); its value at a character is the polynomial evaluated at χ(γ_w).
Multiplicativity of evaluation on convolutions (LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L3/mellin-convolution) gives the interpolation of E_S(µ).
If χ is ramified at w the value is the constant term P_w(0) = 1 only if P_w is computed on inertia coinvariants; the convention is stated by the consumer.
acceptance: F = ℚ, G = ℤ_p^×, w = ℓ, P_ℓ(T) = 1 − T: e_ℓ = 1 − ℓ^{-1}[ℓ], and E_{ℓ}(ζ_p) is the Kubota–Leopoldt measure with the Euler factor at ℓ removed.

Deligne–Ribet’s L-values of functions on G_f exclude the Euler factors at the primes dividing fp.
Dasgupta–Kakde–Ventullo’s L* removes the Euler factors at the primes above p.

nodes.title: Comparisons of periods, coefficients and normalisations across the constructions
nodes.statement: The constructions of L2–L4e are related as follows, with every change of normalisation explicit: (a) BSW for F = ℚ against Pollack–Stevens (L2/specialisations-q-hilbert-bianchi) and for F imaginary quadratic against Williams; (b) Deligne–Ribet for F = ℚ against Kubota–Leopoldt (L3/deligne-ribet-rational-comparison); (c) Hsieh’s square for π induced from a Hecke character of M against the product of two Katz–Hida–Tilouine measures up to a unit of Λ (L3h/theorem-a); (d) EHLS for n = 1 against Katz (L4/ehls-main-theorem); (e) changing a period Ω by a ∈ K(ϕ)^× rescales the corresponding measure by a^{-1}; extending coefficients O → O′ commutes with every construction; (f) primitive against imprimitive normalisations through L0/euler-factor-elements. No comparison between EHLS and Disegni–Liu, or between BSW and Bergdall–Hansen without Leopoldt, is asserted: the sources do not prove one.
hypotheses: Each comparison carries the hypotheses of both constructions it compares.
proofSteps: Each item is the cited comparison node or theorem; (e) is linearity of every construction in the period-normalised class; (f) by euler-factor-elements.
acceptance: Over ℚ the three constructions BSW, Pollack–Stevens and Mazur–Swinnerton-Dyer agree for an ordinary weight-2 form after matching periods.

sources.match: Hsieh observes that for π induced from a Hecke character, L_{Σ_p}(π, λ) is a product of two Katz–Hida–Tilouine p-adic L-functions up to an explicit unit.
EHLS present their construction as extending Hida’s and Katz’s CM constructions.
Bergdall–Hansen note that without Leopoldt’s conjecture it is not known that their construction agrees with the evaluation-map constructions in overlapping cases.

nodes.title: Each construction is an instance of the evaluation principle on an actual ray-class quotient
nodes.statement: Every p-adic L-function of this roadmap is an element of D(G, L) or of a completed group ring of an explicit quotient G of a ray-class limit, and is obtained by the conditional evaluation principle (L0/conditional-evaluation-principle) or by its measure-theoretic special case: BSW’s µ_Φ on Cl⁺_F(p^∞) (norm relation L2/norm-relation, interpolation L2/bsw-interpolation, uniqueness only under L2/growth-uniqueness-totally-real-imaginary-quadratic); Deligne–Ribet’s pseudo-measure on Cl⁺_F(f′p^∞) (L3/deligne-ribet-pseudomeasure); Katz’s and Hida–Tilouine’s measures on Gal(M(Cp^∞)/M) (L3/katz-padic-l-function, L3/katz-hida-tilouine-tame); Hsieh’s measure on the anticyclotomic quotient Γ⁻ (L3h/anticyclotomic-distribution); EHLS’s element of Λ_{X_p} ⊗̂ T over the character group X_p of a ray-class limit of K (L4/ehls-main-theorem); Disegni–Liu’s measure on Γ_{F,p} (L4/dl-padic-l-function); Eischen–Wan’s element of Λ_{K,O_L} on Γ_K (L4e/ew-padic-l-function). In each case the group is identified with a Galois group through L0/ray-class-reciprocity and the interpolated characters are p-adic avatars (L0/hecke-character-avatar); there is one evaluation formalism, not separate incompatible measure definitions.
hypotheses: Each construction’s hypotheses.
proofSteps: For each construction, identify its group with the ray-class limit or the stated quotient (L0/ray-class-unit-sequence, L0/evaluation-norm-twist-maps), its characters with avatars, and its interpolation with the clause (c) of the principle; bounded constructions are measures (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L1) and the principle’s growth clause is vacuous for them.
acceptance: Hsieh’s Γ⁻ is the quotient of Cl⁺_M(p^∞) by the image of the norm from F: its characters are the anticyclotomic avatars.

sources.match: BSW’s p-adic L-function is a distribution on Cl⁺_F(p^∞) obtained from evaluation maps and a norm relation.
Panchishkin defines Gal_p and its character space X_p in §4.1 and, in Conjecture 6.2, places the p-adic L-function of every motive over a totally real field on X_p.
Katz identifies his Galois group with ideal-class limits by the Artin symbol.

nodes.title: The Coates–Perrin-Riou/Panchishkin existence proposition
nodes.statement: Let M be a pure motive of weight w and rank d over a totally real field F with coefficients in a number field T, given through explicit realisation data (SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L4/period-realization, L4/archimedean-realization) with a critical twist (L4/criticality). For a sign ε₀ = (ε_{0,σ}) ∈ {±1}^{J_F}, periods c^±(σ, M) (determined modulo T^×) and Ω(ε₀, M) = (1 ⊗ (2πi))^{r(M)}∏_σc^{ε_{0,σ}}(σ, M), the Newton and Hodge polygons P_Newton,σ(u, M), P_Hodge,σ(u, M) at the embeddings σ above p, the positive integer h = max_σ[P_Newton,σ(d^±) − P_Hodge,σ(d^±)] + 1 with [·] the integer part (so h = 1 when M is admissible at p, i.e. P_Newton,σ(d^±) = P_Hodge,σ(d^±) for all σ, and also whenever the gap at d^± is less than 1), and the modified p-Euler factors A_p(M(χ), s) built from the inverse roots α_i(𝔭) ordered by valuation, the proposition CPRP(M, ε₀) asserts: there is a ℂ_p-analytic function L^{ε₀}_{(p)} on the character space X_p of Gal_p = Gal(F(p^∞)/F) such that (i) for all but finitely many (m, χ) with M(χ)(m) critical at 0 and sign ε₀, L^{ε₀}_{(p)}(χx_p^m) equals the explicit product of i^{…}, G(χ)^{d^{ε₀}}, ∏_{𝔭|p}A_p(M(χ)(m), 0) and the critical value L(M(χ)(m), 0)/Ω(ε₀, M) (read p-adically); (ii) it is holomorphic if M^{…} = 0 and otherwise has poles only at a finite explicit set; (iii) the holomorphic function in (ii) is bounded if M is admissible at p; (iv) in general it is of type o(log_p^h) and is the Mellin transform of an h-admissible measure; (v) if h ≤ m* − m_* + 1 (the width of the critical strip) it is uniquely determined by (i)–(ii) (Panchishkin Conjecture 6.2). No constructor asserts CPRP; it is a proposition about the data, satisfied in the cases constructed in this roadmap.
hypotheses: M given by explicit realisation and criticality data from SelmerIwasawaCohomology L4; periods fixed modulo T^×; the conjecture on factorisation of periods (Panchishkin §2.3) is part of the data, not proved.
proofSteps: Define the critical set, periods and polygons from the realisation data; define h from the polygons (Panchishkin §5).
State (i)–(iii) as a proposition (Panchishkin Conjecture 6.2) using the character space and h-admissible measures (L0/ray-class-distributions, LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L2/order-r-distributions).
acceptance: M = ℚ(1) over ℚ (Tate motive), p odd: admissible and ordinary, h = 1, and CPRP is the existence of the Kubota–Leopoldt measure (DirichletPadicLFunctions).

M = h¹(E)(1) for an elliptic curve with good supersingular reduction at p ≥ 5: d^± = 1, P_Newton(1) − P_Hodge(1) = 1/2, so h = [1/2] + 1 = 1 but M is not admissible at p; clause (iv) asks for a function of type o(log_p), matching the order-1/2 distributions of Amice–Vélu and Višik constructed by Pollack–Stevens.

sources.locator: §3.2, pp. 998–999; §4.2, Definition 4.2, p. 1001; §5, Definitions 5.2–5.5 and the integer h, pp. 1002–1005; §6.1–6.2, Conjecture 6.2 (i)–(v), pp. 1005–1006
sources.match: Panchishkin defines the periods Ω(ε₀, M), h-admissible measures, the Newton and Hodge polygons, the admissibility condition, the integer h and the modified p-Euler factors, and states the conjecture on the existence of p-adic L-functions of motives over totally real fields.
EHLS refer to the conjectures of Coates, Coates–Perrin-Riou, Panchishkin and Hida predicting how critical values fit into p-adic analytic functions.

api.name: CPRP.admissibility
api.statement: h(M) = max_σ[P_Newton,σ(d^±) − P_Hodge,σ(d^±)] + 1 ([·] the integer part), and the admissibility predicate P_Newton,σ(d^±) = P_Hodge,σ(d^±) for all σ (Panchishkin Definition 5.5), which implies h = 1 but is not implied by it.

api.statement: A_p(M(χ), s) as in Panchishkin §6.1.

api.name: CPRP.statement
api.statement: The proposition CPRP(M, ε₀) with clauses (i)–(iii); a Prop, never an axiom.

api.name: CPRP.admissibility_twist
api.statement: h(M) is unchanged by Tate twists and by finite-order twists of conductor prime to p.

api.name: CPRP.of_measure
api.statement: For M admissible at p, a measure on Gal_p with the interpolation (i) gives CPRP via the Mellin transform; in general an h-admissible distribution with (i) does.

tests.name: cprp_tate_motive
tests.statement: M = ℚ(1), p odd: h = 1 and CPRP holds by the Kubota–Leopoldt measure.

tests.name: cprp_ordinary_h_one
tests.statement: If M is p-ordinary (Newton = Hodge) then h = 1 and the predicted function is bounded.

tests.name: cprp_supersingular_not_admissible
tests.statement: For h¹(E)(1) with E supersingular at p, h = 1 although M is not admissible at p (the Newton polygon lies 1/2 above the Hodge polygon at d^± = 1); a definition that took h = 1 to mean bounded, or that dropped the integer part and set h = 3/2, gets the predicted growth wrong: no bounded measure has the predicted values, and the function is of type o(log_p).

tests.name: cprp_no_constructor
tests.statement: CPRP(M, ε₀) is a proposition: the definition provides no element of D(Gal_p, ℂ_p) without a construction.

sourceIssues.locator: §9.2.2 (definition of φ_{a_y}) and Proposition 9.3, p. 31; proof of Proposition 9.9 (first display), p. 34; arXiv:1602.06244v3
sourceIssues.printed: The fibre functions are written with the inverse chart φ_{a_y}(z) = φ(a_y^{-1}z), and Proposition 9.3 and the proof of Proposition 9.9 use the corresponding transformation rules φ_{a_y}(z) = φ_{a′_y}(ũz) and φ_{a_yu_r}(z) = φ_{a_y}(u_r^{-1}z).
sourceIssues.correction: Use the forward chart φ_{a_y}(z) = φ(a_yz), which matches the identification G_y ≅ G by multiplication by a_y^{-1} and equation (13); then φ_{a′_y}(z) = φ_{a_y}(ũz), φ_{a_yu_r}(z) = φ_{a_y}(u_rz), and the matrix identities ϕ*_{a′_y} = (ũ 0; 0 1)·ϕ*_{a_y} and ϕ*_{a_y}|_{G_r} = (ũ_r^{-1} 0; 0 1)·ϕ*_{a_yu_r} used in the proofs of Propositions 9.6 and 9.9 hold as printed.
sourceIssues.reason: With the weight action (u 0; 0 1)·f(z) = u^{k+v}f(u^{-1}z), the identity ϕ*_{a′_y} = (ũ 0; 0 1)·ϕ*_{a_y} holds for the forward chart and fails for the inverse one (it gives (ũ^{-1} 0; 0 1) instead), so with the printed chart the two changes in Proposition 9.6 do not cancel; equation (13), (ϕ_{p-fin})_{a_y} = ε_ϕϕ_f(a_y)z^r, also requires the forward chart (the inverse chart gives ϕ_f(a_y)^{-1}). Test: ℚ_3-units, weight z², ψ(z) = z and u = 4 give 1/16 instead of 1 with the inverse chart.

review.reason: Checked in arXiv v3, §9.2.1–9.2.2 and the proofs of Propositions 9.6 and 9.9 (pp. 30–34): §9.2.1 identifies G_y with G by multiplication by a_y^{-1}, so the fibre function of φ is z ↦ φ(a_y z), while §9.2.2 prints φ(a_y^{-1}z). With the weight action (u 0; 0 1)·f(z) = u^{k+v}f(u^{-1}z) the identity ϕ*_{a′_y} = (ũ 0; 0 1)·ϕ*_{a_y} used in Proposition 9.6, the restriction identity in Proposition 9.9 and equation (13) all hold for the forward chart and fail for the printed one; Proposition 9.3 as printed is the backward-chart rule, so it must be read as ϕ_{a′_y}(z) = ϕ_{a_y}(ũz). review.reason: Checked at Lemma 8.1(iii), p. 24: the hypothesis asks only for an O_L-submodule of the elements of nonnegative norm stable under L[U_i]; stability under L-scalars forces such a submodule to be 0, and the proof needs to rescale an eigenvector into the submodule, so an open bounded lattice stable under the integral Hecke algebra is required. Corollary 8.4 supplies one (integral distributions and the renormalised U′_𝔭).

sourceIssues.locator: §9.2.1, p. 30 (the decomposition of Cl⁺_F(p^∞) and the parenthetical on E(1)); also the definition of G after (11); arXiv:1602.06244v3
sourceIssues.printed: Cl⁺_F(p^∞) is written as a disjoint union over Cl⁺_F of (O_F ⊗ ℤ_p)^×/E(1), with E(1) taken to be the image of the totally positive units in (O_F ⊗ ℤ_p)^×, and G as the congruence units modulo E(f).
sourceIssues.correction: Divide by the topological closure of the image of E(1) (respectively E(f)), as Katz (5.4.6) and Panchishkin §4.1 do.
sourceIssues.reason: The kernel of (O_F ⊗ ℤ_p)^× → Cl⁺_F(p^∞) is closed (the target is profinite) and contains the image of the units densely, so it is the closure; for F with positive unit rank the image itself is not closed and the quotient by it is not Hausdorff.
searched: Canadian Journal of Mathematics article page (metadata only)

review.reason: Checked at §9.2.1, p. 30, and §12, p. 39: the quotients are written as (O_F ⊗ ℤ_p)^×/E(1) and {z ≡ 1 mod f}/E(f) with E the image of the units; for positive unit rank the image is not closed, and the kernel of the map to the profinite group Cl⁺_F(p^∞) is its closure (Katz (5.4.6), p. 275, divides by the closure).
